content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/.claude/skills/energy-efficiency

# Energy Efficiency Analysis

You are finding **energy waste**: code that spends energy on work the program
does not need, and that a specific refactoring can remove without changing what
the program does.

**The task is to cover everything you were asked to look at** — every file,
every function and every method — and to report every case you find there, not
a few that turn up early in one or two files. A run that stops after two or
three findings has not done it. Keep going until every file has been read, and
report what you find whether or not it can be measured here.

Why this matters more than speed: a smell in code you never read is never
found. Nothing later in the procedure goes back to code left out of step 1, and
the report then reads as if that code were clean, so a missed inefficiency
costs more than any minutes spent reading. Keep working until all of it is
done — every file read, every suspicion decided, every accepted one given an
outcome. Do not stop partway to report progress or to ask whether to go on;
stop to ask only when you cannot continue without an answer.

Paths below are relative to this file's directory — call it `$SKILL`. Work out
what `$SKILL` is once, at the start, and use it throughout.

**Time:** you have 120 minutes for the whole run, thinking and measuring
included, and the session is stopped at 120. That is enough to be thorough, so
do not rush: give each unit the reading it needs. Run `date` when you start
and again as you go, so you know how much of the 120 minutes is left.

---

## What counts as a finding

> A finding is a **repair**: a concrete edit to *this* code, with a stated
> reason why the edit saves energy. That it does is a separate claim, and only
> a measurement makes it.

Three consequences you have to hold onto:

- **No repair, no finding.** If you cannot write the actual edit for this code,
  you have not found anything — you have recognised a pattern.
- **No measurement, no claim.** A repair is said to save energy only once it
  has been measured. One left unmeasured is still a finding — with no claim
  attached to it.
- **Report the failures too.** A repair you built, measured, and found saves
  nothing is a result. It stays in `submissions.jsonl`, with its verdict.

## One repair, one reason

Attribute each repair to a single reason: the thing about the code that
explains why the edit saves energy.

One unit can have several repairs, and they can overlap: fixing how a function
searches can make a redundant conversion and a needless copy disappear too,
because they only existed to serve the search. The rule is the same either
way — **every accepted suspicion gets its own repair, written against the
original code, and its own measurement.** That is what says what each one is
worth on its own.

- Two suspicions that would get **exactly the same edit** are one repair:
  submit it once, and record the other as `same_repair_as`.
- Two that get **different edits to the same code** are two repairs: submit
  both.
- Do **not** widen a repair to cover a second suspicion, and do not split one
  edit into several submissions to raise the count.

Since each repair is written against the original, at most one per function
can ever be applied. Choosing it is not part of your job: submit every repair,
measured, and the measurements decide.

## How much you may change

The edit should be as small as removing the waste allows. That bounds its
**size**, never its location, and never how much code you may read to decide.

**What must survive is the unit's contract**: the same return value, the same
effect on its arguments and on the module- and class-level values it uses, the
same printed and logged output, the same files, the same exception type. That
is what gets checked, for every repair, and it is the whole of what callers are
entitled to.

Anything **only the unit depends on** is implementation detail: a helper
nothing else calls, state nothing else reads. You may change a helper's
signature, its return shape or its behaviour, if that is what removes the
waste. A list built in `__init__` and searched only in this method is one
repair, made in both. A value shaped wrongly by a producer and compensated for
by its consumers is one repair, made in all of them — when nothing but the unit
reaches them.

Two obligations come with reaching outside the unit:

- **Give every function you change its own entry** in the submission, named
  `path::qualname`, in whichever file it lives.
- **Establish that nothing else depends on what you changed** — no other
  caller of a changed function, no other reader of changed state — and say how
  in `sole_caller_evidence`. Anything else that depends on it is not
  implementation detail: the change reaches it too, and the check on this unit
  would not notice.

What you may not do is bring anything else along. A patch that also renames
variables, tidies an unrelated branch, or fixes a second problem cannot be
attributed to one reason, and the measurement stops meaning anything. The
second problem is a second finding, or it is nothing.

## What is not energy waste

**Style.** Unreadable, undocumented, poorly named, badly typed code is not
energy waste. If the repair does not change what the machine does, it
is out of scope here.

Everything else that wastes work is in scope, wherever it is in the program:
a real repair is a real repair, and the measurement will say what it came to.

## Energy is not time

They usually move together, but not always. Spreading work across cores cuts
wall-clock time while raising energy. A busy-wait poll burns power while making
no progress. A blocked event loop keeps a core hot for nothing. Judge energy,
and when the two diverge, say so — those cases are the most interesting ones
you can find.

## Measuring for yourself

At any step, whenever you are unsure — whether some code costs anything,
whether a change would save energy or only time, whether a version still does
the same work — measure it. `$SKILL/scripts/energy.py` takes one energy reading
of any Python call:

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "...")    # $SKILL/scripts, written out in full
from energy import measure
r = measure(my_function, data)          # r.joules, r.seconds, r.watts, r.result
```

What you run, on what data, how many times and how you compare is up to you;
the script's docstring says what one reading holds. These readings are for
your own judgement, and nothing records them: a repair is still measured by
`verify.py`, in step 3, on the inputs generated for it.

---

## Procedure

Four steps, in order. **Each step writes its own file in the repository's
root, and when the step is finished you say so** — then the next step begins:

| Step | Writes | When it is finished |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Find | `step1.jsonl` | `python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done 1` |
| 2. Decide | `step2.jsonl` | `python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done 2` |
| 3. Repair and measure | `submissions.jsonl`, `step3.jsonl` | `python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done 3` |
| 4. Finish | your final message | — |

Step 1 is breadth: every file read, and every unit where something may be
wasteful put on a list. Steps 2 and 3 are depth, for the units on that list.

While a step is open, its file is yours: write it, rewrite it, fix it. `done`
keeps the file, outside this session, as that step's output, and makes it
read-only — a finished step is never changed. If a later step shows you
something an earlier one missed, say so in the later step's file: step 2
rejects a step-1 suspicion and adds a new one; it does not touch
`step1.jsonl`. Do not start a step's file before the previous step is done.
`inputs.py` and
`verify.py` run between `done 2` and `done 3`.

Every step after the first is a check on what the first wrote down, and a
check you run against nothing checks nothing.

Each record is one JSON line with **exactly the keys its example below shows —
all of them, and no others**; a key with nothing to say is `null` or `[]`.
`$SKILL/reference/output-format.md` lists every key and what it holds. Every
file goes in the repository's root, the directory you were started in —
nowhere else.

### 1. Find — *in:* a target · *out:* every unit where something may be wasteful, with its suspicions

**The target** is what you were asked to look at: the whole repository, a
directory, a file, or a single unit. Choose units only from inside it; read
outside it as far as you need. A unit named loosely — "the render function" —
is yours to pin down: find it, and record the exact `path::qualname` it
resolved to. If more than one function matches, all of them are the target.

Read the repository first — its entry points, what its tests exercise, what
its README says it is for — so that you know what each part of it is for.

**Know what you are looking for:** work the program does not need, work done
more often than necessary, or work done in a more expensive way than its result
requires. Ask of every function whether any of these is happening there.

**Then you must go through every file in the target, and every unit in each
file.** List the target's Python files first, so you know what there is to
read, and work through that list file by file, reading every function and
method in each. Do not stop at the first files that turn something up: the
target is not done until every file in it has been read.

**The list you finish step 1 with is final.** No later step can add a unit to
it, so a file not read here is a file no one examines.

**You may hand the reading to subagents** — on a large target it is the
quickest way to read all of it. If you can start subagents (in Claude Code, the
Agent tool; its read-only `Explore` type fits), split the file list into groups
and start one subagent per group, all in the same turn so they read in
parallel. Tell each to read every function and method in its files in full,
looking for these three kinds of waste, and to report for each its `path::qualname`, its
lines, and what looks wasteful in it. Their reports are leads, not findings:
look at the code of every lead before you list it, and only you write the step
files and run the scripts.

**Leave nothing out because of what you expect later.** Code that calls a
network or a service, code you doubt any input could be generated for, a
script, a long file: read it all the same, and list what looks wasteful in
it. Whether a repair can be measured is step 3's question — ask for its inputs
and let the generator say — and one that cannot is still a finding, recorded
as `blocked` with the message that showed it.

**Record every unit where something may be wasteful**, and in it every
suspicion: the lines, and why. A suspicion is a reason to look closer, not a
verdict — step 2 decides — so write it down whenever you have the reason, and
do not hold one back because you are unsure. Nothing limits how many units or
suspicions you record — one, ten, a hundred or a thousand, whatever the code
holds. A unit where nothing looks wasteful gets no record.

If you were asked for a number of units, list at most that many. You may
change which units those are until you finish step 1; just do not go over the
number.

```jsonc
{"step": 1, "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render", "suspicions": [
  {"label": "a", "lines": [47],
   "why": "`self.buf` is grown with += once per row; nothing reads it in the loop"},
  {"label": "b", "lines": [44,45],
   "why": "`sorted(self.columns)` is recomputed per row and does not depend on the row"}
]}
```

Give each suspicion a `label` — `a`, `b`, `c` — unique within the unit. Steps 2
and 3 refer to it by that label.

Write one record per unit to `step1.jsonl`, and rewrite it as often as you like
while step 1 is open. Before you finish, check the file list: every file on it
has been read, by you or by a subagent. If one has not, step 1 is not finished.
Then run `python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done 1`.

### 2. Decide — *in:* each unit on the list, with its suspicions · *out:* one record per unit, each suspicion accepted or rejected

Start this step after `step.py done 1`, and write one step-2 record to
`step2.jsonl` for every unit on your list. When every record is written, run
`python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done 2`; step 3 starts after it.

**First, read the unit properly.** Read the whole unit, then follow it
outward in both directions:

- **Down, into what it calls.** If the unit calls something you have not read,
  read it. A three-line loop body calling `normalise(row)` may be compiling a
  regex and rebuilding two dicts per iteration, and none of that is visible
  from the loop. Keep going until you reach the standard library or code that
  plainly does no work.
- **Up, into what calls it.** See what it is given and what is done with what
  it returns: waste can sit between a unit and its callers — a result the
  caller throws away, a shape the caller has to undo.

Then say in one sentence what it computes and where its work goes: that is
`what_it_does`.

Read outward because the expensive waste is not in any one line. Some waste
is — a conversion, a lookup, a concatenation — and you can see it where it
sits. The larger kind is in the *arrangement*: a value computed in one place
and thrown away in another; a shape chosen early that every later step has to
compensate for; six functions doing what a different split does in two; a
result recomputed on each of three paths that each look reasonable alone. No
single statement shows any of it.

Read the unit a second time, now with the repair in mind. What the edit would
have to be is usually what tells you whether your first reading was right.

Every suspicion ends this step **accepted** or **rejected**, and nothing is
edited in place. If the second reading changes your mind, reject the suspicion
and add a new one, with a new label, saying what you now think. That keeps what
you first thought on the record, which is the part worth reading later.

A unit's suspicions may also **grow** here: reading a second time to write a
repair is one of the better ways to notice something you missed. Its units do
not — they were settled in step 1. A rejection with a reason is as much a
result as an acceptance.

**For each suspicion:**

1. **Does it apply here?** Does your account of the waste still hold on a second
   reading, or was it the shape of the code rather than what it does?
1. **Can you write the repair for *this* code**, as an edit rather than a
   rewrite of the unit? No repair, no finding.
1. **Does the repair preserve behaviour** on every input, including the edge
   cases and whatever the callers rely on?
1. **State the mechanism** — what work stops happening, and why that costs
   less. "Built-ins are faster" is not a mechanism, and it is wrong often
   enough to matter.

Accept if all of them hold, and give the mechanism as `why`. Otherwise reject,
and give the check that decided it as `why`.

```jsonc
{"step": 2, "unit": "src/router.py::Router.allowed",
 "what_it_does": "checks each request against `self.blocked`, a list built once in __init__",
 "decisions": [
  {
    "label": "a", "lines": [58], "verdict": "rejected",
    "why": "the repair belongs where the container is built, not where it is searched. Added `b` instead."
  },
  {
    "label": "b", "lines": [31], "verdict": "accepted",
    "why": "`self.blocked` is a list searched once per request, built in __init__ at line 31 and read nowhere else; as a set each search is one hash lookup"
  }
]}
```

Every suspicion from step 1 gets a decision under its label, and a unit whose
suspicions are all rejected still gets its record — a run that examined three
functions and one that examined three hundred have to be distinguishable.

### 3. Repair and measure — *in:* every accepted suspicion · *out:* `submissions.jsonl`, measured, and one record per unit

Start this step once every unit has been through step 2, and work from their
step-2 records.

**You do not edit the repository.** You describe each repair; the script
applies it to a copy and reads `before` from the repository as it stands. That
is what makes the baseline something you could not have shaped to suit the
result. Work in a scratch copy of your own if it helps you think, but the
repository you were pointed at stays untouched — and you measure against it,
`--repo .`, never against a copy: a number taken on edited code is discarded.

Read `$SKILL/reference/verifying.md` before your first submission.

1. **Choose what to measure.** Measuring takes under a minute a repair, so at
   most **20** repairs are measured — the ones you expect to save the most
   energy, across all units. Twenty is a limit, not a target: if fewer
   suspicions were accepted, measure those. A place is used only by a repair
   that gets a verdict (`confirmed`, `partial`, `mixed`, `regressed`,
   `negligible`), and it keeps the place even if its line is later deleted or
   edited: once 20 repairs have one, verify.py measures no more. A repair whose
   unit gets no inputs, or that cannot be made to behave identically, uses no
   place, so take the next accepted suspicion instead. Every other accepted
   suspicion is still a finding: record it as `deferred` in step 3's record.

2. **Ask for the inputs of every unit you will measure** — all of them in one
   request. Inputs are asked for here, in step 3: `inputs.py` opens at
   `step.py done 2`.

   ```bash
   python $SKILL/scripts/inputs.py request src/render.py::Report.render src/parse.py::tokenize
   ```

   You do not write the inputs a repair is measured on. A generator outside
   this session writes them for each unit: **four** measured inputs that make
   the unit do substantial and different work, and a few edge inputs checked
   only for identical behaviour. It keeps an input only if it runs on the
   original code and gives the same output twice. The request returns at once,
   and generation takes a minute or two, all units together — up to five for a
   hard unit. Each unit's file appears in `.energy-inputs/`, read-only: read it
   to see what your repairs will face. You cannot change the inputs; after the
   session, every repair is measured again on our own copy of them.

   `python $SKILL/scripts/inputs.py status` shows which units are ready, and
   for each one that `failed`, why and what to do next. A repair is measured
   by running the original and the repair on the same inputs, here, and
   comparing their output and their energy, so an input counts only if the
   original completes on it from this machine alone and gives the same output
   every time. A unit that needs the network, a remote service, credentials,
   hardware or data the repository does not hold cannot do that, and its
   repairs cannot be measured here. That says nothing against the suspicion:
   it is still a finding, recorded as `blocked` with the reason. When the
   reason is a package missing from this venv, install it and ask for the unit
   again; when the generator simply did not manage, it may on another try
   (three in all). A unit that failed gives its place back: up to 30 units can
   have inputs or be generating at once, failed ones not counted, so ask for
   the next unit you would measure in its place. Up to 30 different units may
   fail in a session.

3. **For each chosen suspicion, write the smallest repair of the original
   code** that removes its waste, as one line in `submissions.jsonl`. Every
   repair is written against the code as it is now, never on top of another —
   so the order does not matter, and nothing you submit changes what the next
   one is written against.
   - **The same edit as one you already wrote** for this unit: do not submit it
     again. Record its outcome in step 3 as `same_repair_as`, with that
     submission's `id` as `submission`.
   - **A different edit to the same code**: submit it as a repair of its own.

4. **Measure the whole file, once.**

   ```bash
   python $SKILL/scripts/verify.py submissions.jsonl --repo .
   ```

   It first waits — up to ten minutes, saying for what — for any inputs still
   being generated, then measures every line in turn, under a minute each, on
   its unit's inputs, and writes the result into that line as soon as it is
   measured, as `agent_measurement`: the verdict in `agent_measurement.status`,
   and the joules and seconds of every input. Never write or edit it yourself.
   Give the command a timeout to match, or run it in the background — and if it
   is still running, wait for it before you finish.

5. **Then fix only what is broken, and run the same command again.** It
   measures only the lines that need it.

   | Result | What you do |
   |---|---|
   | `not_equivalent` | the repair changes behaviour: fix that line |
   | `invalid` | the line is malformed, or the inputs do not load against your repair: fix it as the message says |
   | `no_inputs` | the unit has none: request them if you have not, otherwise record `blocked` with the message |
   | `error` | the environment could not run it: do what the message says — install a missing package here and run again, or record `blocked` |
   | `inconclusive` | the host was too noisy; the next run measures it again |
   | `over_limit` | 20 repairs already have a verdict, so it was not measured: record its suspicion as `deferred` |
   | `confirmed` `partial` `mixed` `regressed` `negligible` | **final.** Do not touch the line |

   A measured result is never revised. Editing a measured line to get a better
   number makes it `invalid`, and the result it had stays on record. If you
   think a genuinely different repair would do better, that is a new line —
   both are kept. A suspicion is `blocked` only when the
   tools showed it cannot be measured: its unit's inputs could not be generated,
   its module does not load, or its repair cannot be made to behave identically
   — quote that message as `why`. One you did not try, because you expect it
   cannot run or it is outside the 20, is `deferred`: ask for its inputs instead
   whenever you can.

6. **Record what happened to every accepted suspicion** in `step3.jsonl`, one
   record per unit:

   ```jsonc
   {"step": 3, "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render", "outcomes": [
     {"label": "a", "outcome": "submitted",      "submission": "render-concat", "why": null},
     {"label": "b", "outcome": "same_repair_as", "submission": "render-concat", "why": null},
     {"label": "c", "outcome": "blocked",        "submission": null, "why": "inputs.py: no inputs could be generated: every call opens a database connection"},
     {"label": "d", "outcome": "deferred",       "submission": null, "why": "outside the 20 repairs measured"}
   ]}
   ```

Every measured repair stays in `submissions.jsonl`, whatever its verdict —
one you delete is still measured after the session. `partial`, `negligible`,
`regressed` and `mixed` are results, and a file that kept only the wins could
not be told apart from one that hid its losses.

7. **Check, then finish the step.** Every suspicion accepted in step 2 has an
   outcome in `step3.jsonl`, and every line of `submissions.jsonl` carries the
   `agent_measurement` the script wrote, with nothing left `inconclusive` or
   `error` that a run could still settle. Then run
   `python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done 3`.

### 4. Finish — *in:* the three steps' files · *out:* a short summary

This step writes no file. End with a short summary for whoever asked: for each submission, the unit,
what it repairs, the verdict, and what it saved across its four inputs. Lead
with what was confirmed, say plainly what was not, and say how many accepted
suspicions were deferred unmeasured.

`$SKILL/reference/output-format.md` has the exact shape of every file.

---

## How this goes wrong

Failure modes, in the order they actually happen:

1. **Stopping early.** Reading a few files, picking two or three units from
   them and taking those through to the end. It feels like progress and leaves
   most of the target unread, and the list cannot grow after step 1. Read every
   file first, yourself or through subagents, and pick from all of them.
1. **Repeating what you have read about Python performance.** Much of it is
   out of date, and some of it was never true. Every claim here gets measured,
   and the ones you are most certain about are the ones worth measuring first.
1. **Submitting one edit twice.** One edit is one repair, attributed to
   one reason; another suspicion it also fixes is `same_repair_as`.
1. **Building one repair on top of another.** Every repair is written against
   the original code. One written against your previous repair is measured
   against code that does not exist.
1. **Ignoring context.** Almost every pattern that looks wasteful is the right
   call somewhere. A bare `except` in a retry loop, a materialised list that
   gets indexed twice, a wrapper that is public API.
   Ask what the author was required to do before deciding they were wrong.
1. **Skipping measurement because the waste is obvious.** The obvious ones are
   exactly where a wrong assumption hides.
1. **Rewriting the unit.** A patch that changes everything cannot be attributed
   to one reason, and cannot be measured against one. Change what removes
   the waste and stop.
1. **Changing more than the unit without checking what else depends on it.**
   The check watches the unit's contract, so another caller or another reader
   of the changed state breaks silently.

## Scope

Python. A finding is a repair with a reason, not a label.

A **unit** is a function or a method. That is the granularity at which units are
examined, cleared and reported, and at which a repair is measured — the cases
call something, and this is the something. A function defined inside another
function is not one: nothing can call it on its own, so the function around it
is the unit.

That is all it bounds. Read as far as you need in either direction, and
repair across as many units as the waste requires. When the waste exists
only in the arrangement — two methods of a class that each look
reasonable and are wrong together, a helper whose shape forces the code around
it to compensate — report it against the unit whose behaviour the repair must
preserve, and give every function you change its own entry in the submission.

- Ignore pure style (naming, docs, typing). Only report things where changing the code would remove real computation/I/O.
- Be concrete. Do not pad: if a function has nothing wasteful, just list it under coverage.

Report back in this exact structure (plain text, concise):
COVERAGE: one line per file read: `path` — list of functions/methods read (qualnames), or "module-level only".
LEADS: one entry per suspicion, in the form:

216	def query_vespa(preferences, facet_filters=None):
217	    """Query Vespa with user preferences and facet filters for search results only"""
218	    # Convert preferences to Vespa feature format
219	    features = []
220	    for key, value in preferences.items():
221	        if key in ['make', 'model']:
222	            # Handle make/model specially
223	            features.append(f"{{features:{key.lower()}}}:{value}")
224	        else:
225	            features.append(f"{{features:{key}}}:{value}")
226	    
227	    # Create the where clause based on selected facets
228	    if not facet_filters or all(len(filters) == 0 for filters in facet_filters.values()):
229	        # No filters, just use "true"
230	        where_clause = "true"
231	    else:
232	        # Start building an AND clause
233	        and_conditions = []
234	        
235	        # Add make filter if any
236	        if facet_filters.get('make') and len(facet_filters['make']) > 0:
237	            make_conditions = []
238	            for make in facet_filters['make']:
239	                make_conditions.append({"contains": ["make", make]})
240	            and_conditions.append({"or": make_conditions})
241	        
242	        # Add model filter if any
243	        if facet_filters.get('model') and len(facet_filters['model']) > 0:
244	            model_conditions = []
245	            for model in facet_filters['model']:
246	                model_conditions.append({"contains": ["model", model]})
247	            and_conditions.append({"or": model_conditions})
248	        
249	        # Add transmission filter if any
250	        if facet_filters.get('transmission') and len(facet_filters['transmission']) > 0:
251	            transmission_conditions = []
252	            for transmission in facet_filters['transmission']:
253	                transmission_conditions.append({"contains": ["transmission", transmission]})
254	            and_conditions.append({"or": transmission_conditions})
255	        
256	        # Add fuelType filter if any
257	        if facet_filters.get('fuelType') and len(facet_filters['fuelType']) > 0:
258	            fuelType_conditions = []
259	            for fuelType in facet_filters['fuelType']:
260	                fuelType_conditions.append({"contains": ["fuelType", fuelType]})
261	            and_conditions.append({"or": fuelType_conditions})
262	        
263	        # Final where clause
264	        where_clause = {"and": and_conditions}
265	    
266	    # Results-only query without grouping
267	    query = {
268	        "select": {
269	            "where": where_clause
270	        },
271	        "hits": 10,
272	        "ranking": "rank_cars",
273	        # default summary, so we also get car_features, rendered as {label: value}
274	        "presentation.format.tensors": "short-value",
275	        "ranking.features.query(user_preferences)": '{' + ','.join(features) + '}',
276	        "trace.level": 1
277	    }
278	    
279	    print(f"Sending results query to Vespa: {json.dumps(query, indent=2)}")
280	    
281	    try:
282	        # Use mTLS certificates for authentication
283	        response = requests.post(
284	            VESPA_SEARCH_URL, 
285	            json=query,
286	            cert=(CERT_PATH, KEY_PATH)
287	        )
288	        
289	        response.raise_for_status()
290	        results = response.json()
291	        
292	        # Don't wait for image loading - just return the results
293	        # Each car result will have a "car_id" that the frontend can use to request images
294	        if results and "root" in results and "children" in results["root"]:
295	            for item in results["root"]["children"]:
296	                if "fields" in item:
297	                    # Add a unique car ID based on make and model
298	                    make = item["fields"].get("make", "")
299	                    model = item["fields"].get("model", "")
300	                    if make and model:
301	                        item["fields"]["car_id"] = f"{make}_{model}".replace(" ", "_")
302	        
303	        return results
304	    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
305	        print(f"Error querying Vespa for results: {e}")
306	        if hasattr(e, 'response') and hasattr(e.response, 'text'):
307	            print(f"Response body: {e.response.text}")
308	        return None

310	def query_vespa_facets(preferences, facet_filters=None):

135	def process_products(output_dir: Path, full: bool = False, limit: int = 10) -> None:

1	# # Visual PDF Retrieval - demo application
2	#
3	# In this notebook, we will prepare the Vespa backend application for our visual retrieval demo.
4	# We will use ColPali as the model to extract patch vectors from images of pdf pages.
5	# At query time, we use MaxSim to retrieve and/or (based on the configuration) rank the page results.
6	#
7	# To see the application in action, visit https://huggingface.co/spaces/vespa-engine/colpali-vespa-visual-retrieval
8	#
9	# The web application is written in FastHTML, meaning the complete application is written in python.
10	#
11	# The steps we will take in this notebook are:
12	#
13	# 0. Setup and configuration
14	# 1. Download the data
15	# 2. Prepare the data
16	# 3. Generate queries for evaluation and typeahead search suggestions
17	# 4. Deploy the Vespa application
18	# 5. Create the Vespa application
19	# 6. Feed the data to the Vespa application
20	#
21	# All the steps that are needed to provision the Vespa application, including feeding the data, can be done from this notebook.

214	    try:

216	        report_response.raise_for_status()
217	        report_soup = BeautifulSoup(report_response.text, "html.parser")
218	        
219	        # Find only the first PDF download link with the specific class
220	        pdf_link = report_soup.select_one("a.btn.btn-secondary[data-right-icon='download']")
221	        if not pdf_link or not pdf_link["href"].endswith(".pdf"):

224	        pdf_url = urljoin(report_url, pdf_link["href"])

240	from nest_asyncio import apply
241	from typing import List
242	
243	apply()
244	
245	max_attempts = 3
246	
247	
248	async def download_pdf(session, url, filename):
249	    attempt = 0
250	    while attempt < max_attempts:
251	        try:
252	            response = await session.get(url)
253	            response.raise_for_status()
254	
255	            # Use Content-Disposition header to get the filename if available
256	            content_disposition = response.headers.get("Content-Disposition")
257	            if content_disposition:
258	                import re
259	
260	                fname = re.findall('filename="(.+)"', content_disposition)
261	                if fname:
262	                    filename = fname[0]
263	
264	            # Ensure the filename is safe to use on the filesystem
265	            safe_filename = filename.replace("/", "_").replace("\\", "_")
266	            if not safe_filename or safe_filename == "_":
267	                print(f"Invalid filename: {filename}")
268	                continue
269	
270	            filepath = os.path.join("pdfs", safe_filename)
271	            with open(filepath, "wb") as f:
272	                f.write(response.content)
273	            print(f"Downloaded {safe_filename}")
274	            return filepath
275	        except Exception as e:
276	            print(f"Error downloading {filename}: {e}")
277	            print(f"Retrying ({attempt})...")
278	            await asyncio.sleep(1)  # Wait a bit before retrying
279	            attempt += 1
280	    return None
281	
282	
283	async def download_pdfs(links: List[str]) -> List[dict]:
284	    """Download PDFs from a list of URLs. Add the filename to the dictionary."""
285	    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
286	        tasks = []
287	
288	        for idx, link in enumerate(links):
289	            # Try to get the filename from the URL
290	            path = urlparse(link).path
291	            filename = os.path.basename(path)
292	
293	            # If filename is empty,skip
294	            if not filename:
295	                continue
296	            tasks.append(download_pdf(client, link, filename))
297	
298	        # Run the tasks concurrently
299	        paths = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
300	        pdf_files = [
301	            {"url": link, "path": path} for link, path in zip(links, paths) if path
302	        ]
303	        return pdf_files
304	
305	
306	# Create the pdfs directory if it doesn't exist
307	os.makedirs("pdfs", exist_ok=True)
308	# Now run the download_pdfs function with the URL
309	pdfs = asyncio.run(download_pdfs(links))

312	pdfs

318	# +
319	def get_pdf_images(pdf_path):
320	    reader = PdfReader(pdf_path)
321	    page_texts = []
322	    for page_number in range(len(reader.pages)):
323	        page = reader.pages[page_number]
324	        text = page.extract_text()
325	        page_texts.append(text)
326	    images = convert_from_path(pdf_path)
327	    # Convert to PIL images
328	    assert len(images) == len(page_texts)
329	    return images, page_texts

331	
332	pdf_folder = "pdfs"
333	pdf_pages = []

335	    pdf_file = pdf["path"]
336	    title = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pdf_file))[0]
337	    images, texts = get_pdf_images(pdf_file)
338	    for page_no, (image, text) in enumerate(zip(images, texts)):
339	        pdf_pages.append(

341	                "title": title,

344	                "path": pdf_file,

1	import base64

4

7	from vespa.application import Vespa
8	from vespa.io import VespaResponse
9	
10	load_dotenv()
11	
12	VESPA_APP_TOKEN_URL = os.getenv("VESPA_APP_TOKEN_URL")
13	VESPA_CLOUD_SECRET_TOKEN = os.getenv("VESPA_CLOUD_SECRET_TOKEN")
14	
15	ds = load_dataset("vespa-engine/gpfg-QA", split="train", streaming=True)
16	
17	app = Vespa(
18	    url=VESPA_APP_TOKEN_URL,
19	    vespa_cloud_secret_token=VESPA_CLOUD_SECRET_TOKEN,
20	)
21	app.get_application_status()
22	
23	
24	def pil_to_base64(pil_image):
25	    """Convert PIL image to base64 string"""
26	    buffer = BytesIO()
27	    pil_image.save(buffer, format="JPEG")
28	    buffer.seek(0)
29	    image_base64 = base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("utf-8")
30	    return image_base64
31	
32	
33	def process_item_for_vespa(item):
34	    """Convert dataset item to Vespa format with base64 images and proper embedding structure"""
35	    # Convert PIL images to base64
36	    blur_image_b64 = pil_to_base64(item["blur_image"])
37	    full_image_b64 = pil_to_base64(item["full_image"])
38	
39	    # Reconstruct embedding dictionary from separate embedding.X fields
40	    embedding_dict = {}
41	    for key, value in item.items():
42	        if key.startswith("embedding."):
43	            # Extract the number after "embedding."
44	            embedding_index = int(key.split(".")[1])
45	            embedding_dict[embedding_index] = value
46	
47	    # Return Vespa-formatted item
48	    return {
49	        "id": item["id"],
50	        "fields": {
51	            "id": item["id"],
52	            "url": item["url"],
53	            "title": item["title"],
54	            "year": item["year"],
55	            "page_number": item["page_number"],
56	            "blur_image": blur_image_b64,
57	            "full_image": full_image_b64,
58	            "text": item["text"],
59	            "embedding": embedding_dict,
60	            "queries": item["queries"],
61	            "questions": item["questions"],
62	        },
63	    }
64	
65	
66	# Map the dataset to convert to Vespa format
67	vespa_feed = ds.map(process_item_for_vespa)
68	
69	
70	def callback(response: VespaResponse, id: str):
71	    if not response.is_successful():
72	        print(
73	            f"Failed to feed document {id} with status code {response.status_code}: Reason {response.get_json()}"
74	        )
75	
76	
77	# Feed data into Vespa asynchronously
78	app.feed_async_iterable(vespa_feed, schema="pdf_page", callback=callback)

55	            )

86	    def format_query_results(

92	        Args:

108	        self,
109	        query: str,
110	        q_emb: torch.Tensor,
111	        hits: int = 3,
112	        timeout: str = "10s",
113	        sim_map: bool = False,
114	        **kwargs,
115	    ) -> dict:
116	        """
117	        Query Vespa using the BM25 ranking profile.
118	        This corresponds to the "BM25" radio button in the UI.
119	
120	        Args:
121	            query (str): The query text.
122	            q_emb (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings.
123	            hits (int, optional): Number of hits to retrieve. Defaults to 3.
124	            timeout (str, optional): Query timeout. Defaults to "10s".
125	
126	        Returns:
127	            dict: The formatted query results.
128	        """
129	        async with self.app.asyncio(connections=1) as session:
130	            query_embedding = self.format_q_embs(q_emb)
131	
132	            start = time.perf_counter()
133	            response: VespaQueryResponse = await session.query(
134	                body={
135	                    "yql": (
136	                        f"select {self.get_fields(sim_map=sim_map)} from {self.VESPA_SCHEMA_NAME} where userQuery();"
137	                    ),
138	                    "ranking": self.get_rank_profile("bm25", sim_map),
139	                    "query": query,
140	                    "timeout": timeout,
141	                    "hits": hits,
142	                    "input.query(qt)": query_embedding,
143	                    "presentation.timing": True,
144	                    **kwargs,
145	                },
146	            )
147	            assert response.is_successful(), response.json
148	            stop = time.perf_counter()
149	            self.logger.debug(
150	                f"Query time + data transfer took: {stop - start} s, Vespa reported searchtime was "
151	                f"{response.json.get('timing', {}).get('searchtime', -1)} s"
152	            )
153	        return self.format_query_results(query, response)
154	
155	    def float_to_binary_embedding(self, float_query_embedding: dict) -> dict:
156	        """
157	        Convert float query embeddings to binary embeddings.
158	
159	        Args:
160	            float_query_embedding (dict): Dictionary of float embeddings.
161	
162	        Returns:
163	            dict: Dictionary of binary embeddings.
164	        """
165	        binary_query_embeddings = {}
166	        for key, vector in float_query_embedding.items():
167	            binary_vector = (
168	                np.packbits(np.where(np.array(vector) > 0, 1, 0))
169	                .astype(np.int8)
170	                .tolist()
171	            )
172	            binary_query_embeddings[key] = binary_vector
173	            if len(binary_query_embeddings) >= self.MAX_QUERY_TERMS:
174	                self.logger.warning(
175	                    f"Warning: Query has more than {self.MAX_QUERY_TERMS} terms. Truncating."
176	                )
177	                break
178	        return binary_query_embeddings
179	
180	    def create_nn_query_strings(
181	        self, binary_query_embeddings: dict, target_hits_per_query_tensor: int = 20
182	    ) -> Tuple[str, dict]:
183	        """
184	        Create nearest neighbor query strings for Vespa.
185	
186	        Args:
187	            binary_query_embeddings (dict): Binary query embeddings.
188	            target_hits_per_query_tensor (int, optional): Target hits per query tensor. Defaults to 20.
189	
190	        Returns:
191	            Tuple[str, dict]: Nearest neighbor query string and query tensor dictionary.
192	        """
193	        nn_query_dict = {}
194	        for i in range(len(binary_query_embeddings)):
195	            nn_query_dict[f"input.query(rq{i})"] = binary_query_embeddings[i]
196	        nn = " OR ".join(
197	            [
198	                f"({{targetHits:{target_hits_per_query_tensor}}}nearestNeighbor(embedding,rq{i}))"
199	                for i in range(len(binary_query_embeddings))
200	            ]
201	        )
202	        return nn, nn_query_dict
203	
204	    def format_q_embs(self, q_embs: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
205	        """
206	        Convert query embeddings to a dictionary of lists.
207	
208	        Args:
209	            q_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings tensor.
210	
211	        Returns:
212	            dict: Dictionary where each key is an index and value is the embedding list.
213	        """
214	        return {idx: emb.tolist() for idx, emb in enumerate(q_embs)}
215	
216	    async def get_result_from_query(
217	        self,
218	        query: str,
219	        q_embs: torch.Tensor,
220	        ranking: str,
221	        idx_to_token: dict,
222	    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
223	        """
224	        Get query results from Vespa based on the ranking method.
225	
226	        Args:
227	            query (str): The query text.
228	            q_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings.
229	            ranking (str): The ranking method to use.
230	            idx_to_token (dict): Index to token mapping.
231	
232	        Returns:
233	            Dict[str, Any]: The query results.
234	        """
235	
236	        # Remove stopwords from the query to avoid visual emphasis on irrelevant words (e.g., "the", "and", "of")
237	        query = backend.stopwords.filter(query)
238	
239	        rank_method = ranking.split("_")[0]
240	        sim_map: bool = len(ranking.split("_")) > 1 and ranking.split("_")[1] == "sim"
241	        if rank_method == "colpali":  # ColPali
242	            result = await self.query_vespa_colpali(
243	                query=query, ranking=rank_method, q_emb=q_embs, sim_map=sim_map
244	            )
245	        elif rank_method == "hybrid":  # Hybrid ColPali+BM25
246	            result = await self.query_vespa_colpali(
247	                query=query, ranking=rank_method, q_emb=q_embs, sim_map=sim_map
248	            )
249	        elif rank_method == "bm25":
250	            result = await self.query_vespa_bm25(query, q_embs, sim_map=sim_map)
251	        else:
252	            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ranking: {rank_method}")
253	        if "root" not in result or "children" not in result["root"]:
254	            result["root"] = {"children": []}
255	            return result
256	        for single_result in result["root"]["children"]:
257	            self.logger.debug(single_result["fields"].keys())
258	        return result
259	
260	    def get_sim_maps_from_query(
261	        self, query: str, q_embs: torch.Tensor, ranking: str, idx_to_token: dict
262	    ):
263	        """
264	        Get similarity maps from Vespa based on the ranking method.
265	
266	        Args:
267	            query (str): The query text.
268	            q_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings.
269	            ranking (str): The ranking method to use.
270	            idx_to_token (dict): Index to token mapping.
271	
272	        Returns:
273	            Dict[str, Any]: The query results.
274	        """
275	        # Get the result by calling asyncio.run
276	        result = asyncio.run(
277	            self.get_result_from_query(query, q_embs, ranking, idx_to_token)
278	        )
279	        vespa_sim_maps = []
280	        for single_result in result["root"]["children"]:
281	            vespa_sim_map = single_result["fields"].get("summaryfeatures", None)
282	            if vespa_sim_map is not None:
283	                vespa_sim_maps.append(vespa_sim_map)
284	            else:
285	                raise ValueError("No sim_map found in Vespa response")
286	        return vespa_sim_maps
287	
288	    async def get_full_image_from_vespa(self, doc_id: str) -> str:
289	        """
290	        Retrieve the full image from Vespa for a given document ID.
291	
292	        Args:
293	            doc_id (str): The document ID.
294	
295	        Returns:
296	            str: The full image data.
297	        """
298	        async with self.app.asyncio(connections=1) as session:
299	            start = time.perf_counter()
300	            response: VespaQueryResponse = await session.query(
301	                body={
302	                    "yql": f'select full_image from {self.VESPA_SCHEMA_NAME} where id contains "{doc_id}"',
303	                    "ranking": "unranked",
304	                    "presentation.timing": True,
305	                    "ranking.matching.numThreadsPerSearch": 1,
306	                },
307	            )
308	            assert response.is_successful(), response.json
309	            stop = time.perf_counter()
310	            self.logger.debug(
311	                f"Getting image from Vespa took: {stop - start} s, Vespa reported searchtime was "
312	                f"{response.json.get('timing', {}).get('searchtime', -1)} s"
313	            )
314	        return response.json["root"]["children"][0]["fields"]["full_image"]
315	
316	    def get_results_children(self, result: VespaQueryResponse) -> list:
317	        return result["root"]["children"]
318	
319	    def results_to_search_results(
320	        self, result: VespaQueryResponse, idx_to_token: dict
321	    ) -> list:
322	        # Initialize sim_map_ fields in the result
323	        fields_to_add = [
324	            f"sim_map_{token}_{idx}"
325	            for idx, token in idx_to_token.items()
326	            if not SimMapGenerator.should_filter_token(token)
327	        ]
328	        for child in result["root"]["children"]:
329	            for sim_map_key in fields_to_add:
330	                child["fields"][sim_map_key] = None
331	        return self.get_results_children(result)
332	
333	    async def get_suggestions(self, query: str) -> list:
334	        async with self.app.asyncio(connections=1) as session:
335	            start = time.perf_counter()
336	            yql = f'select questions from {self.VESPA_SCHEMA_NAME} where questions matches (".*{query}.*")'
337	            response: VespaQueryResponse = await session.query(
338	                body={
339	                    "yql": yql,
340	                    "query": query,
341	                    "ranking": "unranked",
342	                    "presentation.timing": True,
343	                    "presentation.summary": "suggestions",
344	                    "ranking.matching.numThreadsPerSearch": 1,
345	                },
346	            )
347	            assert response.is_successful(), response.json
348	            stop = time.perf_counter()
349	            self.logger.debug(
350	                f"Getting suggestions from Vespa took: {stop - start} s, Vespa reported searchtime was "
351	                f"{response.json.get('timing', {}).get('searchtime', -1)} s"
352	            )
353	            search_results = (
354	                response.json["root"]["children"]
355	                if "root" in response.json and "children" in response.json["root"]
356	                else []
357	            )
358	            questions = [
359	                result["fields"]["questions"]
360	                for result in search_results
361	                if "questions" in result["fields"]
362	            ]
363	
364	            unique_questions = set([item for sublist in questions for item in sublist])
365	
366	            # remove an artifact from our data generation
367	            if "string" in unique_questions:
368	                unique_questions.remove("string")
369	
370	            return list(unique_questions)
371	
372	    def get_rank_profile(self, ranking: str, sim_map: bool) -> str:
373	        if sim_map:
374	            return f"{ranking}_sim"
375	        else:
376	            return ranking
377	
378	    async def query_vespa_colpali(
379	        self,
380	        query: str,
381	        ranking: str,
382	        q_emb: torch.Tensor,
383	        target_hits_per_query_tensor: int = 100,
384	        hnsw_explore_additional_hits: int = 300,
385	        hits: int = 3,
386	        timeout: str = "10s",
387	        sim_map: bool = False,
388	        **kwargs,
389	    ) -> dict:
390	        """
391	        Query Vespa using nearest neighbor search with mixed tensors for MaxSim calculations.
392	        This corresponds to the "ColPali" radio button in the UI.
393	
394	        Args:
395	            query (str): The query text.
396	            q_emb (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings.
397	            target_hits_per_query_tensor (int, optional): Target hits per query tensor. Defaults to 20.
398	            hits (int, optional): Number of hits to retrieve. Defaults to 3.
399	            timeout (str, optional): Query timeout. Defaults to "10s".
400	
401	        Returns:
402	            dict: The formatted query results.
403	        """
404	        async with self.app.asyncio(connections=1) as session:
405	            float_query_embedding = self.format_q_embs(q_emb)
406	            binary_query_embeddings = self.float_to_binary_embedding(
407	                float_query_embedding
408	            )
409	
410	            # Mixed tensors for MaxSim calculations
411	            query_tensors = {
412	                "input.query(qtb)": binary_query_embeddings,
413	                "input.query(qt)": float_query_embedding,
414	            }
415	            nn_string, nn_query_dict = self.create_nn_query_strings(
416	                binary_query_embeddings, target_hits_per_query_tensor
417	            )
418	            query_tensors.update(nn_query_dict)
419	            response: VespaQueryResponse = await session.query(
420	                body={
421	                    **query_tensors,
422	                    "presentation.timing": True,
423	                    "yql": (
424	                        f"select {self.get_fields(sim_map=sim_map)} from {self.VESPA_SCHEMA_NAME} where {nn_string} or userQuery()"
425	                    ),
426	                    "ranking.profile": self.get_rank_profile(
427	                        ranking=ranking, sim_map=sim_map
428	                    ),
429	                    "timeout": timeout,
430	                    "hits": hits,
431	                    "query": query,
432	                    "hnsw.exploreAdditionalHits": hnsw_explore_additional_hits,
433	                    "ranking.rerankCount": 100,
434	                    **kwargs,
435	                },
436	            )
437	            assert response.is_successful(), response.json
438	        return self.format_query_results(query, response)
439	
440	    async def keepalive(self) -> bool:
441	        """
442	        Query Vespa to keep the connection alive.
443	
444	        Returns:
445	            bool: True if the connection is alive.
446	        """
447	        async with self.app.asyncio(connections=1) as session:
448	            response: VespaQueryResponse = await session.query(
449	                body={
450	                    "yql": f"select title from {self.VESPA_SCHEMA_NAME} where true limit 1;",
451	                    "ranking": "unranked",
452	                    "query": "keepalive",
453	                    "timeout": "3s",
454	                    "hits": 1,
455	                },
456	            )
457	            assert response.is_successful(), response.json
458	        return True

1	import torch
2	from PIL import Image
3	import numpy as np
4	from typing import Generator, Tuple, List, Union, Dict
5	from pathlib import Path
6	import base64
7	from io import BytesIO
8	import re
9	import io
10	import matplotlib.cm as cm
11	
12	from colpali_engine.models import ColPali, ColPaliProcessor
13	from colpali_engine.utils.torch_utils import get_torch_device
14	from colpali_engine.interpretability.similarity_map_utils import normalize_similarity_map
15	from functools import lru_cache
16	import logging
17	
18	
19	class SimMapGenerator:
20	    """
21	    Generates similarity maps based on query embeddings and image patches using the ColPali model.
22	    """
23	
24	    colormap = cm.viridis  # Preload colormap for efficiency
25	
26	    def __init__(
27	        self,
28	        logger: logging.Logger,
29	        model_name: str = "vidore/colpali-v1.2",
30	        n_patch: int = 32,
31	    ):
32	        """
33	        Initializes the SimMapGenerator class with a specified model and patch dimension.
34	
35	        Args:
36	            model_name (str): The model name for loading the ColPali model.
37	            n_patch (int): The number of patches per dimension.
38	        """
39	        self.model_name = model_name
40	        self.n_patch = n_patch
41	        self.device = get_torch_device("auto")
42	        self.logger = logger
43	        self.logger.info(f"Using device: {self.device}")
44	        self.model, self.processor = self.load_model()
45	
46	    def load_model(self) -> Tuple[ColPali, ColPaliProcessor]:
47	        """
48	        Loads the ColPali model and processor.
49	
50	        Returns:
51	            Tuple[ColPali, ColPaliProcessor]: Loaded model and processor.
52	        """
53	        model = ColPali.from_pretrained(
54	            self.model_name,
55	            dtype=torch.bfloat16,  # Note that the embeddings created during feed were float32 -> binarized, yet setting this seem to produce the most similar results both locally (mps) and HF (Cuda)
56	            device_map=self.device,
57	        ).eval()
58	
59	        processor = ColPaliProcessor.from_pretrained(self.model_name)
60	        return model, processor
61	
62	    def gen_similarity_maps(
63	        self,
64	        query: str,
65	        query_embs: torch.Tensor,
66	        token_idx_map: Dict[int, str],
67	        images: List[Union[Path, str]],
68	        vespa_sim_maps: List[Dict],
69	    ) -> Generator[Tuple[int, str, str], None, None]:
70	        """
71	        Generates similarity maps for the provided images and query, and returns base64-encoded blended images.
72	
73	        Args:
74	            query (str): The query string.
75	            query_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings tensor.
76	            token_idx_map (dict): Mapping from indices to tokens.
77	            images (List[Union[Path, str]]): List of image paths or base64-encoded strings.
78	            vespa_sim_maps (List[Dict]): List of Vespa similarity maps.
79	
80	        Yields:
81	            Tuple[int, str, str]: A tuple containing the image index, selected token, and base64-encoded image.
82	        """
83	        processed_images, original_images, original_sizes = [], [], []
84	        for img in images:
85	            img_pil = self._load_image(img)
86	            original_images.append(img_pil.copy())
87	            original_sizes.append(img_pil.size)
88	            processed_images.append(img_pil)
89	
90	        vespa_sim_map_tensor = self._prepare_similarity_map_tensor(
91	            query_embs, vespa_sim_maps
92	        )
93	        similarity_map_normalized = normalize_similarity_map(
94	            vespa_sim_map_tensor.flatten(0, 1)
95	        ).reshape(vespa_sim_map_tensor.shape)
96	
97	        for idx, img in enumerate(original_images):
98	            for token_idx, token in token_idx_map.items():
99	                if self.should_filter_token(token):
100	                    continue
101	
102	                sim_map = similarity_map_normalized[idx, token_idx, :, :]
103	                blended_img_base64 = self._blend_image(
104	                    img, sim_map, original_sizes[idx]
105	                )
106	                yield idx, token, token_idx, blended_img_base64
107	
108	    def _load_image(self, img: Union[Path, str]) -> Image:
109	        """
110	        Loads an image from a file path or a base64-encoded string.
111	
112	        Args:
113	            img (Union[Path, str]): The image to load.
114	
115	        Returns:
116	            Image: The loaded PIL image.
117	        """
118	        try:
119	            if isinstance(img, Path):
120	                return Image.open(img).convert("RGB")
121	            elif isinstance(img, str):
122	                return Image.open(BytesIO(base64.b64decode(img))).convert("RGB")
123	        except Exception as e:
124	            raise ValueError(f"Failed to load image: {e}")
125	
126	    def _prepare_similarity_map_tensor(
127	        self, query_embs: torch.Tensor, vespa_sim_maps: List[Dict]
128	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
129	        """
130	        Prepares a similarity map tensor from Vespa similarity maps.
131	
132	        Args:
133	            query_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings tensor.
134	            vespa_sim_maps (List[Dict]): List of Vespa similarity maps.
135	
136	        Returns:
137	            torch.Tensor: The prepared similarity map tensor.
138	        """
139	        vespa_sim_map_tensor = torch.zeros(
140	            (len(vespa_sim_maps), query_embs.size(0), self.n_patch, self.n_patch)
141	        )
142	        for idx, vespa_sim_map in enumerate(vespa_sim_maps):
143	            for cell in vespa_sim_map["quantized"]["cells"]:
144	                patch = int(cell["address"]["patch"])
145	                query_token = int(cell["address"]["querytoken"])
146	                value = cell["value"]
147	                if hasattr(self.processor, "image_seq_length"):
148	                    image_seq_length = self.processor.image_seq_length
149	                else:
150	                    image_seq_length = 1024
151	
152	                if patch >= image_seq_length:
153	                    continue
154	                vespa_sim_map_tensor[
155	                    idx,
156	                    query_token,
157	                    patch // self.n_patch,
158	                    patch % self.n_patch,
159	                ] = value
160	        return vespa_sim_map_tensor
161	
162	    def _blend_image(
163	        self, img: Image, sim_map: torch.Tensor, original_size: Tuple[int, int]
164	    ) -> str:
165	        """
166	        Blends an image with a similarity map and encodes it to base64.
167	
168	        Args:
169	            img (Image): The original image.
170	            sim_map (torch.Tensor): The similarity map tensor.
171	            original_size (Tuple[int, int]): The original size of the image.
172	
173	        Returns:
174	            str: The base64-encoded blended image.
175	        """
176	        SCALING_FACTOR = 8
177	        sim_map_resolution = (
178	            max(32, int(original_size[0] / SCALING_FACTOR)),
179	            max(32, int(original_size[1] / SCALING_FACTOR)),
180	        )
181	
182	        sim_map_np = sim_map.cpu().float().numpy()
183	        sim_map_img = Image.fromarray(sim_map_np).resize(
184	            sim_map_resolution, resample=Image.BICUBIC
185	        )
186	        sim_map_resized_np = np.array(sim_map_img, dtype=np.float32)
187	        sim_map_normalized = self._normalize_sim_map(sim_map_resized_np)
188	
189	        heatmap = self.colormap(sim_map_normalized)
190	        heatmap_img = Image.fromarray((heatmap * 255).astype(np.uint8)).convert("RGBA")
191	
192	        buffer = io.BytesIO()
193	        heatmap_img.save(buffer, format="PNG")
194	        return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("utf-8")
195	
196	    @staticmethod
197	    def _normalize_sim_map(sim_map: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
198	        """
199	        Normalizes a similarity map to range [0, 1].
200	
201	        Args:
202	            sim_map (np.ndarray): The similarity map.
203	
204	        Returns:
205	            np.ndarray: The normalized similarity map.
206	        """
207	        sim_map_min, sim_map_max = sim_map.min(), sim_map.max()
208	        if sim_map_max - sim_map_min > 1e-6:
209	            return (sim_map - sim_map_min) / (sim_map_max - sim_map_min)
210	        return np.zeros_like(sim_map)
211	
212	    @staticmethod
213	    def should_filter_token(token: str) -> bool:
214	        """
215	        Determines if a token should be filtered out based on predefined patterns.
216	
217	        The function filters out tokens that:
218	
219	            - Start with '<' (e.g., '<bos>')
220	            - Consist entirely of whitespace
221	            - Are purely punctuation (excluding tokens that contain digits or start with '▁')
222	            - Start with an underscore '_'
223	            - Exactly match the word 'Question'
224	            - Are exactly the single character '▁'
225	
226	        Output of test:
227	            Token: '2'         | False
228	            Token: '0'         | False
229	            Token: '2'         | False
230	            Token: '3'         | False
231	            Token: '▁2'        | False
232	            Token: '▁hi'       | False
233	            Token: 'norwegian' | False
234	            Token: 'unlisted'  | False
235	            Token: '<bos>'     | True
236	            Token: 'Question'  | True
237	            Token: ':'         | True
238	            Token: '<pad>'     | True
239	            Token: '\n'        | True
240	            Token: '▁'         | True
241	            Token: '?'         | True
242	            Token: ')'         | True
243	            Token: '%'         | True
244	            Token: '/)'        | True
245	
246	
247	        Args:
248	            token (str): The token to check.
249	
250	        Returns:
251	            bool: True if the token should be filtered out, False otherwise.
252	        """
253	        pattern = re.compile(

4	# Initialize LRU Cache
5	class LRUCache:
6	    def __init__(self, max_size=20):
7	        self.max_size = max_size
8	        self.cache = OrderedDict()
9	
10	    def get(self, key):
11	        if key in self.cache:
12	            self.cache.move_to_end(key)
13	            return self.cache[key]
14	        return None
15	
16	    def set(self, key, value):
17	        if key in self.cache:
18	            self.cache.move_to_end(key)
19	        else:
20	            if len(self.cache) >= self.max_size:
21	                self.cache.popitem(last=False)
22	        self.cache[key] = value
23	
24	    def delete(self, key):
25	        if key in self.cache:
26	            del self.cache[key]

8	# but that would require a java plugin which we didn't want to complicate this sample app with.
9	def filter(text):
10	    doc = nlp(text)
11	    tokens = [token.text for token in doc if not token.is_stop]
12	    if len(tokens) == 0:
13	        # if we remove all the words we don't have a query at all, so use the original
14	        return text
15	    return " ".join(tokens)

19	def read_embeddings(file_name):
20	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
21	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
22	        sys.exit(1)
23	    print("Reading embeddings data from " + file_name)
24	    embeddings = {}
25	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
26	        for line in f:
27	            id, vector = line.split("\t")
28	            embeddings[id] = np.array(vector.split(","), dtype=np.float32)
29	    return embeddings
30	
31	
32	def convert_user_embeddings():
33	    user_embeddings = read_embeddings(user_embeddings_file)
34	    with open(user_embeddings_vespa, "w") as out:
35	        out.write("[\n")
36	        for i, (user_id, embedding) in enumerate(user_embeddings.items()):
37	            if i > 0:
38	                out.write(",\n")
39	            embedding_str = ",".join(["%.6f" % v for v in embedding])
40	            out.write('{"put": "id:user:user::%s", ' % user_id +
41	                      '"fields": {"user_id":"%s", ' % user_id +
42	                      '"embedding": {"values": [%s]} }}' % embedding_str)
43	        out.write("\n]\n")
44	
45	
46	def convert_news_embeddings():
47	    news_embeddings = read_embeddings(news_embeddings_file)
48	    with open(news_embeddings_vespa, "w") as out:
49	        out.write("[\n")
50	        for i, (news_id, embedding) in enumerate(news_embeddings.items()):
51	            if i > 0:
52	                out.write(",\n")
53	            embedding_str = ",".join(["%.6f" % v for v in embedding])
54	            out.write('{"update": "id:news:news::%s", ' % news_id +
55	                      '"fields": {"embedding": {"assign": { "values": [%s]} }}}' % embedding_str)
56	        out.write("\n]\n")
57	
58	
59	def main():
60	    convert_user_embeddings()
61	    convert_news_embeddings()
62	
63	
64	if __name__ == "__main__":
65	    main()

20	dev_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news.tsv")
21	dev_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "behaviors.tsv")
22	out_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "vespa.json")
23	
24	
25	def read_impressions_file(file_name, click_map):
26	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
27	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
28	        sys.exit(1)
29	    print("Reading impressions data from " + file_name)
30	
31	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
32	        field_list = ["id", "user_id", "timestamp", "history", "impressions"]
33	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
34	        for line in reader:
35	            for impression in line["impressions"].split(" "):
36	                news_id, label = impression.split("-")
37	                click_map[news_id]["impressions"] += 1
38	                if label == "1":
39	                    click_map[news_id]["clicks"] += 1
40	
41	
42	def convert_file(output, file_name, docids, click_map):
43	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
44	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
45	        sys.exit(1)
46	    print("Reading news data from " + file_name)
47	
48	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
49	
50	        field_list = ["news_id", "category", "subcategory", "title", "abstract", "url", "title_entities", "abstract_entities"]
51	        include_fields = set(field_list[0:6])
52	
53	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
54	        for line in reader:
55	            if line["news_id"] in docids:
56	                continue
57	            if len(docids) > 0:
58	                output.write(",\n")
59	            docid = line["news_id"]
60	            docids.add(docid)
61	
62	            clicks = click_map[docid]["clicks"]
63	            impressions = click_map[docid]["impressions"]
64	
65	            doc = {"put": f"id:{doc_type}:{doc_type}::{docid}", "fields" : {} }
66	            for field in include_fields:
67	                doc["fields"][field] = line[field]
68	            doc["fields"]["date"] = generate_random_date()  # data set does not include a publish date
69	            doc["fields"]["clicks"] = clicks
70	            doc["fields"]["impressions"] = impressions
71	            json.dump(doc, output)
72	
73	
74	def generate_random_date():
75	    random_date = dt.fromtimestamp(random.randint(1572562800, 1573686000))
76	    return int(dt.strftime(random_date, "%Y%m%d"))
77	
78	
79	def main():
80	    click_map = defaultdict(lambda: {"clicks":0,"impressions":0})
81	    read_impressions_file(train_impressions_file, click_map)
82	    read_impressions_file(dev_impressions_file, click_map)
83	    with open(out_file, "w") as out:
84	        out.write("[\n")
85	        docids = set()
86	        convert_file(out, train_news_file, docids, click_map)
87	        convert_file(out, dev_news_file, docids, click_map)
88	        out.write("\n]\n")
89	        print("{} documents".format(len(docids)))
90	
91	
92	if __name__ == "__main__":
93	    main()

11	
12	
13	logging.set_verbosity_error()
14	
15	data_dir = sys.argv[1]
16	doc_type = "mind"

18	train_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news.tsv")
19	train_embedding_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news_embeddings.tsv")
20	dev_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news.tsv")
21	dev_embedding_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news_embeddings.tsv")
22	
23	field_list = ["docid", "category", "subcategory", "title", "abstract", "url", "title_entities", "abstract_entities"]
24	
25	
26	def create_embeddings(input_file_name, output_file_name):
27	    docids = set()
28	    titles = {}
29	    abstracts = {}
30	    categories = {}
31	    subcategories = {}
32	
33	    # read
34	    with io.open(input_file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
35	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
36	        for line in reader:
37	            docid = line["docid"]
38	            docids.add(docid)
39	            titles[docid] = line["title"]
40	            abstracts[docid] = line["abstract"]
41	            categories[docid] = line["category"]
42	            subcategories[docid] = line["subcategory"]
43	
44	    print("Read {} documents".format(len(docids)))
45	
46	    # convert and write
47	    tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
48	    model = BertModel.from_pretrained('google/bert_uncased_L-8_H-512_A-8')
49	    t = time.time()
50	    with open(output_file_name, "w") as f:
51	        for i, docid in enumerate(docids):
52	            title = titles[docid]
53	            abstract = abstracts[docid]
54	
55	            f.write(docid)
56	
57	            tokens = tokenizer(title, abstract, return_tensors="pt", max_length=100, truncation=True, padding=True)
58	            outputs = model(**tokens)
59	            write_embedding(f, outputs[0].tolist()[0][0])
60	
61	            f.write("\n")
62	
63	            if i % (len(docids)//100) == (len(docids)//100 - 1):
64	                print("Completed {} embeddings ({:.0f} %) [{:.2f} s]".format(i + 1, 100.0 *(i+1)/len(docids), time.time()-t))
65	                t = time.time()
66	
67	
68	def write_embedding(f, embedding):
69	    f.write("\t")
70	    for j, num in enumerate(embedding):
71	        if j > 0:
72	            f.write(",")
73	        f.write("%.4f" % num)
74	
75	
76	def main():
77	    create_embeddings(train_news_file, train_embedding_file)
78	    create_embeddings(dev_news_file, dev_embedding_file)
79	
80	
81	if __name__ == "__main__":
82	    main()

24	def read_impressions_file(file_name, click_map, news_map):
25	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
26	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
27	        sys.exit(1)
28	    print("Reading impressions data from " + file_name)
29	
30	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
31	        field_list = ["id", "user_id", "timestamp", "history", "impressions"]
32	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
33	        for line in reader:
34	            for impression in line["impressions"].split(" "):
35	                news_id, label = impression.split("-")
36	                if news_id in news_map:
37	                    category = news_map[news_id]
38	                    click_map[category]["impressions"] += 1
39	                    if label == "1":
40	                        click_map[category]["clicks"] += 1
41	
42	
43	def read_content_file(file_name, news_map):
44	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
45	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
46	        sys.exit(1)
47	    print("Reading news data from " + file_name)
48	
49	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
50	        field_list = ["news_id", "category", "subcategory", "title", "abstract", "url", "title_entities", "abstract_entities"]
51	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
52	        for line in reader:
53	            news_map[line["news_id"]] = line["category"]
54	
55	
56	def write_global_ctr_document(category_ctr_map):
57	    tensor_cells = []
58	    for category, ctr_data in category_ctr_map.items():
59	        category_ctr = ctr_data["clicks"] / ctr_data["impressions"] if ctr_data["impressions"] > 0 else 0.0
60	        cell = {"address":{"category":category}, "value": category_ctr}
61	        tensor_cells.append(cell)
62	    ctrs_tensor = {"ctrs": {"cells": tensor_cells}}
63	
64	    global_ctr_document = {"put": "id:category_ctr:category_ctr::global", "fields": ctrs_tensor}
65	    with open(global_ctr_file, "w") as out:
66	        json.dump(global_ctr_document, out)
67	
68	
69	def write_news_category_ctr_update(news_to_cat_map):
70	    global_ctr_document_id = "id:category_ctr:category_ctr::global"
71	    with open(news_category_ctr_update_file, "w") as out:
72	        out.write("[\n")
73	        for i, (news_id, category) in enumerate(news_to_cat_map.items()):
74	            if i > 0:
75	                out.write(",\n")
76	            category_tensor = '{"cells": [{"address":{"category":"%s"}, "value": 1.0}]}' % category
77	            out.write('{"update": "id:news:news::%s", ' % news_id +
78	                      '"fields": {' +
79	                          '"category_ctr_ref": {"assign": "%s"}, ' % global_ctr_document_id +
80	                          '"category_tensor": {"assign": %s}' % category_tensor +
81	                      '}}')
82	        out.write("\n]\n")
83	
84	
85	def main():
86	    news_to_cat_map = {}
87	    read_content_file(train_news_file, news_to_cat_map)
88	    read_content_file(dev_news_file, news_to_cat_map)

91	    read_impressions_file(train_impressions_file, category_ctr_map, news_to_cat_map)
92	    read_impressions_file(dev_impressions_file, category_ctr_map, news_to_cat_map)
93	
94	    write_global_ctr_document(category_ctr_map)
95	    write_news_category_ctr_update(news_to_cat_map)

99	    main()

25	def read_impressions_file(file_name):
26	    impressions = []
27	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
28	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
29	        sys.exit(1)
30	    print("Reading impressions data from " + file_name)
31	
32	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
33	        field_list = ["id", "user_id", "timestamp", "history", "impressions"]
34	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
35	        for line in reader:
36	            user_id = line["user_id"]
37	            impression = {
38	                "user_id": user_id,
39	                "news_ids": [],
40	                "labels": []
41	            }
42	            for i in line["impressions"].split(" "):
43	                news_id, label = i.split("-")
44	                impression["news_ids"].append(news_id)
45	                impression["labels"].append(int(label))
46	            impressions.append(impression)
47	    return impressions
48	
49	
50	def query_news_ids(user_vector, news_ids):
51	    news_id_filter = [ 'news_id contains "{}"'.format(i) for i in news_ids ]
52	    news_id_filter = "AND ({})".format(" OR ".join(news_id_filter))
53	    return query_news(user_vector, len(news_ids), news_id_filter, url, cert, timeout=10)
54	
55	def find_hit(hits, news_id):
56	    for child in hits["root"]["children"]:
57	        if child["fields"]["news_id"] == news_id:
58	            return child
59	    return None
60	
61	
62	def predictions(hits, news_ids):
63	    preds = []
64	    for news_id in news_ids:
65	        hit = find_hit(hits, news_id)
66	        relevance = hit["relevance"]
67	        preds.append(relevance)
68	    return preds
69	
70	
71	def calc_impression(impression):
72	    user_id = impression["user_id"]
73	    user_vector = query_user_embedding(user_id, url, cert)
74	    result = query_news_ids(user_vector, impression["news_ids"])
75	    preds = predictions(result, impression["news_ids"])
76	    labels = impression["labels"]
77	
78	    return preds, labels
79	
80	
81	def calc_metrics(file):
82	    all_predictions = []
83	    all_labels = []
84	    impressions = read_impressions_file(file)
85	    if sample_size > 0:
86	        impressions = random.sample(impressions, sample_size)
87	    for i, impression in enumerate(impressions):
88	        preds, labels = calc_impression(impression)
89	        all_predictions.append(preds)
90	        all_labels.append(labels)
91	        if i % 100 == 99:
92	            print("Completed {} / {}".format(i+1,len(impressions)))
93	
94	    metrics = {
95	        "auc": group_auc(all_predictions, all_labels),
96	        "mrr": mrr(all_predictions, all_labels),
97	        "ndcg@5": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 5),
98	        "ndcg@10": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 10)
99	    }
100	    return metrics

102
