3	
4	import numpy as np
5	from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
6	
7	
8	def group_auc(preds, labels):
9	    group_auc = np.mean(
10	        [
11	            roc_auc_score(each_labels, each_preds)
12	            for each_labels, each_preds in zip(labels, preds)
13	        ]
14	    )
15	    return round(group_auc, 4)
16	
17	
18	def dcg_score(y_true, y_score, k=10):
19	    k = min(np.shape(y_true)[-1], k)
20	    order = np.argsort(y_score)[::-1]
21	    y_true = np.take(y_true, order[:k])
22	    gains = 2 ** y_true - 1
23	    discounts = np.log2(np.arange(len(y_true)) + 2)
24	    return np.sum(gains / discounts)
25	
26	
27	def ndcg_score(y_true, y_score, k=10):
28	    best = dcg_score(y_true, y_true, k)
29	    actual = dcg_score(y_true, y_score, k)
30	    return actual / best
31	
32	
33	def ndcg(preds, labels, k):
34	    ndcg_temp = np.mean(
35	        [
36	            ndcg_score(each_labels, each_preds, k)
37	            for each_labels, each_preds in zip(labels, preds)
38	        ]
39	    )
40	    return round(ndcg_temp, 4)
41	
42	
43	def mrr_score(y_true, y_score):
44	    order = np.argsort(y_score)[::-1]
45	    y_true = np.take(y_true, order)
46	    rr_score = y_true / (np.arange(len(y_true)) + 1)
47	    return np.sum(rr_score) / np.sum(y_true)
48	
49	
50	def mrr(preds, labels):
51	    mean_mrr = np.mean(
52	        [
53	            mrr_score(each_labels, each_preds)
54	            for each_labels, each_preds in zip(labels, preds)
55	        ]
56	    )
57	    return round(mean_mrr, 4)

4	import os

15	class MindData:
16	    def __init__(self, train_news_file, train_impressions_file, valid_news_file, valid_impressions_file):
17	        self.user_map = {}    # Mapping from user_id to index, e.g. "U82271" -> 0, "U84185" -> 1 etc
18	        self.news_map = {}    # Mapping from news_id to index, e.g. "N27209" -> 0
19	        self.cat_map = {}     # Mapping from category to index, e.g. "health" -> 0
20	        self.sub_cat_map = {} # Mapping from subcategory to index, e.g. "medical" -> 0
21	        self.entity_map = {}  # Mapping from entity id to index, e.g. "Q212" -> 0  (WikidataId for "ukraine")
22	        self.news_content = {}
23	        self.train_impressions = []
24	        self.valid_impressions = []
25	        self.read_data(train_impressions_file, self.train_impressions)
26	        self.read_data(valid_impressions_file, self.valid_impressions)
27	        self.read_news(train_news_file)
28	        self.read_news(valid_news_file)
29	
30	    def users(self):
31	        return self.user_map
32	
33	    def news(self):
34	        return self.news_map
35	
36	    def categories(self):
37	        return self.cat_map
38	
39	    def subcategories(self):
40	        return self.sub_cat_map
41	
42	    def entities(self):
43	        return self.entity_map
44	
45	    def read_news(self, news_file):
46	        if not os.path.exists(news_file):
47	            print("{} not found.".format(news_file))
48	            sys.exit(1)
49	        print("Reading data from " + news_file)
50	
51	        with io.open(news_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
52	            for line in f:
53	                news_data = line.split("\t")
54	                doc_id = news_data[0]
55	                category = news_data[1]
56	                subcategory = news_data[2]
57	                title = news_data[3]
58	                abstract = news_data[4]
59	                url = news_data[5]
60	                title_entities = json.loads(news_data[6]) if len(news_data) > 6 else []
61	                abstract_entities = json.loads(news_data[7]) if len(news_data) > 7 else []
62	
63	                entities_to_keep = 2
64	                entity_ids = []
65	                self.add_entities(entity_ids, title_entities)
66	                self.add_entities(entity_ids, abstract_entities)
67	                entity_ids.extend([""] * entities_to_keep)
68	
69	                self.news_content[self.lookup_news_index(doc_id)] = {
70	                    "news_id": doc_id,
71	                    "category_index": self.lookup_category_index(category),
72	                    "subcategory_index": self.lookup_subcategory_index(subcategory),
73	                    "entity_index": [ self.lookup_entity_index(id) for id in entity_ids[:entities_to_keep]]
74	                }
75	
76	    def add_entities(self, entity_ids: list, entities: list):
77	        for entity in entities:
78	            entity_id = entity["WikidataId"]
79	            if entity_id not in entity_ids:
80	                entity_ids.append(entity_id)
81	
82	    def read_data(self, impressions_file, impression_list):
83	        if not os.path.exists(impressions_file):
84	            print("{} not found.".format(impressions_file))
85	            sys.exit(1)
86	        print("Reading data from " + impressions_file)
87	
88	        with io.open(impressions_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
89	            for line in f:
90	                impression_data = line.split("\t")
91	                impression_id = impression_data[0]
92	                user_id = impression_data[1]
93	                time = datetime.datetime.strptime(impression_data[2], "%m/%d/%Y %I:%M:%S %p")
94	                history = set(impression_data[3].split(" "))
95	                impressions = impression_data[4].split(" ")
96	
97	                news_indices, labels = self.find_labels(impressions, history)
98	
99	                impression_list.append({
100	                    "user_index": self.lookup_user_index(user_id),
101	                    "timestamp": time,
102	                    "news_indices": news_indices,
103	                    "labels": labels
104	                })
105	
106	    def find_labels(self, impressions, history):
107	        news_indices = []
108	        labels = []
109	        for impression in impressions:
110	            news_id, label = impression.split("-")
111	            if news_id not in history:  # don't add news previously clicked (in history)
112	                news_indices.append(self.lookup_news_index(news_id))
113	                labels.append(int(label))
114	        return news_indices, labels
115	
116	    def lookup_user_index(self, user_id):
117	        return self.lookup_index(user_id, self.user_map)
118	
119	    def lookup_news_index(self, news_id):
120	        return self.lookup_index(news_id, self.news_map)
121	
122	    def lookup_category_index(self, category):
123	        return self.lookup_index(category, self.cat_map)
124	
125	    def lookup_subcategory_index(self, subcategory):
126	        return self.lookup_index(subcategory, self.sub_cat_map)
127	
128	    def lookup_entity_index(self, entity_id):
129	        return self.lookup_index(entity_id, self.entity_map)
130	
131	    def lookup_index(self, id, map):
132	        if id not in map:
133	            map[id] = len(map)
134	        return map[id]
135	
136	    def sample_training_data(self, batch_size, num_negatives, prob=1.0):
137	        user_indices = []
138	        news_indices = []
139	        category_indices = []
140	        subcategory_indices = []
141	        entity_indices = []
142	        labels = []
143	
144	        for impression in self.train_impressions:
145	            if random.random() <= prob:
146	                self.add_impressions(impression, user_indices, news_indices, category_indices, subcategory_indices, entity_indices, labels, num_negatives)
147	
148	        data_set = TensorDataset(
149	                        torch.LongTensor(user_indices),
150	                        torch.LongTensor(news_indices),
151	                        torch.LongTensor(category_indices),
152	                        torch.LongTensor(subcategory_indices),
153	                        torch.LongTensor(entity_indices),
154	                        torch.FloatTensor(labels))
155	        generator = torch.Generator()
156	        random_sampler = RandomSampler(data_set, generator=generator)
157	        return DataLoader(data_set, batch_size=batch_size, sampler=random_sampler)
158	
159	    def sample_valid_data(self, prob=1.0, train=False):
160	        data = []
161	        impressions = self.train_impressions if train else self.valid_impressions
162	        for impression in impressions:
163	            if random.random() <= prob:
164	                news_indices = impression["news_indices"]
165	                labels = impression["labels"]
166	                category_indices = [ self.news_content[index]["category_index"] for index in news_indices ]
167	                subcategory_indices = [ self.news_content[index]["subcategory_index"] for index in news_indices ]
168	                entity_indices = [ self.news_content[index]["entity_index"] for index in news_indices ]
169	                user_index = [ impression["user_index"] ] * len(labels)
170	                if sum(labels) > 0 and sum(labels) != len(labels):
171	                    data.append([
172	                        torch.LongTensor(user_index),
173	                        torch.LongTensor(news_indices),
174	                        torch.LongTensor(category_indices),
175	                        torch.LongTensor(subcategory_indices),
176	                        torch.LongTensor(entity_indices),
177	                        torch.FloatTensor(labels)
178	                    ])
179	        return data
180	
181	    def add_impressions(self, impression, user_indices, news_indices, category_indices, subcategory_indices, entity_indices, labels, num_negatives):
182	        user_index = impression["user_index"]
183	        positive, negative = self.find_clicked(impression["news_indices"], impression["labels"])
184	
185	        # add each positive label
186	        for pos_news_index in positive:
187	            user_indices.append(user_index)
188	            news_indices.append(pos_news_index)
189	            category_indices.append(self.news_content[pos_news_index]["category_index"])
190	            subcategory_indices.append(self.news_content[pos_news_index]["subcategory_index"])
191	            entity_indices.append(self.news_content[pos_news_index]["entity_index"])
192	            labels.append(1)
193	
194	            # for each positive label, sample negative labels
195	            for neg_news_index in random.sample(negative, min(num_negatives, len(negative))):
196	                user_indices.append(user_index)
197	                news_indices.append(neg_news_index)
198	                category_indices.append(self.news_content[neg_news_index]["category_index"])
199	                subcategory_indices.append(self.news_content[neg_news_index]["subcategory_index"])
200	                entity_indices.append(self.news_content[neg_news_index]["entity_index"])
201	                labels.append(0)
202	
203	    def find_clicked(self, news_ids, labels):
204	        clicked = []
205	        skipped = []
206	        for news_id, label in zip(news_ids, labels):
207	            if label > 0:
208	                clicked.append(news_id)
209	            else:
210	                skipped.append(news_id)
211	        return clicked, skipped
212	
213	    def get_news_content_tensors(self):
214	        num_docs = len(self.news_map)
215	        news_indices = [0] * num_docs
216	        category_indices = [0] * num_docs
217	        subcategory_indices = [0] * num_docs
218	        entity_indices = [0] * num_docs
219	
220	        for news_index, content in self.news_content.items():
221	            news_indices[news_index] = news_index
222	            category_indices[news_index] = content["category_index"]
223	            subcategory_indices[news_index] = content["subcategory_index"]
224	            entity_indices[news_index] = content["entity_index"]
225	
226	        return torch.LongTensor(news_indices), \
227	               torch.LongTensor(category_indices), \
228	               torch.LongTensor(subcategory_indices),\
229	               torch.LongTensor(entity_indices),

1	#! /usr/bin/env python3
2	# Copyright Vespa.ai. Licensed under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. See LICENSE in the project root.
3	
4	import io
5	import os
6	import sys
7	import numpy
8	import random
9	import torch
10	import numpy as np
11	
12	from mind_data import MindData
13	from metrics import ndcg, mrr, group_auc
14	
15	
16	data_dir = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "../../mind/"
17	epochs = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 15
18	
19	train_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news.tsv")
20	valid_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news.tsv")
21	train_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "behaviors.tsv")
22	valid_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "behaviors.tsv")
23	train_embeddings_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news_embeddings.tsv")
24	valid_embeddings_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news_embeddings.tsv")
25	
26	# hyperparameters
27	embedding_size = 50
28	negative_sample_size = 4
29	batch_size = 128
30	
31	adam_lr = 1e-3  # 5e-4
32	l2_regularization = 1e-5  # 0.01
33	
34	
35	class ContentBasedModel(torch.nn.Module):
36	    def __init__(self, num_users, num_news, num_categories, num_subcategories, num_entities, embedding_size, bert_embeddings):
37	        super(ContentBasedModel, self).__init__()
38	
39	        # Embedding tables for category variables
40	        self.user_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_users, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
41	        self.news_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_news, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
42	        self.cat_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_categories, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
43	        self.sub_cat_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_subcategories, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
44	        self.entity_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_entities, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
45	
46	        # Pretrained BERT embeddings
47	        self.news_bert_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding.from_pretrained(bert_embeddings, freeze=True)
48	
49	        # Linear transformation from BERT size to embedding size (512 -> 50)
50	        self.news_bert_transform = torch.nn.Linear(bert_embeddings.shape[1], embedding_size)
51	
52	        # Linear transformation from concatenation of category, subcategory, entity and BERT embedding
53	        self.news_content_transform = torch.nn.Linear(in_features=embedding_size*5, out_features=embedding_size)
54	
55	    def get_user_embeddings(self, users):
56	        return self.user_embeddings(users)
57	
58	    def get_news_embeddings(self, items, categories, subcategories, entities):
59	        # Transform BERT representation to a shorter embedding
60	        bert_embeddings = self.news_bert_embeddings(items)
61	        bert_embeddings = self.news_bert_transform(bert_embeddings)
62	        bert_embeddings = torch.sigmoid(bert_embeddings)
63	
64	        # Create news content representation by concatenating BERT, category, subcategory and entities
65	        cat_embeddings = self.cat_embeddings(categories)
66	        news_embeddings = self.news_embeddings(items)
67	        sub_cat_embeddings = self.sub_cat_embeddings(subcategories)
68	        entity_embeddings_1 = self.entity_embeddings(entities[:,0])
69	        news_embedding = torch.cat((news_embeddings, bert_embeddings, cat_embeddings, sub_cat_embeddings, entity_embeddings_1), 1)
70	        news_embedding = self.news_content_transform(news_embedding)
71	        news_embedding = torch.sigmoid(news_embedding)
72	
73	        return news_embedding
74	
75	    def forward(self, users, items, categories, subcategories, entities):
76	        user_embeddings = self.get_user_embeddings(users)
77	        news_embeddings = self.get_news_embeddings(items, categories, subcategories, entities)
78	        dot_prod = torch.sum(torch.mul(user_embeddings, news_embeddings), 1)
79	        return torch.sigmoid(dot_prod)
80	
81	
82	def train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, criterion):
83	    total_loss = 0
84	    for batch_num, batch in enumerate(sample_data):
85	
86	        # get the inputs - data is a user_id and news_id which looks up the embedding, and a label
87	        user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities, labels = batch
88	
89	        # zero to parameter gradients
90	        optimizer.zero_grad()
91	
92	        # forward + backward + optimize
93	        prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities)
94	        loss = criterion(prediction.view(-1), labels)
95	        loss.backward()
96	        optimizer.step()
97	
98	        # keep track of statistics
99	        total_loss += loss
100	
101	    print("Total loss after epoch {}: {} ({} avg)".format(epoch+1, total_loss, total_loss / len(sample_data)))
102	
103	
104	def train_model(model, data_loader):
105	    criterion = torch.nn.BCELoss()
106	    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=adam_lr, weight_decay=l2_regularization)
107	    for epoch in range(epochs):
108	
109	        # create data for this epoch
110	        sample_data = data_loader.sample_training_data(batch_size, negative_sample_size)
111	
112	        # train
113	        train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, criterion)
114	
115	        # evaluate every epoch
116	        eval_model(model, data_loader, train=True)
117	        eval_model(model, data_loader, 1.0)
118	
119	        # save embeddings if better auc - TODO
120	        save_embeddings(model, data_loader)
121	
122	
123	def eval_model(model, data_loader, sample_prob=1.0, train=False):
124	    sample_data = data_loader.sample_valid_data(sample_prob, train=train)
125	    with torch.no_grad():
126	
127	        all_predictions = []
128	        all_labels = []
129	
130	        for impression in sample_data:  # make an iterator instead
131	            user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities, labels = impression
132	            prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities).view(-1)

3	
4	import os
5	import sys
6	import numpy
7	import random
8	import torch
9	
10	from mind_data import MindData
11	from metrics import ndcg, mrr, group_auc
12	
13	
14	data_dir = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "../../mind/"
15	epochs = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100
16	
17	train_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news.tsv")
18	valid_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news.tsv")
19	train_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "behaviors.tsv")
20	valid_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "behaviors.tsv")
21	train_embeddings_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news_embeddings.tsv")
22	valid_embeddings_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news_embeddings.tsv")
23	
24	# hyperparameters
25	embedding_size = 50
26	negative_sample_size = 4
27	batch_size = 1024
28	
29	adam_lr = 1e-3
30	l2_regularization = 0  # 1e-5
31	
32	
33	class MF(torch.nn.Module):
34	    def __init__(self, num_users, num_items, embedding_size):
35	        super(MF, self).__init__()
36	        self.user_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_users, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
37	        self.news_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_items, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
38	
39	    def forward(self, users, items):
40	        user_embeddings = self.user_embeddings(users)
41	        news_embeddings = self.news_embeddings(items)
42	        dot_prod = torch.sum(torch.mul(user_embeddings, news_embeddings), 1)
43	        return torch.sigmoid(dot_prod)
44	
45	
46	def train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, loss_function):
47	    total_loss = 0
48	    for batch_num, batch in enumerate(sample_data):
49	
50	        # get the inputs - data is a user_id and news_id which looks up the embedding, and a label
51	        user_ids, news_ids, _, _, _, labels = batch
52	
53	        # zero to parameter gradients
54	        optimizer.zero_grad()
55	
56	        # forward + backward + optimize
57	        prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids)
58	        loss = loss_function(prediction.view(-1), labels)
59	        loss.backward()
60	        optimizer.step()
61	
62	        # keep track of statistics
63	        total_loss += loss
64	
65	    print("Total loss after epoch {}: {} ({} avg)".format(epoch+1, total_loss, total_loss / len(sample_data)))
66	
67	
68	def train_model(model, data_loader):
69	    loss_func = torch.nn.BCELoss()
70	    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=adam_lr, weight_decay=l2_regularization)
71	    for epoch in range(epochs):
72	
73	        # create data for this epoch
74	        sample_data = data_loader.sample_training_data(batch_size, negative_sample_size)
75	
76	        # train
77	        train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, loss_func)
78	
79	        if epoch % 10 == 9:
80	            eval_model(model, data_loader, train=True)
81	            eval_model(model, data_loader)
82	
83	
84	def eval_model(model, data_loader, sample_prob=1.0, train=False):
85	    sample_data = data_loader.sample_valid_data(sample_prob, train=train)
86	    with torch.no_grad():
87	
88	        all_predictions = []
89	        all_labels = []
90	
91	        for impression in sample_data:
92	            user_ids, news_ids, _, _, _, labels = impression
93	            prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids).view(-1)
94	            all_predictions.append(prediction.detach().numpy())
95	            all_labels.append(labels.detach().numpy())
96	
97	        metrics = {
98	            "auc": group_auc(all_predictions, all_labels),
99	            "mrr": mrr(all_predictions, all_labels),
100	            "ndcg@5": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 5),
101	            "ndcg@10": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 10)
102	        }
103	        print(metrics)
104	
105	
106	def save_embeddings(model, data_loader):
107	    user_map = data_loader.users()
108	    news_map = data_loader.news()
109	    user_embeddings = model.user_embeddings(torch.LongTensor(range(len(user_map))))
110	    news_embeddings = model.news_embeddings(torch.LongTensor(range(len(news_map))))
111	    write_embeddings(user_map, user_embeddings, "user_embeddings.tsv")
112	    write_embeddings(news_map, news_embeddings, "news_embeddings.tsv")
113	
114	
115	def write_embeddings(id_to_index_map, embeddings, file_name):
116	    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, file_name), "w") as f:
117	        for id, index in id_to_index_map.items():
118	            f.write("{}\t{}\n".format(id, ",".join(["%.6f" % i for i in embeddings[index].tolist()])))
119	
120	
121	def set_random_seed(seed):
122	    os.environ['PYTHONHASHSEED'] = str(seed)
123	    torch.manual_seed(seed)
124	    torch.cuda.manual_seed(seed)
125	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
126	    numpy.random.seed(seed)
127	    random.seed(seed)
128	
129	
130	def main():
131	    set_random_seed(1)
132	
133	    # read data
134	    data_loader = MindData(train_news_file, train_impressions_file, valid_news_file, valid_impressions_file)
135	    num_users = len(data_loader.users())
136	    num_news = len(data_loader.news())
137	
138	    # create model
139	    model = MF(num_users, num_news, embedding_size)
140	
141	    # train model
142	    train_model(model, data_loader)
143	
144	    # evaluate model
145	    eval_model(model, data_loader, train=True)
146	    eval_model(model, data_loader)
147	
148	    # save embeddings
149	    save_embeddings(model, data_loader)
150	
151	
152	if __name__ == "__main__":
153	    main()

1	#! /usr/bin/env python3
2	# Copyright Vespa.ai. Licensed under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. See LICENSE in the project root.
3	
4	"""Shared query helpers for the news sample application.
5	
6	The endpoint and - on Vespa Cloud - the mTLS certificate are resolved from the
7	Vespa CLI, so the same scripts work against a local container and against a
8	Vespa Cloud deployment without any changes.
9	"""
10	
11	import re
12	import subprocess
13	import urllib.parse
14	
15	import requests
16	
17	
18	def vespa_endpoint():
19	    """Return the endpoint URL of the current 'vespa' CLI target."""
20	    result = subprocess.run(["vespa", "status", "--format", "plain"],
21	                            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
22	    return result.stdout.strip()
23	
24	
25	def vespa_cert():
26	    """Return (cert, key) paths from 'vespa curl', or None when no mTLS is configured."""
27	    result = subprocess.run(["vespa", "curl", "-n", "/"],
28	                            capture_output=True, text=True)
29	    output = result.stdout + result.stderr
30	    paths = dict(re.findall(r'--(cert|key) (\S+)', output))
31	    if "cert" in paths and "key" in paths:
32	        return (paths["cert"], paths["key"])
33	    return None
34	
35	
36	def connect():
37	    """Return (url, cert) for the current 'vespa' CLI target."""
38	    return vespa_endpoint(), vespa_cert()
39	
40	
41	def parse_embedding(hit_json):
42	    return hit_json["fields"]["embedding"]["values"]
43	
44	
45	def query_user_embedding(user_id, url, cert):
46	    yql = 'select * from sources user where user_id contains "{}"'.format(user_id)
47	    url = '{}/search/?yql={}&hits=1'.format(url, urllib.parse.quote_plus(yql))
48	    result = requests.get(url, cert=cert).json()
49	    return parse_embedding(result["root"]["children"][0])
50	
51	
52	def query_news(user_vector, hits, filter, url, cert, timeout=None):
53	    nn_annotations = [
54	        'targetHits:{}'.format(hits)
55	        ]

1	import os
2	import glob
3	import ntpath
4	from collections import Counter

6	import numpy as np
7	import imageio
8	
9	
10	from vespa.package import ApplicationPackage, Field, HNSW, RankProfile, QueryTypeField
11	from vespa.application import Vespa
12	import torch
13	from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader
14	from torchvision.transforms import ToPILImage
15	import clip
16	from tenacity import retry, wait_exponential, stop_after_attempt
17	
18	
19	def translate_model_names_to_valid_vespa_field_names(model_name):
20	    return model_name.replace("/", "_").replace("-", "_").lower()
21	
22	
23	def sample_images(images, number_to_sample):
24	    """
25	    Sample equally spaced frames from a list of image frames
26	
27	    :param images: a list of image frames.
28	    :param number_to_sample: int representing the number os frames to sample.
29	
30	    :return: a numpy array containing the sample of frames.
31	    """
32	    if number_to_sample < len(images):
33	        idx = np.round(np.linspace(0, len(images) - 1, number_to_sample)).astype(int)
34	        return np.array(images)[idx]
35	    else:
36	        return np.array(images)
37	
38	
39	def extract_images(video_path, number_frames):
40	    """
41	    Extract equally spaced frames from a video.
42	
43	    :param video_path: Full .mp4 video path.
44	    :param number_frames: Number of frames to sample.
45	
46	    :return: a numpy array containing the sample of frames.
47	    """
48	    reader = imageio.get_reader(video_path, fps=1)
49	    frames = []
50	    for i, im in enumerate(reader):
51	        frames.append(im)
52	    return sample_images(frames, number_frames)
53	
54	
55	class VideoFeedDataset(Dataset):
56	    def __init__(self, video_dir, model_name, number_frames_per_video):
57	        """
58	        PyTorch Dataset to compute video embeddings and return pyvespa-compatible feed data.
59	
60	        :param video_dir: Folder containing .mp4 video files.
61	        :param model_name: CLIP model name.
62	        :param number_frames_per_video: Number of embeddings per video.
63	        """
64	        self.video_dir = video_dir
65	        self.number_frames_per_video = number_frames_per_video
66	        valid_vespa_model_name = translate_model_names_to_valid_vespa_field_names(
67	            model_name
68	        )
69	        self.from_tensor_to_PIL = ToPILImage()
70	        self.model, self.preprocess = clip.load(model_name)
71	        self.video_file_names = glob.glob(os.path.join(video_dir, "*.mp4"))
72	        self.image_embedding_name = valid_vespa_model_name + "_image"
73	
74	    def _from_image_to_vector(self, x):
75	        """
76	        From image to embedding.
77	
78	        :param x: PIL images
79	        :return: normalized image embeddings.
80	        """
81	        with torch.no_grad():
82	            image_features = self.model.encode_image(
83	                self.preprocess(x).unsqueeze(0)
84	            ).float()
85	            image_features /= image_features.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
86	        return image_features
87	
88	    def __len__(self):
89	        return len(self.video_file_names)
90	
91	    def __getitem__(self, idx):
92	        video_file_name = self.video_file_names[idx]
93	        images = extract_images(
94	            video_path=video_file_name, number_frames=self.number_frames_per_video
95	        )
96	        pil_images = [self.from_tensor_to_PIL(x) for x in images]
97	        frames = []
98	        for idx, image in enumerate(pil_images):
99	            image = self._from_image_to_vector(image)
100	            video_base_name = ntpath.basename(video_file_name)
101	            frames.append(
102	                {
103	                    "id": video_base_name.split(".mp4")[0] + "_{}".format(idx),
104	                    "fields": {
105	                        "video_file_name": video_base_name,
106	                        self.image_embedding_name: {"values": image.tolist()[0]},
107	                    },
108	                    "create": True,
109	                }
110	            )
111	        return frames
112	
113	
114	@retry(wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=1), stop=stop_after_attempt(3))
115	def send_video_embeddings(app, batch):
116	    """
117	    Send pyvespa-compatible batch to Vespa app.
118	
119	    :param app: pyvespa connection to a Vespa instance
120	    :param batch: pyvespa-compatible list of data points to be updated.
121	    :return: None
122	    """
123	    responses = app.update_batch(batch=batch)
124	    status_code_summary = Counter([x.status_code for x in responses])
125	    if status_code_summary[200] != len(batch):
126	        print([response.json for response in responses if response.status_code != 200])
127	        raise ValueError("Failed to send data.")
128	    print("Successfully sent {} data points.".format(status_code_summary[200]))
129	
130	
131	def compute_and_send_video_embeddings(
132	    app, batch_size, clip_model_names, number_frames_per_video, video_dir, num_workers=0
133	):
134	    """
135	    Loop through video folder, compute embeddings and send to Vespa app.
136	
137	    :param app: pyvespa connection to a Vespa instance
138	    :param batch_size: Number of images to process per iteration.
139	    :param clip_model_names: CLIP models names. It will generate one image embedding per model name.
140	    :param number_frames_per_video: Number of frames to use per video.
141	    :param video_dir: Complete path of the folder containing .mp4 video files.
142	    :param num_workers: Number of workers to use (refers to the DataLoader parallelization)
143	    :return: None
144	    """
145	    for model_name in clip_model_names:
146	        video_dataset = VideoFeedDataset(
147	            video_dir=video_dir,  # Folder containing image files
148	            model_name=model_name,  # CLIP model name used to convert image into vector
149	            number_frames_per_video=number_frames_per_video,
150	        )
151	        dataloader = DataLoader(
152	            video_dataset,
153	            batch_size=batch_size,
154	            shuffle=False,
155	            collate_fn=lambda x: [item for sublist in x for item in sublist],
156	            num_workers=num_workers,
157	        )
158	        for idx, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
159	            print(
160	                "Model name: {}. Iteration: {}/{}".format(
161	                    model_name, idx, len(dataloader)
162	                )
163	            )
164	            send_video_embeddings(app=app, batch=batch)

167	class TextProcessor(object):
168	    def __init__(self, model_name):
169	        """
170	        Python-based text processor.
171	
172	        :param model_name: CLIP model name to use embedding text.
173	        """
174	        self.model, _ = clip.load(model_name)
175	        self.model_name = model_name
176	
177	    def embed(self, text):
178	        """
179	        Convert text to (normalized) embedding
180	
181	        :param text: a string to be embedded.
182	        :return: Normalized embedding vector.
183	        """
184	        text_tokens = clip.tokenize(text)
185	        with torch.no_grad():
186	            text_features = self.model.encode_text(text_tokens).float()
187	            text_features /= text_features.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
188	        return text_features.tolist()[0]
189	
190	
191	def create_text_video_app(model_info):
192	    """
193	    Create text to video search app based on a variety of CLIP models
194	
195	    :param model_info: dict containing model names as keys and embedding size as values.
196	        Check `clip.available_models()` to check which models are available.
197	
198	    :return: A Vespa application package.
199	    """
200	    app_package = ApplicationPackage(name="videosearch")
201	
202	    app_package.schema.add_fields(
203	        Field(name="video_file_name", type="string", indexing=["summary", "attribute"]),
204	    )
205	    for model_name, embedding_size in model_info.items():
206	        model_name = translate_model_names_to_valid_vespa_field_names(model_name)
207	        app_package.schema.add_fields(
208	            Field(
209	                name=model_name + "_image",
210	                type="tensor<float>(x[{}])".format(embedding_size),
211	                indexing=["attribute", "index"],
212	                ann=HNSW(
213	                    distance_metric="euclidean",
214	                    max_links_per_node=16,
215	                    neighbors_to_explore_at_insert=500,
216	                ),
217	            )
218	        )
219	        app_package.schema.add_rank_profile(
220	            RankProfile(
221	                name=model_name + "_similarity",
222	                inherits="default",
223	                first_phase="closeness({})".format(model_name + "_image"),
224	            )
225	        )
226	        app_package.query_profile_type.add_fields(
227	            QueryTypeField(
228	                name="ranking.features.query({})".format(model_name + "_text"),
229	                type="tensor<float>(x[{}])".format(embedding_size),
230	            )
231	        )
232	    return app_package
233	
234	
235	def create_vespa_query(query, text_processor, number_videos):
236	    """
237	    Create the body of a Vespa query.
238	
239	    :param query: a string representing the query.
240	    :param text_processor: an instance of `TextProcessor` to convert string to embedding.
241	    :param number_videos: Number of videos to return.
242	    :return: body of a Vespa query request.
243	    """
244	    valid_vespa_model_name = translate_model_names_to_valid_vespa_field_names(
245	        text_processor.model_name
246	    )
247	    image_field_name = valid_vespa_model_name + "_image"
248	    text_field_name = valid_vespa_model_name + "_text"
249	    ranking_name = valid_vespa_model_name + "_similarity"
250	
251	    return {
252	        "yql": 'select * from sources * where ({{"targetNumHits":100}}nearestNeighbor({},{})) | all(group(video_file_name) max({}) order(-max(relevance())) each( max(1) each(output(summary())) as(frame)) as(video))'.format(
253	            image_field_name, text_field_name, number_videos
254	        ),
255	        "hits": 0,
256	        "ranking.features.query({})".format(text_field_name): text_processor.embed(
257	            query
258	        ),
259	        "ranking.profile": ranking_name,
260	        "timeout": 10,
261	    }
262	
263	
264	def search_video_file_names(app, query, text_processor, number_videos):
265	    """
266	    Parse the output of the Vespa query.
267	
268	    Parse the output of the Vespa query to return a list with the video file name and
269	    relevance score for each hit.
270	
271	    :param app: The pyvespa Vespa connection to the app.
272	    :param query: The text query to be sent.
273	    :param text_processor: An instance of the TextProcessor to turn text into embedding.
274	    :param number_videos: The number of videos to be retrieved.
275	    :return: a list with the video file name and relevance score for each hit.
276	    """
277	
278	    result = app.query(
279	        body=create_vespa_query(
280	            query=query, text_processor=text_processor, number_videos=number_videos
281	        )
282	    )
283	    parsed_results = [
284	        {
285	            "video_file_name": video["children"][0]["children"][0]["fields"][
286	                "video_file_name"
287	            ],
288	            "relevance": video["children"][0]["children"][0]["relevance"],
289	        }
290	        for video in result.json["root"]["children"][0]["children"][0]["children"]
291	    ]
292	    return parsed_results
293	
294	
295	class VideoSearchApp(object):
296	    def __init__(self, app: Vespa, clip_model_name=None, text_processor=None):
297	        """
298	        Video search app with custom query for video retrieval.
299	
300	        :param app: The pyvespa Vespa connection to the app.
301	        :param clip_model_name: CLIP model name to turn text into embedding
302	        :param text_processor: TextProcessor instance. `clip_model_name` will
303	            be ignored if an instance is provided.
304	        """
305	        if text_processor:
306	            self.text_processor = text_processor
307	        elif clip_model_name:
308	            self.text_processor = TextProcessor(clip_model_name)
309	        else:
310	            ValueError("Provide a clip_model_name or an instance of TextProcessor")
311	        self.app = app
312	
313	    def query(self, text, number_videos):
314	        """
315	        Video search
316	
317	        :param text: Text query describing an action.
318	        :param number_videos: Number of videos to retrieve.
319	        :return: a list with the video file name and relevance score for each hit.
320	        """
321	        return search_video_file_names(
322	            app=self.app,
323	            query=text,
324	            text_processor=self.text_processor,
325	            number_videos=number_videos,
326	        )

30	def get_label(text, examples):
31	    """
32	    Ask the LLM to categorize the input text into a single category
33	
34	    :param text:        Input query
35	    :param examples:    Array of (text, relevance, label)
36	    :return:            String with predicted category name
37	    """

39	    examples_string = "\n".join(
40	        [f"Text: {text}, Category: {predicted_label}" for text, relevance, predicted_label in examples])
41	    prompt = f"""

45	
46	    Think step by step and predict the category of the text, using examples provided below. 
47

76	    :param response:    A JSON Query response in https://docs.vespa.ai/en/reference/default-result-format.html
77	    :return:            Array of examples in (text, relevance, label) tuples
78	    """
79	    result = []
80	    groups = response['root'].get('children', []).pop().get('children', []).pop().get('children', [])
81	    for group in groups:
82	        hits = group.get('children', [])
83	        for hit in hits.pop().get('children', []):
84	            label = hit['fields']['label']
85	            text = hit['fields']['text']

93	    Fetch results from Vespa with different rank profiles.
94	    For simplicity, all queries here parse a result from a grouping expression,
95	    but queries can group on the label or not:
96	
97	        To run without grouping the result on label (i.e. no result diversity), use
98	            all(group(1) max(1) each(max(10) each(output(summary()))))
99	        This means, all in _one_ group, with 10 hits total.
100	
101	        To run _with_ grouping on the label, use
102	            all(group(label) max(10) each(max(2) each(output(summary()))))

104	
105	    {targetHits:10} for the NN operator should be large enough for the expected set of examples returned.

107	    Set the correct rank-profile in the ranking query parameter.
108	    The rank-profiles are configured in train.sd.

110	    timeout is set unusually high here, for laptop experiments.

112	    Note that the hybrid rank-profiles need

114	    to generate rank scores from both operators.

116	    When experimenting with different embedders, make sure to set the name in _both_ the ranking profile and
117	    the query ranking feature like
118	        'input.query(query_embedding)': 'embed(arctic, @query)'
119	    Here, the "arctic" embedder model is used, also see services.xml configuration for configuring this.
120	
121	    See start of file for how to configure the LLM client, opanAI/local / which local model to use.

1	import os
2	from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
3	from models.state import SubgraphState
4	from langgraph_modules.subgraph import subgraph
5	from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
6	from langgraph.graph import START

8	from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage
9	
10	from langchain_community.tools.tavily_search import TavilySearchResults
11	from langgraph.prebuilt import tools_condition, ToolNode
12	from utils.secrets import OPENAI_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY
13	
14	if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
15	  os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = OPENAI_API_KEY
16	if not os.environ.get("TAVILY_API_KEY"):  
17	  os.environ["TAVILY_API_KEY"] = TAVILY_API_KEY
18	
19	def VespaRetrieverTool(UserQuery: str) -> str:
20	    """Retrieves all items for sale matching the user query.
21	
22	    Args:
23	        UserQuery: User Query for items they are looking for.
24	    """
25	
26	    # Initiate a conversation with the UserQuery as a human message
27	    conversation = [ HumanMessage(content=UserQuery) ]
28	
29	    # Create an instance of SubgraphState with default values.
30	    # Make sure the constructor of SubgraphState accepts the required parameters.
31	    subgraph_state = SubgraphState(
32	        messages=conversation,
33	        SearchEngineQuery="",
34	        ClarifyingQuestion="",
35	        SearchEngineResults="",
36	        Filters=['quantity > 0'],
37	        Categories=[]
38	    )
39	
40	    # Test Invocation
41	    thread_config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "some_id"}}
42	
43	    # Invoke graph with a valid SubgraphState object
44	    result_state=subgraph.invoke(subgraph_state, config=thread_config)
45	
46	    #Fetch final result
47	    result=result_state["SearchEngineResults"]
48	
49	    return result
50	
51	TavilySearch = TavilySearchResults(max_results=2)
52	
53	tools = [TavilySearch, VespaRetrieverTool]
54	
55	llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini")
56	llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools(tools)
57	
58	# System message
59	sys_msg = SystemMessage(content="""You are a helpful sales assistant willing to answer any user questions about items to sell. You will abide by the following rules:
60	                                   - Rule 1: You will try your best to provide all the information regarding an item for sale to a customer.
61	                                   - Rule 2: When the user asks you a question unrelated to an item for sale, you can try to address the question, but always prompt the user back to ask for any items for sale, or relate their question to an item they might be looking for.
62	                                   - Rule 3: You may get a clarifying question as a result. In this case, please ask the question to the user. You do not need to be apologetic.
63	                                   - Rule 4: You may get an empty resultset as an answer. In this case, apologize and ask the the user if they are looking for something else.
64	                                    """)
65	# Node
66	def assistant(state: MessagesState):
67	   return {"messages": [llm_with_tools.invoke([sys_msg] + state["messages"])]}
68	
69	# Graph
70	builder = StateGraph(MessagesState)
71	
72	# Define nodes: these do the work
73	builder.add_node("assistant", assistant)
74	builder.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tools))
75	
76	# Define edges: these determine how the control flow moves
77	builder.add_edge(START, "assistant")
78	builder.add_conditional_edges(
79	    "assistant",
80	    # If the latest message (result) from assistant is a tool call -> tools_condition routes to tools
81	    # If the latest message (result) from assistant is a not a tool call -> tools_condition routes to END
82	    tools_condition,
83	)
84	builder.add_edge("tools", "assistant")

12	query_models =  {

30	  },

33	    'input.query(q)': 'embed(e5_embedding_model, "{query}")',

35	    'ranking': 'e5-colbert',
36	    'ranking.rerankCount': 100
37	  },

40	    'input.query(q)': 'embed(e5_embedding_model, "{query}")',

42	    'input.query(query_token_ids)':'embed(tokenizer, "{query}")',

44	    'ranking.rerankCount': 100,

46	  }
47	}
48	
49	def format_query(template, query):
50	    return template.format(query=query)
51	
52	# Fetch data from Vespa 
53	def get_result(query):
54	    global session, args
55	    params = query_models[args.model]
56	    formatted_params = dict()
57	    for key, value in params.items():
58	        if isinstance(value, str) and "{query}" in value:
59	            formatted_params[key] = format_query(value, query)
60	        else:
61	            formatted_params[key] = value
62	    request_body = {
63	        'hits': args.hits,
64	        'timeout': 10,
65	        'ranking.softtimeout.enable': 'false',
66	        **formatted_params
67	    }
68	    
69	    response = session.post(args.endpoint, json=request_body, timeout=10.0)
70	    if not response.ok:
71	        print("Failed request for query {}, response {}, response json {}".format(query, response, response.json()))
72	        return []
73	
74	    result = response.json()
75	    if result['root']['fields']['totalCount'] == 0:
76	        return []
77	    docs = []
78	    for h in result['root']['children']:
79	        fields = h.get('fields', None)
80	        if not fields:
81	            continue
82	        docs.append(fields.get('id'))
83	    return docs
84	
85	def eval_query(query):
86	    global args, session
87	    id, text = query
88	    docs = get_result(text)
89	    result_list = []
90	    for i, d in enumerate(docs):
91	        if args.trec_format:
92	            result_list.append("{}\tQ0\t{}\t{}\t{}\trun".format(id, d, i + 1, 1000 - i))
93	        else:
94	            result_list.append("{}\t{}\t{}".format(id, d, i + 1))
95	    return result_list
96	
97	def eval():
98	    queries = []
99	    dataset = ir_datasets.load('msmarco-passage/' + args.query_split + '/small')
100	    for query_id, text in dataset.queries_iter():
101	        queries.append((query_id, text))
102	    
103	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as executor:
104	        results = list(tqdm(executor.map(eval_query, queries), total=len(queries), desc="Fetching Results", leave=False))
105	    
106	    with open(args.run_file, "w") as fp:
107	        for result_list in results:
108	            for line in result_list:
109	                fp.write("{}\n".format(line))
110	
111	def main():
112	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
113	    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", type=str, default="http://localhost:8080/search/")
114	    parser.add_argument("--hits", type=int, default=10)
115	    parser.add_argument("--model", choices=list(query_models.keys()), required=True)
116	    parser.add_argument("--run_file", type=str, default="runfile")
117	    parser.add_argument("--query_split", choices=["dev", "eval"], required=True)
118	    parser.add_argument('--trec_format', dest='trec_format', default=False, action='store_true')
119	    parser.add_argument("--certificate", type=str)
120	    parser.add_argument("--key", type=str)
121	
122	    global args
123	    args = parser.parse_args()
124	    global session
125	    session = requests.Session()
126	    retries = Retry(total=5, connect=2,
127	      backoff_factor=0.3,
128	      status_forcelist=[ 500, 503, 504, 429 ]
129	    )
130	    session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
131	    session.mount('http://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
132	
133	    if args.certificate and args.key:
134	      session.cert = (args.certificate, args.key)
135

137

139	    main()

10	def create_request_specific_ids(query, rankprofile, doc_ids):
11	    body = {

14	        "hits": len(doc_ids),
15	        "recall": "+(" + " ".join(["id:" + str(doc) for doc in doc_ids]) + ")",

17	        "presentation.format": "json",

19	    }

24	
25	    body = {

30	        "presentation.format": "json",

36	def get_features(url, body):

54	        rankfeatures.update({"qid": query_id})
55	        rankfeatures.update({"relevant": 1 if h["fields"]["id"] == relevant_id else 0})
56	        data.append(rankfeatures)
57	    return data

61	    try:

63	        processed_queries = [int(x) for x in f_processed.readlines()]
64	        f_processed.close()
65	    except FileNotFoundError:

14	encoding = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("gpt-3.5-turbo")
15	note_pattern = re.compile(r"{%\s*include.*?%}", flags=re.DOTALL)
16	highlight_pattern = re.compile(r"{%\s*.*?\s%}", flags=re.DOTALL)
17	
18	
19	def what_language(el):
20	    z = re.match(r"{%\s*highlight\s*(\w+)\s%}", el.text)
21	    if z:
22	        lang =  z.group(1)
23	        return lang
24	    if el.text.find("curl") > 0:
25	        return "bash"
26	    if el.text.find("import com.yahoo") > 0:
27	        return "java"
28	    return ""
29	
30	def remove_jekyll(text):
31	    text = note_pattern.sub("", text)
32	    text = highlight_pattern.sub("", text)
33	    return text
34	
35	def xml_fixup(text):
36	    regex = r"{%\s*highlight xml\s*%}(.*?){%\s*endhighlight\s*%}"
37	    matches = re.findall(regex, text, re.DOTALL)
38	    for match in matches:
39	        escaped_match = escape(match)
40	        text = text.replace(match,escaped_match)
41	    return text
42	
43	def create_text_doc(doc, paragraph, paragraph_id, header):
44	    id = doc['put']
45	    #id:open:doc::open/en/access-logging.html#
46	    _,namespace,doc_type,_,id = id.split(":")
47	    #print("n={},doc_type={},id={}".format(namespace,doc_type,id))
48	   
49	    new_namespace = namespace + "-p"
50	    id = "id:{}:{}::{}".format(new_namespace, "paragraph", id)
51	    fields = doc['fields']
52	    n_tokens = len(encoding.encode(paragraph))
53	    new_doc = {
54	        "put": id,
55	        "fields": {
56	            "title": fields['title'],
57	            "path": fields['path'],
58	            "doc_id": fields['path'],
59	            "namespace": new_namespace,
60	            "content": paragraph,
61	            "content_tokens": n_tokens,
62	            "base_uri": sys.argv[2]
63	        }
64	    }
65	    
66	    if header:
67	        title = fields['title']
68	        new_title = title + " - " + header
69	        new_doc["fields"]["title"] = new_title
70	
71	    if paragraph_id is None:
72	        paragraph_id = str(random.randint(0,1000))
73	
74	    new_doc['fields']['path'] = new_doc['fields']['path'] + "#" + paragraph_id
75	    new_doc['put'] = new_doc['put'] + "-" + urllib.parse.quote(paragraph_id)
76	    
77	    return new_doc
78	
79	
80	def split_text(soup):
81	    split_tables(soup)
82	    split_lists(soup)
83	    md = markdownify(str(soup), heading_style='ATX', code_language_callback=what_language, strip=['img'])
84	    lines = md.split("\n")
85	    header = ""
86	    text = ""
87	    id = ""
88	    data = []
89	    for line in lines:
90	        if line.startswith("#"):
91	            if text:
92	                data.append((id, header, text))
93	                text = ""
94	            header = line.lstrip("#")
95	            id = "-".join(header.split()).lower()
96	        else:
97	            text = text + "\n" + line
98	
99	    data.append((id, header, text)) #Flush any last data
100	    return data
101	
102	
103	def remove_notext_tags(soup):
104	    for remove_tag in soup.find_all(['style']):
105	        remove_tag.decompose()
106	
107	
108	def split_lists(soup):
109	    for list in soup.body.find_all(['ul', 'ol']):
110	        for list_item in list.find_all('li'):
111	            move_linkable_item_to_single_entity(soup, list_item)
112	
113	
114	def split_tables(soup):
115	    top_level_tables = soup.body.find_all('table', recursive=False)  # i.e., do not find rows in tables within tables
116	    for table in top_level_tables:
117	        tbody = table.find('tbody')  # tbody is implicit and always there
118	        for row in tbody.find_all('tr', recursive=False):
119	            move_linkable_item_to_single_entity(soup, row)
120	
121	
122	def table_header_row(row):
123	    thead = row.find_parent('table').find('thead')
124	    if thead is not None:
125	        return thead.find('tr')
126	    return None
127	
128	
129	def move_linkable_item_to_single_entity(soup, item):
130	    id_elem = item.find('p', {'id': True})
131	    if id_elem is not None:
132	        new_h4 = soup.new_tag('h4', id=id_elem['id'])
133	        new_h4.string = id_elem['id']
134	        if item.name == 'tr':
135	            header_row = table_header_row(item)
136	            new_container = soup.new_tag('table')
137	            if header_row is not None:
138	                new_container.insert(0, copy.copy(header_row))
139	        else:
140	            new_container = soup.new_tag(item.parent.name)  # ul or ol
141	
142	        new_container.append(item)
143	        soup.append(new_h4)
144	        soup.append(new_container)
145	
146	
147	def main():
148	    with open(sys.argv[1]) as fp:
149	        random.seed(42)
150	        docs = json.load(fp)
151	        operations = []
152	        for doc in docs:
153	            html_doc = doc['fields']['html']
154	            html_doc = xml_fixup(html_doc)
155	            soup = BeautifulSoup(html_doc, 'html5lib')
156	            remove_notext_tags(soup)
157	            data = split_text(soup)
158	
159	            for paragraph_id, header, paragraph in data:
160	
161	                paragraph = paragraph.lstrip('\n').lstrip(" ")
162	                paragraph = paragraph.rstrip('\n')
163	
164	                paragraph = re.sub(r"\n{2,}", "\n\n", paragraph)
165	
166	                paragraph = re.sub(r"\n*```", "\n```", paragraph)
167	                paragraph = re.sub(r"```\n*", "```\n", paragraph)
168	
169	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\njson","```json")
170	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nxml","```xml")
171	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nbash","```bash")
172	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nsh","```sh")
173	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nraw","```\n")
174	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\njava","```java\n")
175	
176	                paragraph = remove_jekyll(paragraph)
177	
178	                if paragraph:
179	                    paragraph_doc = create_text_doc(doc, paragraph, paragraph_id, header)
180	                    operations.append(paragraph_doc)
181	
182	    #Merge question expansion
183	    questions_expansion = dict()
184	    with open(sys.argv[3]) as fp:
185	        for line in fp:
186	            op = json.loads(line)
187	            id = op['update']
188	            fields = op['fields']
189	            if "questions" in fields:
190	                questions = fields['questions']['assign']
191	                questions_expansion[id] = questions
192	    for op in operations:
193	        id = op['put']
194	        if id in questions_expansion:
195	            op['fields']['questions'] = questions_expansion[id]
196	        else: 
197	            op['fields']['questions'] = [op['fields']['title']]
198	    with open("paragraph_index.json", "w") as fp:

56	    options = []
57	    options.append("wantedDocumentCount=500")
58	    options.append("timeout=60s")
59	    if continuation is not None and len(continuation) > 0:

105	        documents = find(json, "documents")
106	        if documents is not None:
107	            ids = [ find(document, "id") for document in documents ]
108	            for id in ids:
109	                # The document id might contain chars that needs to be escaped for the delete/put operation to work
110	                # also for comparison with what is in the feed
111	                docid = get_document_id(id) # return the last part
112	                encoded = urllib.parse.quote(docid) #escape
113	                id = id.replace(docid, encoded)
114	                docids.add(id)
115	        continuation = find(json, "continuation")
116	    return docids
117	
118	
119	def get_feed_docids(feed, namespace, doc_type):
120	    with open(feed, "r", encoding='utf-8') as f:
121	        feed_json = json.load(f)
122	    if doc_type == "doc":
123	        return set(["id:{0}:doc::".format(namespace) + find(doc, "fields.namespace") + find(doc, "fields.path") for doc in feed_json])
124	    elif doc_type == "term":
125	        return set(["id:{0}:term::".format(namespace) + str(find(doc, "fields.hash")) for doc in feed_json])
126	    elif doc_type == "paragraph":
127	        return set([doc['put'] for doc in feed_json])
128	
129	
130	def print_header(msg):
131	    print("")
132	    print("*" * 80)
133	    print("* {0}".format(msg))
134	    print("*" * 80)
135	
136	
137	def read_config(config_file):
138	    with open(config_file, "r") as f:
139	        return yaml.safe_load(f)
140	
141	
142	def update_endpoint(endpoint, config):
143	    do_remove_index = config["search"]["do_index_removal_before_feed"]
144	    do_feed = config["search"]["do_feed"]
145	    namespace = config["search"]["namespace"]
146	    doc_type = config["search"]["doc_type"]
147	
148	    endpoint_url = endpoint["url"]
149	    endpoint_url = endpoint_url[:-1] if endpoint_url.endswith("/") else endpoint_url
150	    endpoint_indexes = endpoint["indexes"]
151	
152	    print_header("Retrieving already indexed document ids for endpoint {0}".format(endpoint_url))
153	    docids_in_index = get_indexed_docids(endpoint_url, namespace, doc_type)
154	    print("{0} documents found.".format(len(docids_in_index)))
155	
156	    if do_remove_index:
157	        print_header("Removing all indexed documents in {0}".format(endpoint_url))
158	        vespa_remove(endpoint_url, docids_in_index, namespace, doc_type)
159	        print("{0} documents removed.".format(len(docids_in_index)))
160	
161	    if do_feed:
162	        docids_in_feed = set()
163	        print_header("Parsing feed file(s) for document ids")
164	        for index in endpoint_indexes:
165	            assert os.path.exists(index)
166	            docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(get_feed_docids(index, namespace, doc_type))
167	        print("{0} documents found.".format(len(docids_in_feed)))
168	
169	        if len(docids_in_feed) == 0:
170	            return
171	
172	        docids_to_remove = docids_in_index.difference(docids_in_feed)
173	        if len(docids_to_remove) > 0:
174	            print_header("Removing indexed documents not in feed in {0}".format(endpoint_url))
175	            for id in docids_to_remove:
176	                print("To Remove: {0}".format(id))
177	            vespa_remove(endpoint_url, docids_to_remove, namespace, doc_type)
178	            print("{0} documents removed.".format(len(docids_to_remove)))
179	        else:
180	            print("No documents to be removed.")
181	
182	        for index in endpoint_indexes:
183	            print_header("Feeding {0} to {1}...".format(index, endpoint_url))
184	            print(vespa_feed(endpoint_url, index, namespace, doc_type))
185	
186	        print("{0} documents fed.".format(len(docids_in_feed)))
187	
188	
189	def main():
190	    configuration_file = sys.argv[1]
191	    config = read_config(configuration_file)
192	    global session
193	    session = requests.Session()
194	    retries = Retry(total=10, connect=10,
195	        backoff_factor=0.8,
196	        status_forcelist=[ 500, 503, 504, 429 ]
197	    )
198	    session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
199	    session.cert = (get_public_cert_path(), get_private_key_path())
200	    for endpoint in config["search"]["feed_endpoints"]:
201	        update_endpoint(endpoint, config)
202	
203	
204	if __name__ == "__main__":
205	    main()

1	"""Helper: emit the JSON body to send to /search/ for each rank profile.
2	
3	Four modes:
4	
5	  --cosine      For the `cosine_baseline` rank profile. Sends only the query
6	                text - Vespa runs the passage embedder server-side via embed()
7	                to produce the query vector.
8	
9	  --rerank      For the `hypencoder_rerank` rank profile. Sends the query text
10	                (server-side embed() for the cosine first phase) AND the
11	                tokenized query (for the ONNX q-net second phase).
12	
13	  --lexical     For the `hypencoder_lexical_rerank` rank profile. BM25
14	                first-phase against the text field, hypencoder q-net on the
15	                top candidates. Sends `userQuery()` + tokenized query; no
16	                vector.
17	
18	  default       For the `hypencoder_onnx` rank profile (rank-all). Sends only
19	                token IDs + attention mask. ~830 byte payload.
20	
21	All modes are designed to be piped into `vespa query --file`:
22	
23	    python encode_query.py "tallest mountain in the world" > q.json
24	    vespa query --file q.json
25	"""
26	import argparse
27	import json
28	import sys
29	
30	import numpy as np
31	from tokenizers import Tokenizer
32	
33	MAX_SEQ = 64
34	PAD_TOKEN = "[PAD]"
35	
36	
37	def main() -> None:
38	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
39	    ap.add_argument("query", help="The query text.")
40	    ap.add_argument("--tokenizer", default="app/models/tokenizer.json",
41	                    help="Path to tokenizer.json (downloaded alongside the ONNX models).")
42	    mode = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
43	    mode.add_argument("--rerank", action="store_true",
44	                      help="Emit a body for hypencoder_rerank.")
45	    mode.add_argument("--cosine", action="store_true",
46	                      help="Emit a body for cosine_baseline.")
47	    mode.add_argument("--lexical", action="store_true",
48	                      help="Emit a body for hypencoder_lexical_rerank.")
49	    ap.add_argument("--hits", type=int, default=10)
50	    args = ap.parse_args()
51	
52	    body = {
53	        "yql": "select id, text from doc where true",
54	        "hits": args.hits,
55	        "timeout": "30s",
56	    }
57	
58	    if args.cosine:
59	        body["ranking.profile"] = "cosine_baseline"
60	        body["input.query(q_vec)"] = "embed(passage_embedder, @q)"
61	        body["q"] = args.query
62	    else:
63	        tok = Tokenizer.from_file(args.tokenizer)
64	        pad_id = tok.token_to_id(PAD_TOKEN)
65	        if pad_id is None:
66	            sys.exit(f"{args.tokenizer}: no {PAD_TOKEN} token in the vocabulary")
67	        tok.enable_truncation(max_length=MAX_SEQ)
68	        tok.enable_padding(length=MAX_SEQ, pad_id=pad_id, pad_token=PAD_TOKEN)
69	        enc = tok.encode(args.query)
70	        body["input.query(input_ids)"] = [np.array(enc.ids, dtype=np.float32).tolist()]
71	        body["input.query(attention_mask)"] = [
72	            np.array(enc.attention_mask, dtype=np.float32).tolist()]
73	        if args.rerank:
74	            body["ranking.profile"] = "hypencoder_rerank"
75	            body["input.query(q_vec)"] = "embed(passage_embedder, @q)"
76	            body["q"] = args.query
77	        elif args.lexical:
78	            body["yql"] = ('select id, text from doc where '
79	                           '{grammar: "weakAnd", defaultIndex: "text"}userInput(@q)')
80	            body["q"] = args.query
81	            body["ranking.profile"] = "hypencoder_lexical_rerank"
82	        else:
83	            body["ranking.profile"] = "hypencoder_onnx"
84	
85	    json.dump(body, sys.stdout)
86	
87	
88	if __name__ == "__main__":
89	    main()

1	#! /usr/bin/env python3
2	
3	import re
4	import os
5	import csv
6	import gzip
7	
8	
9	download_dir = os.path.join("ext", "download")
10	query_file = os.path.join("ext", "queries.tsv")
11	docs_file = os.path.join("ext", "docs.tsv")
12	offset_file = os.path.join("ext", "docs-offset.tsv")
13	
14	# if data is not downloaded - use sample data
15	if not os.path.isdir(download_dir):
16	    download_dir = os.path.join("ext", "sample")
17	
18	
19	# The query string for each queryid is querystring[queryid]
20	def load_msmarco_queries(qrel):
21	    print("Loading queries...")
22	    queries = {}
23	    with gzip.open(os.path.join(download_dir, "msmarco-doctrain-queries.tsv.gz"), "rt", encoding="utf8", ) as f:
24	        tsvreader = csv.reader(f, delimiter="\t")
25	        for [queryid, query] in tsvreader:
26	            query = re.sub(r"[^\w ]", " ", query).lower()
27	            queries[queryid] = query
28	    return queries
29	
30	
31	# In the corpus tsv, each docid occurs at offset docoffset[docid]
32	def load_msmarco_document_lookup_table():
33	    print("Loading document lookup table...")
34	    docoffset = {}
35	    with gzip.open(os.path.join(download_dir, "msmarco-docs-lookup.tsv.gz"), "rt", encoding="utf8" ) as f:
36	        tsvreader = csv.reader(f, delimiter="\t")
37	        for [docid, _, offset] in tsvreader:
38	            docoffset[docid] = int(offset)
39	    return docoffset
40	
41	
42	# For each queryid, the list of positive docids is qrel[queryid]
43	def load_msmarco_qrels():
44	    print("Loading query relevance judgements...")
45	    qrel = {}
46	    with gzip.open(os.path.join(download_dir, "msmarco-doctrain-qrels.tsv.gz"), "rt", encoding="utf8") as f:
47	        tsvreader = csv.reader(f, delimiter="\t")
48	        for row in tsvreader:
49	            if len(row) == 4:
50	                [queryid, _, docid, rel] = row
51	            elif len(row) == 1:
52	                [queryid, _, docid, rel] = row[0].split(' ')
53	            assert rel == "1"
54	            if queryid in qrel:
55	                qrel[queryid].add(docid)
56	            else:
57	                qrel[queryid] = set([docid])
58	    return qrel
59	
60	
61	def getcontent(docid, f, docoffset):
62	    try:
63	        f.seek(docoffset[docid])
64	        line = f.readline()
65	        line = line.rstrip()
66	        [found_docid, url, title, body] = line.split("\t")
67	        assert docid == found_docid, f"Looking for {docid}, found {found_docid}"
68	        title = re.sub(r"(?<=[a-z\.])(?=[A-Z])", " ", title )  # Fix "corrosion resistanceInstall with" etc
69	        title = re.sub(r"\W", " ", title)  # Remove whitespace
70	        body = re.sub(r"(?<=[a-z\.])(?=[A-Z])", " ", body)
71	        body = re.sub(r"\W", " ", body)
72	        return "{0}\t{1}\t{2}\t{3}\n".format(docid, url, title, body)
73	    except Exception as e:
74	        pass
75	    return ""
76	
77	
78	# TODO: speed up, takes about an hour...
79	def extract_documents(docoffset):
80	    print("Extracting {0} documents...".format(len(docoffset.keys())))
81	    with open(os.path.join(download_dir, "msmarco-docs.tsv"), encoding="utf8" ) as f, \
82	         open(docs_file, "w", encoding="utf8") as out, \
83	         open(offset_file, "w", encoding="utf8") as offset:
84	        for docid in docoffset.keys():
85	            offset.write("{0}\t{1}\n".format(docid, out.tell()))
86	            out.write(getcontent(docid, f, docoffset))
87	
88	
89	def extract_queries(qrel, query_strings, docoffset):
90	    print("Extracting {0} queries...".format(len(qrel)))
91	    with open(query_file, "w", encoding="utf8") as out:
92	        for qid in qrel.keys():
93	            relevant_documents = ",".join( [docid for docid in qrel[qid] if docid in docoffset] )
94	            out.write("{0}\t{1}\n".format(query_strings[qid], relevant_documents))
95	
96	
97	def main():
98	    query_relevance = load_msmarco_qrels()
99	    query_strings = load_msmarco_queries(query_relevance)
100	    document_offset = load_msmarco_document_lookup_table()
101	
102	    extract_documents(document_offset)
103	    extract_queries(query_relevance, query_strings, document_offset)
104	
105	
106	if __name__ == "__main__":
107	    main()

1	"""Export the passage encoder and the query encoder of a Hypencoder checkpoint
2	to ONNX, and save the tokenizer. Optionally INT8-quantize the query encoder
3	for ~3x faster CPU inference via ONNX Runtime's MLAS kernels.
4	
5	Usage:
6	    python model2onnx.py --checkpoint jfkback/hypencoder.2_layer
7	    python model2onnx.py --checkpoint jfkback/hypencoder.2_layer --quantize-int8
8	
9	Outputs (under ./app/models/, where services.xml references them):
10	    passage_encoder.onnx       Inlined-weight ONNX of the BERT-base passage encoder.
11	    query_encoder.onnx         Inlined-weight ONNX of the query encoder (BERT + hyperhead),
12	                               with multi-output (W0, b0, W1, b1, Wout) for the 2-layer q-net.
13	    tokenizer.json             HuggingFace fast-tokenizer JSON, used by both encoders.
14	
15	The query encoder's wrapper performs a few important transforms so the rank
16	profile in schemas/doc.sd doesn't have to:
17	    * Casts float input_ids/attention_mask to int64 internally (Vespa cell
18	      types don't include int64, so we ship them as floats).
19	    * Pre-transposes weight matrices to (out, in) to match Vespa's
20	      alphabetical tensor-dimension ordering (the rank profile reads
21	      onnx(query_encoder).W0 as (d0=h, d1=x) - the in/out we want).
22	    * Uses static layer-norm shapes inside `_get_weights_and_biases` so the
23	      legacy TorchScript exporter inlines weights into a single .onnx file
24	      (Vespa filedistribution doesn't track external .data sidecars).
25	"""
26	import argparse
27	import shutil
28	from pathlib import Path
29	
30	import numpy as np
31	import torch
32	import torch.nn.functional as F
33	from transformers import AutoTokenizer
34	
35	from hypencoder_cb.modeling.hypencoder import (
36	    HypencoderDualEncoder,
37	    scaled_dot_product_attention,
38	)
39	
40	OUT_DIR = Path("app/models")
41	
42	
43	# ============================================================================
44	# Passage encoder export (just BERT base; CLS pooling done by Vespa's HF embedder)
45	# ============================================================================
46	class PassageEncoderWrapper(torch.nn.Module):
47	    def __init__(self, m):
48	        super().__init__()
49	        self.m = m
50	
51	    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask):
52	        return self.m(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask).last_hidden_state
53	
54	
55	def export_passage_encoder(dual: HypencoderDualEncoder, out_path: Path) -> None:
56	    print(f"Exporting passage encoder to {out_path} ...")
57	    wrapped = PassageEncoderWrapper(dual.passage_encoder.transformer).eval()
58	    dummy_ids = torch.tensor([[101, 2023, 2003, 1037, 3231, 102]], dtype=torch.long)
59	    dummy_mask = torch.ones_like(dummy_ids)
60	    sidecar = out_path.with_suffix(out_path.suffix + ".data")
61	    if sidecar.exists():
62	        sidecar.unlink()
63	    torch.onnx.export(
64	        wrapped,
65	        (dummy_ids, dummy_mask),
66	        out_path.as_posix(),
67	        input_names=["input_ids", "attention_mask"],
68	        output_names=["last_hidden_state"],
69	        dynamic_axes={
70	            "input_ids": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"},
71	            "attention_mask": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"},
72	            "last_hidden_state": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"},
73	        },
74	        opset_version=14,
75	        do_constant_folding=True,
76	        dynamo=False,
77	    )
78	    if sidecar.exists():
79	        sidecar.unlink()
80	    print(f"  size: {out_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB")
81	
82	
83	# ============================================================================
84	# Query encoder export (BERT + hyperhead, multi-output)
85	# ============================================================================
86	class QueryEncoderWrapper(torch.nn.Module):
87	    """Wraps the Hypencoder query encoder so its forward() returns the q-net
88	    weight tensors (W0, b0, W1, b1, Wout) directly instead of a callable
89	    NoTorchSequential. Internally reimplements `_get_weights_and_biases` with
90	    static layer-norm shapes (so the legacy ONNX exporter inlines weights)
91	    and pre-transposes Ws so the Vespa rank expression doesn't have to.
92	    """
93	
94	    def __init__(self, hyp):
95	        super().__init__()
96	        self.hyp = hyp
97	
98	    def _get_weights_and_biases_static(self, last_hidden_state, attention_mask):
99	        h = self.hyp
100	        batch_size = last_hidden_state.size(0)
101	        keys = [kp(last_hidden_state) for kp in h.key_projections]
102	        values = [vp(last_hidden_state) for vp in h.value_projections]
103	        weights_final, biases_final = [], []
104	        for i in range(len(h.weight_shapes)):
105	            w = scaled_dot_product_attention(
106	                query=h.weight_query_embeddings[i].repeat_interleave(batch_size, dim=0),
107	                key=keys[i], value=values[i],
108	                dim=h.weight_shapes[i][1], mask=attention_mask,
109	            )[0]
110	            w = F.layer_norm(F.relu(w), [h.weight_shapes[i][0]])
111	            w = h.weight_hyper_projection[i](w)
112	            w = (w + h.hyper_base_matrices[i].repeat(batch_size, 1, 1)).transpose(2, 1)
113	            weights_final.append(w)
114	        offset = len(h.weight_shapes)
115	        for i in range(len(h.bias_shapes)):
116	            b = scaled_dot_product_attention(
117	                query=h.bias_query_embeddings[i].repeat_interleave(batch_size, dim=0),
118	                key=keys[i + offset], value=values[i + offset],
119	                dim=h.bias_shapes[i][1], mask=attention_mask,
120	            )[0]
121	            b = F.layer_norm(F.relu(b), [h.bias_shapes[i][0]])
122	            b = h.bias_hyper_projection[i](b)
123	            b = (b + h.hyper_base_vectors[i].repeat(batch_size, 1, 1)).transpose(2, 1)
124	            biases_final.append(b)
125	        return weights_final, biases_final
126	
127	    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask):
128	        # Vespa tensor cells are float/double/bfloat16/int8 (no int64), so
129	        # accept floats and cast.
130	        ids = input_ids.to(torch.long)
131	        mask = attention_mask.to(torch.long)
132	        out = self.hyp.transformer(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=mask)
133	        weights, biases = self._get_weights_and_biases_static(out.last_hidden_state, mask)
134	        # Squeeze batch + transpose Ws to (out, in) so the rank profile gets
135	        # them in the order Vespa stores tensor dims alphabetically (h, x).
136	        # Use explicit indexing rather than .squeeze() so ONNX Squeeze ops
137	        # only reduce dims that are statically size 1.
138	        # Last entry in `weights` is the final Wout (768->1, no bias).
139	        # All earlier entries pair with `biases` for residual blocks.
140	        n_blocks = len(biases)
141	        outs = []
142	        for i in range(n_blocks):
143	            outs.append(weights[i][0].transpose(0, 1).contiguous())  # W_i (out=768, in=768)
144	            outs.append(biases[i][0, :, 0].contiguous())              # b_i (out=768,)
145	        outs.append(weights[-1][0, :, 0].contiguous())                # Wout (in=768,)
146	        return tuple(outs)
147	
148	
149	def export_query_encoder(dual: HypencoderDualEncoder, out_path: Path) -> None:
150	    print(f"Exporting query encoder to {out_path} ...")
151	    wrapped = QueryEncoderWrapper(dual.query_encoder).eval()
152	    n_blocks = len(dual.query_encoder.bias_shapes)
153	    output_names = []
154	    for i in range(n_blocks):
155	        output_names += [f"W{i}", f"b{i}"]
156	    output_names.append("Wout")
157	    print(f"  q-net layers: {n_blocks} residual blocks + 1 final linear -> outputs {output_names}")
158	    dummy_ids = torch.tensor([[101, 2023, 2003, 1037, 3231, 102]], dtype=torch.float32)
159	    dummy_mask = torch.ones_like(dummy_ids)
160	    sidecar = out_path.with_suffix(out_path.suffix + ".data")
161	    if sidecar.exists():
162	        sidecar.unlink()
163	    torch.onnx.export(
164	        wrapped,
165	        (dummy_ids, dummy_mask),
166	        out_path.as_posix(),
167	        input_names=["input_ids", "attention_mask"],
168	        output_names=output_names,
169	        dynamic_axes={
170	            "input_ids": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"},
171	            "attention_mask": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"},
172	        },
173	        opset_version=14,
174	        do_constant_folding=True,
175	        dynamo=False,
176	    )
177	    if sidecar.exists():
178	        sidecar.unlink()
179	    print(f"  size: {out_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB")
180	
181	
182	def quantize_query_encoder_int8(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
183	    """ORT dynamic int8 quantization of the BERT linears. Uses MLAS SMMLA
184	    on aarch64 with i8mm and VNNI on x86; ~3x faster BERT forward in our
185	    measurements with ~1% retrieval-quality drift. Static quantization with
186	    calibration data would do better."""
187	    from onnxruntime.quantization import QuantType, quantize_dynamic
188	    print(f"INT8-quantizing {src} -> {dst} ...")
189	    quantize_dynamic(model_input=src.as_posix(), model_output=dst.as_posix(), weight_type=QuantType.QInt8)
190	    print(f"  size after quant: {dst.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB")
191	
192	
193	def main() -> None:
194	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
195	    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint", default="jfkback/hypencoder.2_layer",
196	                    help="HF model id of a Hypencoder checkpoint (default: jfkback/hypencoder.2_layer).")
197	    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="app/models",
198	                    help="Output directory for the ONNX files and tokenizer (default: ./app/models, "
199	                         "where services.xml expects them).")
200	    ap.add_argument("--quantize-int8", action="store_true",
201	                    help="After exporting, also run ORT dynamic INT8 quantization on the query encoder "
202	                         "and use that as the active query_encoder.onnx.")
203	    args = ap.parse_args()
204	
205	    out_dir = Path(args.out_dir)
206	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
207	
208	    print(f"Loading {args.checkpoint} ...")
209	    dual = HypencoderDualEncoder.from_pretrained(args.checkpoint)
210	    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.checkpoint, use_fast=True)
211	    dual.eval()
212

214	    export_query_encoder(dual, out_dir / "query_encoder.onnx")
215

11	min_relevant_docs_per_query = 1

14	documents_to_generate = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 100000

24	def load_queries():
25	    queries = {}
26	    with io.open(query_file, "r", encoding="utf8") as f:
27	        tsvreader = csv.reader(f, delimiter="\t")
28	        for [query, relevant_documents] in tsvreader:
29	            query = re.sub(r"[^\w ]", " ", query).lower()
30	            queries[len(queries)] = {
31	                "query": query,
32	                "docs": relevant_documents.split(","),
33	            }
34	    return queries
