This is O(unique_terms x num_docs) and builds a list per term. Incrementing `terms[term]["docs"]` once per (doc, term) in the first pass (lines 91-97) is O(total terms). Quadratic in practice. Confidence high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/incremental-search/search-suggestions/count_terms.py::process_docs` line 92 — [kind 1] `total_count = sum([...])` is computed for every document and never used. Confidence high (magnitude small, O(terms)).

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/incremental-search/search-suggestions/count_terms.py::count_terms` lines 55-65 — [kind 2/3] For each window length k, every word of each window is re-tested against `common_words` through `map` plus a lambda, and each window is sliced and joined. Words already tested in smaller windows are retested, so the cost is O(n x L^2) rather than O(n x L). Once a window at start i contains a common word, all longer windows from i do too, so the k-loop can break. The redundancy only matters when `term_length > 1`; with the default of 1 the per-token cost is slice+map+lambda, where `doc[i] in common_words` would suffice. Confidence medium.

Each request also opens a fresh TCP/TLS connection and nothing is batched. Confidence high. Batching through the Vespa feed API or a persistent HTTP session would remove the per-document process and connection cost.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/incremental-search/search-as-you-type/feed_to_vespa.py::vespa_remove` lines 75-80 — [kind 3] Same pattern as above: one `curl -X DELETE` subprocess per document id. Confidence high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/incremental-search/search-as-you-type/feed_to_vespa.py::update_endpoint` lines 139-142 and 155-161 — [kind 1] When both `do_remove_index` and `do_feed` are set, all indexed docs are deleted (lines 139-141). Then `docids_to_remove` (line 155), which is a subset of the same stale `docids_in_index`, is deleted again (line 160). Those DELETEs are redundant because the ids are already gone. The full delete is also unnecessary before a feed, since puts overwrite. Confidence medium-high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/incremental-search/search-as-you-type/feed_to_vespa.py::update_endpoint` line 149 with `vespa_feed` line 84 — [kind 2] Each feed file is read and JSON-parsed twice: once in `get_feed_docids` for the id set and again in `get_docs` for feeding. Also line 149 `docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(...)` copies the accumulated set on every index; `update()` would not. Confidence medium (magnitude depends on feed size).

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/collect_training_data.py::build_dataset` lines 98-99 — [kind 1/2] The `with open(PROCESSED_QUERIES_FILE, "a")` block sits at the loop level (8 spaces), outside the `if` on line 75. So every query is re-opened and appended to the processed file on every run, including queries already processed. The file grows by the full query count each run, and the next run loads all those lines into `processed_queries`. Confidence high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/collect_training_data.py::build_dataset` line 75 with `load_processed_queries` lines 60-67 — [kind 3] `int(qid) not in processed_queries` is a membership test on a list, O(P) per query, so O(Q x P) overall. A set would be O(1). It only costs on a resumed run, where P is nonzero, and the duplicate lines from the bug above make P grow. Confidence high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/collect_training_data.py::get_features` line 38 — [kind 3] `requests.post(url, json=body)` uses no `requests.Session`, so every request opens a new TCP connection. Two requests per query are made serially (lines 79-87), so about 2 connection setups per query. Confidence medium-high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/collect_training_data.py::build_dataset` lines 92-97 — [kind 3] Per query: a DataFrame is built, `os.path.isfile` is stat-ed, and `to_csv` opens and closes the output in append mode. Batching rows and writing periodically would avoid this. Confidence medium.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-video-search/src/python/embedding.py::compute_and_send_video_embeddings` lines 145-164 — [kind 2] The loop is over CLIP model names, and for each model a new DataLoader re-runs `extract_images` (full ffmpeg decode of every video, lines 39-52) plus the PIL conversion for every video. Video decoding is repeated once per model. Decode once and run all models on the same frames. Confidence high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-video-search/src/python/embedding.py::VideoFeedDataset.__getitem__` lines 98-99 with `_from_image_to_vector` lines 74-86 — [kind 3] Each frame is passed through `preprocess` and `encode_image` one at a time (batch size 1, a new `torch.no_grad()` each time). Stacking the frames of a video (or the batch of videos) into one forward pass is the obvious batching. Confidence medium-high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-video-search/src/python/embedding.py::extract_images` lines 39-52 with `sample_images` lines 23-36 — [kind 3] Every decoded frame is appended to a Python list, and `np.array(images)` (line 34) then copies all frames into one array before fancy-indexing `number_frames` of them. Selecting indices first would avoid the copy and retention of unused frames. Low, because UCF-style clips are short.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-video-search/src/python/embedding.py::send_video_embeddings` lines 114-128 — [kind 1] `@retry` re-sends the whole batch if any document fails. Successful documents are re-POSTed. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-video-search/src/python/app.py::get_predefined_queries` lines 33-36, called on lines 43-44 — [kind 2] Streamlit re-runs the script on every widget interaction, so this issues an uncached remote HTTP GET each time while the checkbox is on. `st.cache` (already used on line 23) would make it once per process. Confidence medium.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-video-search/src/python/app.py` lines 17-20 — [kind 2] `Vespa(...)` is constructed at module level and so is rebuilt on every rerun. Probably cheap. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/extract-msmarco.py::extract_documents` lines 84-86 and 78 (TODO) — [kind 1] Writes the entire lookup corpus (~3.2M documents, the author notes about an hour). `sample-queries-and-documents.py` only consumes the qrels documents plus `documents_to_generate` (default 100000) random ones. Extracting only those would cut most of the work. Confidence medium (depends on whether the full docs.tsv is used elsewhere).

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/extract-msmarco.py::extract_documents` line 85 — [kind 3] `out.tell()` on a text-mode file flushes the write buffer, so each document causes one write syscall. Tracking a running byte count would avoid it. Confidence medium-high.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/extract-msmarco.py::load_msmarco_queries` lines 20, 26-27 — [kind 1] The `qrel` parameter is unused, so every query in the file is normalised, though only queries in `qrel` are written. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/sample-queries-and-documents.py::load_queries` line 29 — [kind 1] Re-applies the same `re.sub` normalisation that `extract-msmarco.py` already applied to the file. Idempotent, so wasted per query. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/convert-to-vespa-format.py::main` lines 43-45 — [kind 3] Random seek plus `readline` per document in offset-dict order. Each seek discards the buffered-reader block, and each read pulls a fresh block. Sorting by offset once gives monotonic reads. Confidence low. Also line 62, `json.dump` streams many small writes; `json.dumps` plus one write is typically faster. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/text-search/python/create-sample-data.py` lines 36-38 — [kind 3] `readlines()` materialises the whole lookup file, then the dict comprehension splits each line twice. One split would do. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/scaling-tutorial/ext/transform_ms_marco.py::<module>` lines 28-33 — [kind 1] Every line is checked against all five subset limits, and the four truncated subsets are written in parallel with the full file. These are prefixes of the full output and could be derived from it with a cheap head. Extra writes are about 556k documents (roughly 6% of the full output). The loop also continues over all subsets after line 500000. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/use-case-shopping/convert_meta.py::main` line 67 and `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/use-case-shopping/convert_reviews.py::main` line 58 — [kind 3] `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` builds the whole output as one pretty-printed string, which inflates bytes written and then re-parsed by the feed. Also `sys.stdin.readlines()` (convert_meta line 57, convert_reviews line 46) materialises all input. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/multilingual-search/ext/evaluate.py::search` lines 12-13 — [kind 3] `query_group.iterrows()` is used just to read one value, and only the last row survives. `query_group['query'].iloc[0]` would do. The same function is also driven by `groupby(...).apply` (line 75), which builds a sub-DataFrame per group. Confidence low (one row per group in practice).

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/multilingual-search/ext/evaluate.py::main` line 75 with `search` line 24 — [kind 3, wall-clock] Requests run serially, one blocking HTTP round-trip per query. The sibling `msmarco-ranking/python/evaluate_passage_run.py` uses a 16-thread pool. Idle waiting keeps the machine busy for longer. Confidence low-medium.

NOTHING-FOUND-NOTES:
- `embedding.py` lines 96 (ToPILImage) and 98-99: array to PIL to tensor is needed because CLIP's `preprocess` is PIL-based. Not a removable round-trip.
- `embedding.py` line 100 `ntpath.basename` and line 103 split inside the frame loop: a few frames per video, negligible.
- `embedding.py` `TextProcessor.__init__`: loads the full CLIP model including the unused visual tower. One-time, cached by `st.cache` in app.py, and the clip API has no text-only load. Not per-call waste.
- `embedding.py` `extract_images`: ffmpeg decodes all source frames even with `fps=1`. Decoding is needed to get frames at all, and clips are short. Only the retention issue is flagged above.
- `embedding.py` `VideoSearchApp.__init__` line 310 creates a `ValueError` without raising it. Correctness bug, not energy.
- `count_terms.py` `write_json_file` line 27: `re.sub(r" ", ...)` per term. Module re cache avoids recompilation; cost is trivial next to the rest.
- `count_terms.py` `get_phrases`: quadratic string slicing, but per term with few words.
- `count_terms.py` `process_doc` lines 76-79: list concatenation and double `.get` per term. Constant factor only.
- `accepted_words.py` (all): single linear passes with set operations. Nothing significant.
- `dump_passage_dev_qrels.py`, `to-vespa-feed.py`: already streaming, one item at a time.
- `evaluate_passage_run.py`: already uses a shared `requests.Session` and a 16-thread pool. Per-query `formatted_params` build is trivial.
- `convert_meta.py` `eval(line)`: input is Python-repr, not JSON, so `json` cannot replace it. `ast.literal_eval` has similar parse cost.
- `convert_meta.py` `categories_text +=` and `convert_reviews.py` string building: per-document category counts are tiny.
- `create_suggestions.py` `filter` iterates 27 substring checks per call: small constant per title.
- `create_suggestions.py` lines 113-117 double dict lookup and line 121 dead `suggest = []`: trivial.
- `create-sample-data.py` line 48 `out.tell()` per document: only 1000 documents (constant sample size).
- `create-sample-data.py` line 42 `random.sample` over `dict_keys`: Python 3.11+ raises TypeError on a non-Sequence. That is a correctness problem; on older versions the population is converted per call but the loop normally runs once. Also line 27 keeps only one qrel per query (correctness).
- `sample-queries-and-documents.py` `select_documents` line 61 `min()` per iteration, and line 60 copying offset keys to a list: negligible; the list is needed for `random.choice`.
- `feed_to_vespa.py` recursive `find` and per-id `print` in `get_indexed_docids` line 103 and `vespa_remove` line 79: low-value I/O, flagged only as minor.
- `collect_training_data.py` line 17-19 `annotate_data` three `update()` calls per hit: negligible.
- `collect_training_data.py` imports `from msmarco import ...`, which is not in this repo and was not read. The cost of its loaders is unverified.

Round-trips scale with the number of stale docs; the shared `session` already reuses the connection, so the cost is per-request overhead plus JSON parsing. Batching would need the feed/removal path to switch to a bulk mechanism. Confidence medium.
- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/feed_to_vespa.py::update_endpoint` lines 164-166 — [kind 2] Every feed file is re-read and re-JSON-parsed (`get_feed_docids`) once per endpoint in `feed_endpoints`. With multiple endpoints sharing the same index files, the same large JSON is parsed N times. The parsed docid sets could be computed once and reused. - `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/feed_to_vespa.py::update_endpoint` line 166 — [kind 3] `docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(...)` builds a new set on each iteration instead of `update()`. Negligible for few files. Confidence low.

- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/feed-split.py::split_text` line 97 — [kind 3] `text = text + "\n" + line` copies the accumulated section text on every line. The first `+` takes a non-in-place copy because the left operand is the local still referenced by the variable, so each line copies the whole section, giving O(lines × section size). Fix: collect lines in a list and `"\n".join`. Confidence medium-high.
- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/feed-split.py::split_tables` / `table_header_row` lines 115-126, 135 — [kind 2] `table_header_row` does `row.find_parent('table').find('thead')` for every row. For tables without a `<thead>`, `find('thead')` scans the whole table on each row, giving O(rows × table size) per table. The header lookup is the same for every row of a table and could be computed once per table. Confidence medium; magnitude depends on table size.
- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/feed-split.py::xml_fixup` lines 36-41 — [kind 1/3] For every matched block, `text.replace(match, escaped_match)` scans the whole document. Duplicate blocks are processed repeatedly, and when `escape()` leaves a block unchanged the replace is a full scan that does nothing. Confidence low (xml blocks almost always contain `<`, so the no-op case is rare).
- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/feed-split.py::main` line 155 — [kind 3] `BeautifulSoup(html_doc, 'html5lib')` is a slow pure-Python parser; `lxml` is typically much faster. Changing it may alter the tree for malformed HTML and therefore the output. Confidence low (a semantic risk, not a clear waste).
- `/home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps/reverse-image-search/script/feed.py::run` lines 152-153 — [kind 2] The JPEG was just encoded in `_save_image` from an in-memory PIL image, then re-read via `abs_path.read_bytes()` (line 152) and fully re-decoded via `Image.open(abs_path).convert("RGB")` (line 153) only to produce the embedding input. The in-memory image could be used directly, avoiding one JPEG decode and one file read per image. Caveat: the embedding would then be computed on the pre-quantized image instead of the q=88 JPEG, a small change in vectors. Confidence high on the redundancy, medium on whether the change is acceptable.

Moving the path/exists check before `ex["image"]` avoids that. Confidence medium (I could not verify datasets' decode-on-access behaviour; pyvespa and datasets are not installed in this environment).

Each call presumably sets up a fresh worker pool and connections, and the embedding (GPU/CPU) and HTTP feed run serially with no overlap. Hoisting the feed call so one `feed_iterable` consumes a generator across all batches, or pipelining embedding with feeding, would reduce per-batch setup and idle time. The patterns are cached by `re`, so the cost is keys × blocks × text length scans. Could be combined into one alternation, but the cost is small. Confidence low.

- `reverse-image-search/script/feed.py`: `full_image` base64 is NOT waste. `reverse-image-search/app/schemas/image.sd` (lines 37-38, 197-205) defines `full_image` as a summary field, and `with-image` summary returns it; `visual-retrieval-colpali` and the backend read it. The `id-only` summary used by search.py does not fetch it, which is expected.
- `feed.py::run` model and processor load (lines 105-106) and Vespa app creation (line 112): once per run, not per batch.
- `feed.py::_iter_split` and `_batched`: streaming with batching, correct.
- `feed.py::run` `torch.inference_mode()` batched processor and model call: already batched.
- `feed.py::_save_image` `mkdir(exist_ok=True)` per image: one syscall, negligible.

8	def create_conditions(conditions_list):
9	    """Convert an array of condition strings into Vespa QueryBuilder conditions."""
10	
11	    # Define supported operators
12	    operators = {
13	        ">": lambda f, v: f > v,
14	        "<": lambda f, v: f < v,
15	        "=": lambda f, v: f == v,
16	        "!=": lambda f, v: f != v,
17	        ">=": lambda f, v: f >= v,
18	        "<=": lambda f, v: f <= v,
19	        "contains": lambda f, v: f.contains(v),  # Special case for text search
20	    }
21	
22	    parsed_conditions = []
23	
24	    for condition_str in conditions_list:
25	        parts = condition_str.split(
26	            " ", 2
27	        )  # Split into max 3 parts to handle "contains" operator properly
28	
29	        if len(parts) < 3:
30	            raise ValueError(
31	                f"Invalid condition format: '{condition_str}'. Expected format: 'field operator value'"
32	            )
33	
34	        field, operator, value = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2]
35	
36	        # Convert numeric values if applicable
37	        try:
38	            value = float(value) if "." in value or value.isdigit() else value
39	        except ValueError:
40	            pass  # Keep as string if conversion fails
41	
42	        # Validate operator
43	        if operator not in operators:
44	            raise ValueError(
45	                f"Unsupported operator: '{operator}' in condition '{condition_str}'"
46	            )
47	
48	        # Create QueryField object and apply operator function
49	        query_field = qf(field)
50	        parsed_conditions.append(operators[operator](query_field, value))
51	
52	    return parsed_conditions  # Returns a list of Condition objects
53	
54	
55	def VespaRetriever(state: SubgraphState):
56	    user_query = state["SearchEngineQuery"]
57	    filters = state["Filters"]
58	    num_hits = 10
59	
60	    print(filters)
61	    columns = ["id", "category", "title", "description", "average_rating", "price"]
62	    schema = "product"
63	
64	    inlistcol = qf("category")
65	    catlist = state["Categories"]
66	
67	    vespa_app = Vespa(url=VESPA_URL, cert=PUBLIC_CERT_PATH, key=PRIVATE_KEY_PATH)
68	
69	    condition_uq = qb.userInput(user_query)
70	
71	    condition_ann = qb.nearestNeighbor(
72	        field="embedding",
73	        query_vector="q_embedding",
74	    )
75	
76	    condition_cat = inlistcol.in_(*catlist)
77	
78	    if filters != ["None"]:
79	        cond_list = create_conditions(filters)
80	        cond_opt = qb.all(*cond_list)
81	
82	        q = (
83	            qb.select(columns)
84	            .from_(schema)
85	            .where((condition_ann | condition_uq) & condition_cat & cond_opt)
86	        )
87	    else:
88	        q = (
89	            qb.select(columns)
90	            .from_(schema)
91	            .where((condition_ann | condition_uq) & condition_cat)
92	        )
93	
94	    print(str(q))
95	    resp = vespa_app.query(
96	        yql=q,
97	        ranking="hybrid",
98	        body={"input.query(q_embedding)": f"embed({user_query})"},
99	        hits=num_hits,
100	    )
101	
102	    # Extract only the 'fields' content from each entry
103	    filtered_data = [hit["fields"] for hit in resp.hits]
104	
105	    state["SearchEngineResults"] = filtered_data
106	    print(state["SearchEngineResults"])

1	import base64
2	import os
3	from io import BytesIO
4	
5	from datasets import load_dataset
6	from dotenv import load_dotenv
7	from vespa.application import Vespa
8	from vespa.io import VespaResponse
9	
10	load_dotenv()
11	
12	VESPA_APP_TOKEN_URL = os.getenv("VESPA_APP_TOKEN_URL")
13	VESPA_CLOUD_SECRET_TOKEN = os.getenv("VESPA_CLOUD_SECRET_TOKEN")
14	
15	ds = load_dataset("vespa-engine/gpfg-QA", split="train", streaming=True)
16	
17	app = Vespa(
18	    url=VESPA_APP_TOKEN_URL,
19	    vespa_cloud_secret_token=VESPA_CLOUD_SECRET_TOKEN,
20	)
21	app.get_application_status()
22	
23	
24	def pil_to_base64(pil_image):
25	    """Convert PIL image to base64 string"""
26	    buffer = BytesIO()
27	    pil_image.save(buffer, format="JPEG")
28	    buffer.seek(0)
29	    image_base64 = base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("utf-8")
30	    return image_base64
31	
32	
33	def process_item_for_vespa(item):
34	    """Convert dataset item to Vespa format with base64 images and proper embedding structure"""
35	    # Convert PIL images to base64
36	    blur_image_b64 = pil_to_base64(item["blur_image"])
37	    full_image_b64 = pil_to_base64(item["full_image"])
38	
39	    # Reconstruct embedding dictionary from separate embedding.X fields
40	    embedding_dict = {}
41	    for key, value in item.items():
42	        if key.startswith("embedding."):
43	            # Extract the number after "embedding."
44	            embedding_index = int(key.split(".")[1])
45	            embedding_dict[embedding_index] = value
46	
47	    # Return Vespa-formatted item
48	    return {
49	        "id": item["id"],
50	        "fields": {
51	            "id": item["id"],
52	            "url": item["url"],
53	            "title": item["title"],
54	            "year": item["year"],
55	            "page_number": item["page_number"],
56	            "blur_image": blur_image_b64,
57	            "full_image": full_image_b64,
58	            "text": item["text"],
59	            "embedding": embedding_dict,
60	            "queries": item["queries"],
61	            "questions": item["questions"],
62	        },
63	    }
64	
65	
66	# Map the dataset to convert to Vespa format
67	vespa_feed = ds.map(process_item_for_vespa)
68	
69

1	import torch
2	from PIL import Image
3	import numpy as np
4	from typing import Generator, Tuple, List, Union, Dict
5	from pathlib import Path
6	import base64
7	from io import BytesIO
8	import re
9	import io
10	import matplotlib.cm as cm
11	
12	from colpali_engine.models import ColPali, ColPaliProcessor
13	from colpali_engine.utils.torch_utils import get_torch_device
14	from colpali_engine.interpretability.similarity_map_utils import normalize_similarity_map
15	from functools import lru_cache
16	import logging
17	
18	
19	class SimMapGenerator:
20	    """
21	    Generates similarity maps based on query embeddings and image patches using the ColPali model.
22	    """
23	
24	    colormap = cm.viridis  # Preload colormap for efficiency
25	
26	    def __init__(
27	        self,
28	        logger: logging.Logger,
29	        model_name: str = "vidore/colpali-v1.2",
30	        n_patch: int = 32,
31	    ):
32	        """
33	        Initializes the SimMapGenerator class with a specified model and patch dimension.
34	
35	        Args:
36	            model_name (str): The model name for loading the ColPali model.
37	            n_patch (int): The number of patches per dimension.
38	        """
39	        self.model_name = model_name
40	        self.n_patch = n_patch
41	        self.device = get_torch_device("auto")
42	        self.logger = logger
43	        self.logger.info(f"Using device: {self.device}")
44	        self.model, self.processor = self.load_model()
45	
46	    def load_model(self) -> Tuple[ColPali, ColPaliProcessor]:
47	        """
48	        Loads the ColPali model and processor.
49	
50	        Returns:
51	            Tuple[ColPali, ColPaliProcessor]: Loaded model and processor.
52	        """
53	        model = ColPali.from_pretrained(
54	            self.model_name,
55	            dtype=torch.bfloat16,  # Note that the embeddings created during feed were float32 -> binarized, yet setting this seem to produce the most similar results both locally (mps) and HF (Cuda)
56	            device_map=self.device,
57	        ).eval()
58	
59	        processor = ColPaliProcessor.from_pretrained(self.model_name)
60	        return model, processor
61	
62	    def gen_similarity_maps(
63	        self,
64	        query: str,
65	        query_embs: torch.Tensor,
66	        token_idx_map: Dict[int, str],
67	        images: List[Union[Path, str]],
68	        vespa_sim_maps: List[Dict],
69	    ) -> Generator[Tuple[int, str, str], None, None]:
70	        """
71	        Generates similarity maps for the provided images and query, and returns base64-encoded blended images.
72	
73	        Args:
74	            query (str): The query string.
75	            query_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings tensor.
76	            token_idx_map (dict): Mapping from indices to tokens.
77	            images (List[Union[Path, str]]): List of image paths or base64-encoded strings.
78	            vespa_sim_maps (List[Dict]): List of Vespa similarity maps.
79	
80	        Yields:
81	            Tuple[int, str, str]: A tuple containing the image index, selected token, and base64-encoded image.
82	        """
83	        processed_images, original_images, original_sizes = [], [], []
84	        for img in images:
85	            img_pil = self._load_image(img)
86	            original_images.append(img_pil.copy())
87	            original_sizes.append(img_pil.size)
88	            processed_images.append(img_pil)
89	
90	        vespa_sim_map_tensor = self._prepare_similarity_map_tensor(
91	            query_embs, vespa_sim_maps
92	        )
93	        similarity_map_normalized = normalize_similarity_map(
94	            vespa_sim_map_tensor.flatten(0, 1)
95	        ).reshape(vespa_sim_map_tensor.shape)
96	
97	        for idx, img in enumerate(original_images):
98	            for token_idx, token in token_idx_map.items():
99	                if self.should_filter_token(token):
100	                    continue
101	
102	                sim_map = similarity_map_normalized[idx, token_idx, :, :]
103	                blended_img_base64 = self._blend_image(
104	                    img, sim_map, original_sizes[idx]
105	                )
106	                yield idx, token, token_idx, blended_img_base64
107	
108	    def _load_image(self, img: Union[Path, str]) -> Image:
109	        """
110	        Loads an image from a file path or a base64-encoded string.
111	
112	        Args:
113	            img (Union[Path, str]): The image to load.
114	
115	        Returns:
116	            Image: The loaded PIL image.
117	        """
118	        try:
119	            if isinstance(img, Path):
120	                return Image.open(img).convert("RGB")
121	            elif isinstance(img, str):
122	                return Image.open(BytesIO(base64.b64decode(img))).convert("RGB")
123	        except Exception as e:
124	            raise ValueError(f"Failed to load image: {e}")
125	
126	    def _prepare_similarity_map_tensor(
127	        self, query_embs: torch.Tensor, vespa_sim_maps: List[Dict]
128	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
129	        """
130	        Prepares a similarity map tensor from Vespa similarity maps.
131	
132	        Args:
133	            query_embs (torch.Tensor): Query embeddings tensor.
134	            vespa_sim_maps (List[Dict]): List of Vespa similarity maps.
135	
136	        Returns:
137	            torch.Tensor: The prepared similarity map tensor.
138	        """
139	        vespa_sim_map_tensor = torch.zeros(
140	            (len(vespa_sim_maps), query_embs.size(0), self.n_patch, self.n_patch)
141	        )
142	        for idx, vespa_sim_map in enumerate(vespa_sim_maps):
143	            for cell in vespa_sim_map["quantized"]["cells"]:
144	                patch = int(cell["address"]["patch"])
145	                query_token = int(cell["address"]["querytoken"])
146	                value = cell["value"]
147	                if hasattr(self.processor, "image_seq_length"):
148	                    image_seq_length = self.processor.image_seq_length
149	                else:
150	                    image_seq_length = 1024
151	
152	                if patch >= image_seq_length:
153	                    continue
154	                vespa_sim_map_tensor[
155	                    idx,
156	                    query_token,
157	                    patch // self.n_patch,
158	                    patch % self.n_patch,
159	                ] = value
160	        return vespa_sim_map_tensor
161	
162	    def _blend_image(
163	        self, img: Image, sim_map: torch.Tensor, original_size: Tuple[int, int]
164	    ) -> str:
165	        """
166	        Blends an image with a similarity map and encodes it to base64.
167	
168	        Args:
169	            img (Image): The original image.
170	            sim_map (torch.Tensor): The similarity map tensor.
171	            original_size (Tuple[int, int]): The original size of the image.
172	
173	        Returns:
174	            str: The base64-encoded blended image.
175	        """
176	        SCALING_FACTOR = 8
177	        sim_map_resolution = (
178	            max(32, int(original_size[0] / SCALING_FACTOR)),
179	            max(32, int(original_size[1] / SCALING_FACTOR)),
180	        )
181	
182	        sim_map_np = sim_map.cpu().float().numpy()
183	        sim_map_img = Image.fromarray(sim_map_np).resize(
184	            sim_map_resolution, resample=Image.BICUBIC
185	        )
186	        sim_map_resized_np = np.array(sim_map_img, dtype=np.float32)
187	        sim_map_normalized = self._normalize_sim_map(sim_map_resized_np)
188	
189	        heatmap = self.colormap(sim_map_normalized)
190	        heatmap_img = Image.fromarray((heatmap * 255).astype(np.uint8)).convert("RGBA")
191	
192	        buffer = io.BytesIO()
193	        heatmap_img.save(buffer, format="PNG")
194	        return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("utf-8")
195	
196	    @staticmethod
197	    def _normalize_sim_map(sim_map: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
198	        """
199	        Normalizes a similarity map to range [0, 1].
200	
201	        Args:
202	            sim_map (np.ndarray): The similarity map.
203	
204	        Returns:
205	            np.ndarray: The normalized similarity map.
206	        """
207	        sim_map_min, sim_map_max = sim_map.min(), sim_map.max()
208	        if sim_map_max - sim_map_min > 1e-6:
209	            return (sim_map - sim_map_min) / (sim_map_max - sim_map_min)
210	        return np.zeros_like(sim_map)
211	
212	    @staticmethod
213	    def should_filter_token(token: str) -> bool:
214	        """
215	        Determines if a token should be filtered out based on predefined patterns.
216	
217	        The function filters out tokens that:
218	
219	            - Start with '<' (e.g., '<bos>')
220	            - Consist entirely of whitespace
221	            - Are purely punctuation (excluding tokens that contain digits or start with '▁')
222	            - Start with an underscore '_'
223	            - Exactly match the word 'Question'
224	            - Are exactly the single character '▁'
225	
226	        Output of test:
227	            Token: '2'         | False
228	            Token: '0'         | False
229	            Token: '2'         | False
230	            Token: '3'         | False
231	            Token: '▁2'        | False
232	            Token: '▁hi'       | False
233	            Token: 'norwegian' | False
234	            Token: 'unlisted'  | False
235	            Token: '<bos>'     | True
236	            Token: 'Question'  | True
237	            Token: ':'         | True
238	            Token: '<pad>'     | True
239	            Token: '\n'        | True
240	            Token: '▁'         | True
241	            Token: '?'         | True
242	            Token: ')'         | True
243	            Token: '%'         | True
244	            Token: '/)'        | True
245	
246	
247	        Args:
248	            token (str): The token to check.
249	
250	        Returns:
251	            bool: True if the token should be filtered out, False otherwise.
252	        """
253	        pattern = re.compile(
254	            r"^<.*$|^\s+$|^(?!.*\d)(?!▁)[^\w\s]+$|^_.*$|^Question$|^▁$"
255	        )
256	        return bool(pattern.match(token))
257	
258	    @lru_cache(maxsize=128)
259	    def get_query_embeddings_and_token_map(
260	        self, query: str
261	    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, dict]:
262	        """
263	        Retrieves query embeddings and a token index map.
264	
265	        Args:
266	            query (str): The query string.
267	
268	        Returns:
269	            Tuple[torch.Tensor, dict]: Query embeddings and token index map.
270	        """
271	        inputs = self.processor.process_queries([query]).to(self.model.device)
272	        with torch.no_grad():
273	            q_emb = self.model(**inputs).to("cpu")[0]
274	
275	        query_tokens = self.processor.tokenizer.tokenize(
276	            self.processor.decode(inputs.input_ids[0])
277	        )
278	        idx_to_token = {idx: token for idx, token in enumerate(query_tokens)}
279	        return q_emb, idx_to_token

You are deciding energy-waste suspicions in a Python repository at /home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps. Read-only: write no files.

Step 1 (already done) listed units with suspicions. Your job is step 2: for each unit assigned below, read it and decide every suspicion ACCEPTED or REJECTED.

Procedure per unit:
1. Read the whole unit (use Read on its file, at the line range given, plus its surroundings as needed). Follow it DOWN into what it calls within the repo, and UP into its callers (grep the repo for the function name and for the attributes/state it reads or writes). Check every caller and every reader of any state the edit would change.
2. Say in one sentence what the unit computes and where its work goes (what_it_does).
3. For each suspicion, check on a second reading:
   - Does the waste really apply to this code (name the variable, line, structure)?
   - Can you write the repair as a concrete edit to THIS unit? State it in one or two sentences. If you cannot write it, REJECT.
   - Does the repair preserve the unit's contract on every input: same return value; same effect on arguments and on module/class-level values it uses; same printed output and log records; same files written; same exception type. Removing a print or a log call changes printed output, so REJECT such a repair. Changing a return value's type or shape is REJECTED unless every caller in the repo is checked and listed.
   - State the mechanism: what work stops happening and why that costs less energy. 'Built-ins are faster' is not a mechanism.
   - If the edit reaches beyond the unit (another function or state read elsewhere), REJECT unless you verified and can say what you checked (sole_caller_evidence).

11	
12	
13	logging.set_verbosity_error()
14	
15	data_dir = sys.argv[1]
16	doc_type = "mind"
17	
18	train_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news.tsv")
19	train_embedding_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news_embeddings.tsv")
20	dev_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news.tsv")
21	dev_embedding_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "news_embeddings.tsv")
22	
23	field_list = ["docid", "category", "subcategory", "title", "abstract", "url", "title_entities", "abstract_entities"]
24	
25	
26	def create_embeddings(input_file_name, output_file_name):
27	    docids = set()
28	    titles = {}
29	    abstracts = {}
30	    categories = {}
31	    subcategories = {}
32	
33	    # read
34	    with io.open(input_file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
35	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
36	        for line in reader:
37	            docid = line["docid"]
38	            docids.add(docid)
39	            titles[docid] = line["title"]
40	            abstracts[docid] = line["abstract"]
41	            categories[docid] = line["category"]
42	            subcategories[docid] = line["subcategory"]
43	
44	    print("Read {} documents".format(len(docids)))
45	
46	    # convert and write
47	    tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
48	    model = BertModel.from_pretrained('google/bert_uncased_L-8_H-512_A-8')
49	    t = time.time()
50	    with open(output_file_name, "w") as f:
51	        for i, docid in enumerate(docids):
52	            title = titles[docid]
53	            abstract = abstracts[docid]
54	
55	            f.write(docid)
56	
57	            tokens = tokenizer(title, abstract, return_tensors="pt", max_length=100, truncation=True, padding=True)
58	            outputs = model(**tokens)
59	            write_embedding(f, outputs[0].tolist()[0][0])
60	
61	            f.write("\n")
62	
63	            if i % (len(docids)//100) == (len(docids)//100 - 1):
64	                print("Completed {} embeddings ({:.0f} %) [{:.2f} s]".format(i + 1, 100.0 *(i+1)/len(docids), time.time()-t))
65	                t = time.time()
66	
67	
68	def write_embedding(f, embedding):
69	    f.write("\t")
70	    for j, num in enumerate(embedding):
71	        if j > 0:
72	            f.write(",")
73	        f.write("%.4f" % num)
74	
75	
76	def main():
77	    create_embeddings(train_news_file, train_embedding_file)
78	    create_embeddings(dev_news_file, dev_embedding_file)
79	
80	
81	if __name__ == "__main__":
82	    main()

19	dev_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "behaviors.tsv")
20	global_ctr_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "global_category_ctr.json")
21	news_category_ctr_update_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "news_category_ctr_update.json")
22	
23	
24	def read_impressions_file(file_name, click_map, news_map):
25	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
26	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
27	        sys.exit(1)
28	    print("Reading impressions data from " + file_name)
29	
30	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
31	        field_list = ["id", "user_id", "timestamp", "history", "impressions"]
32	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
33	        for line in reader:
34	            for impression in line["impressions"].split(" "):
35	                news_id, label = impression.split("-")
36	                if news_id in news_map:
37	                    category = news_map[news_id]
38	                    click_map[category]["impressions"] += 1
39	                    if label == "1":
40	                        click_map[category]["clicks"] += 1
41	
42	
43	def read_content_file(file_name, news_map):
44	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
45	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
46	        sys.exit(1)
47	    print("Reading news data from " + file_name)
48	
49	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
50	        field_list = ["news_id", "category", "subcategory", "title", "abstract", "url", "title_entities", "abstract_entities"]
51	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
52	        for line in reader:
53	            news_map[line["news_id"]] = line["category"]
54	
55	
56	def write_global_ctr_document(category_ctr_map):
57	    tensor_cells = []
58	    for category, ctr_data in category_ctr_map.items():
59	        category_ctr = ctr_data["clicks"] / ctr_data["impressions"] if ctr_data["impressions"] > 0 else 0.0
60	        cell = {"address":{"category":category}, "value": category_ctr}
61	        tensor_cells.append(cell)
62	    ctrs_tensor = {"ctrs": {"cells": tensor_cells}}
63	
64	    global_ctr_document = {"put": "id:category_ctr:category_ctr::global", "fields": ctrs_tensor}
65	    with open(global_ctr_file, "w") as out:
66	        json.dump(global_ctr_document, out)
67	
68	
69	def write_news_category_ctr_update(news_to_cat_map):
70	    global_ctr_document_id = "id:category_ctr:category_ctr::global"
71	    with open(news_category_ctr_update_file, "w") as out:
72	        out.write("[\n")
73	        for i, (news_id, category) in enumerate(news_to_cat_map.items()):
74	            if i > 0:
75	                out.write(",\n")
76	            category_tensor = '{"cells": [{"address":{"category":"%s"}, "value": 1.0}]}' % category
77	            out.write('{"update": "id:news:news::%s", ' % news_id +
78	                      '"fields": {' +
79	                          '"category_ctr_ref": {"assign": "%s"}, ' % global_ctr_document_id +
80	                          '"category_tensor": {"assign": %s}' % category_tensor +
81	                      '}}')
82	        out.write("\n]\n")
83	
84

94	    write_global_ctr_document(category_ctr_map)

33	class MF(torch.nn.Module):
34	    def __init__(self, num_users, num_items, embedding_size):
35	        super(MF, self).__init__()
36	        self.user_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_users, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
37	        self.news_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_items, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
38

40	        user_embeddings = self.user_embeddings(users)
41	        news_embeddings = self.news_embeddings(items)
42	        dot_prod = torch.sum(torch.mul(user_embeddings, news_embeddings), 1)
43	        return torch.sigmoid(dot_prod)
44	
45	
46	def train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, loss_function):
47	    total_loss = 0
48	    for batch_num, batch in enumerate(sample_data):
49	
50	        # get the inputs - data is a user_id and news_id which looks up the embedding, and a label
51	        user_ids, news_ids, _, _, _, labels = batch
52	
53	        # zero to parameter gradients
54	        optimizer.zero_grad()
55	
56	        # forward + backward + optimize
57	        prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids)
58	        loss = loss_function(prediction.view(-1), labels)

12	from mind_data import MindData
13	from metrics import ndcg, mrr, group_auc
14	
15	
16	data_dir = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "../../mind/"
17	epochs = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 15

19	train_news_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "news.tsv")

21	train_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "train", "behaviors.tsv")
22	valid_impressions_file = os.path.join(data_dir, "dev", "behaviors.tsv")

27	embedding_size = 50
28	negative_sample_size = 4
29	batch_size = 128
30	
31	adam_lr = 1e-3  # 5e-4
32	l2_regularization = 1e-5  # 0.01
33	
34	
35	class ContentBasedModel(torch.nn.Module):
36	    def __init__(self, num_users, num_news, num_categories, num_subcategories, num_entities, embedding_size, bert_embeddings):
37	        super(ContentBasedModel, self).__init__()
38	
39	        # Embedding tables for category variables
40	        self.user_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_users, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
41	        self.news_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_news, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
42	        self.cat_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_categories, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
43	        self.sub_cat_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_subcategories, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
44	        self.entity_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding(num_embeddings=num_entities, embedding_dim=embedding_size)
45	
46	        # Pretrained BERT embeddings
47	        self.news_bert_embeddings = torch.nn.Embedding.from_pretrained(bert_embeddings, freeze=True)
48	
49	        # Linear transformation from BERT size to embedding size (512 -> 50)
50	        self.news_bert_transform = torch.nn.Linear(bert_embeddings.shape[1], embedding_size)
51	
52	        # Linear transformation from concatenation of category, subcategory, entity and BERT embedding
53	        self.news_content_transform = torch.nn.Linear(in_features=embedding_size*5, out_features=embedding_size)
54	
55	    def get_user_embeddings(self, users):
56	        return self.user_embeddings(users)
57	
58	    def get_news_embeddings(self, items, categories, subcategories, entities):
59	        # Transform BERT representation to a shorter embedding
60	        bert_embeddings = self.news_bert_embeddings(items)
61	        bert_embeddings = self.news_bert_transform(bert_embeddings)
62	        bert_embeddings = torch.sigmoid(bert_embeddings)
63	
64	        # Create news content representation by concatenating BERT, category, subcategory and entities
65	        cat_embeddings = self.cat_embeddings(categories)
66	        news_embeddings = self.news_embeddings(items)
67	        sub_cat_embeddings = self.sub_cat_embeddings(subcategories)
68	        entity_embeddings_1 = self.entity_embeddings(entities[:,0])
69	        news_embedding = torch.cat((news_embeddings, bert_embeddings, cat_embeddings, sub_cat_embeddings, entity_embeddings_1), 1)
70	        news_embedding = self.news_content_transform(news_embedding)
71	        news_embedding = torch.sigmoid(news_embedding)
72	
73	        return news_embedding
74	
75	    def forward(self, users, items, categories, subcategories, entities):
76	        user_embeddings = self.get_user_embeddings(users)
77	        news_embeddings = self.get_news_embeddings(items, categories, subcategories, entities)
78	        dot_prod = torch.sum(torch.mul(user_embeddings, news_embeddings), 1)
79	        return torch.sigmoid(dot_prod)
80	
81	
82	def train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, criterion):
83	    total_loss = 0
84	    for batch_num, batch in enumerate(sample_data):
85	
86	        # get the inputs - data is a user_id and news_id which looks up the embedding, and a label
87	        user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities, labels = batch
88	
89	        # zero to parameter gradients
90	        optimizer.zero_grad()
91	
92	        # forward + backward + optimize
93	        prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities)
94	        loss = criterion(prediction.view(-1), labels)
95	        loss.backward()
96	        optimizer.step()
97	
98	        # keep track of statistics
99	        total_loss += loss
100	
101	    print("Total loss after epoch {}: {} ({} avg)".format(epoch+1, total_loss, total_loss / len(sample_data)))
102	
103	
104	def train_model(model, data_loader):
105	    criterion = torch.nn.BCELoss()
106	    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=adam_lr, weight_decay=l2_regularization)
107	    for epoch in range(epochs):
108	
109	        # create data for this epoch
110	        sample_data = data_loader.sample_training_data(batch_size, negative_sample_size)
111	
112	        # train
113	        train_epoch(model, sample_data, epoch, optimizer, criterion)
114	
115	        # evaluate every epoch
116	        eval_model(model, data_loader, train=True)
117	        eval_model(model, data_loader, 1.0)
118	
119	        # save embeddings if better auc - TODO
120	        save_embeddings(model, data_loader)
121	
122	
123	def eval_model(model, data_loader, sample_prob=1.0, train=False):
124	    sample_data = data_loader.sample_valid_data(sample_prob, train=train)
125	    with torch.no_grad():
126	
127	        all_predictions = []
128	        all_labels = []
129	
130	        for impression in sample_data:  # make an iterator instead
131	            user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities, labels = impression
132	            prediction = model(user_ids, news_ids, category_ids, subcategory_ids, entities).view(-1)
133	
134	            all_predictions.append(prediction.detach().numpy())
135	            all_labels.append(labels.detach().numpy())
136	
137	        metrics = {
138	            "auc": group_auc(all_predictions, all_labels),
139	            "mrr": mrr(all_predictions, all_labels),
140	            "ndcg@5": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 5),
141	            "ndcg@10": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 10)
142	        }
143	        print(metrics)
144	
145	
146	def save_embeddings(model, data_loader):
147	    user_map = data_loader.users()
148	    news_map = data_loader.news()
149	    users = torch.LongTensor(range(len(user_map)))
150	    news, cats, subcats, entities = data_loader.get_news_content_tensors()
151	    user_embeddings = model.get_user_embeddings(users)
152	    news_embeddings = model.get_news_embeddings(news, cats, subcats, entities)
153	    write_embeddings(user_map, user_embeddings, "user_embeddings.tsv")
154	    write_embeddings(news_map, news_embeddings, "news_embeddings.tsv")
155	
156	
157	def write_embeddings(id_to_index_map, embeddings, file_name):
158	    with open(os.path.join(data_dir, file_name), "w") as f:
159	        for id, index in id_to_index_map.items():
160	            f.write("{}\t{}\n".format(id, ",".join(["%.6f" % i for i in embeddings[index].tolist()])))
161	
162	
163	def read_bert_embeddings(data_loader, train_embeddings_file, valid_embeddings_file):
164	    embeddings = np.zeros([len(data_loader.news()), 512])
165	    read_bert_embeddings_from_file(data_loader, train_embeddings_file, embeddings)
166	    read_bert_embeddings_from_file(data_loader, valid_embeddings_file, embeddings)
167	    return torch.FloatTensor(embeddings)
168	
169	
170	def read_bert_embeddings_from_file(data_loader, embeddings_file, embeddings):
171	    if not os.path.exists(embeddings_file):
172	        print("{} not found.".format(embeddings_file))
173	        sys.exit(1)
174	    print("Reading data from " + embeddings_file)
175	
176	    with io.open(embeddings_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
177	        for line in f:
178	            embeddings_data = line.split("\t")
179	            news_id = embeddings_data[0]
180	            if news_id not in data_loader.news():
181	                continue # not used
182	            title_and_abstract_embedding = [ float(i) for i in embeddings_data[1].split(",") ]
183	            news_index = data_loader.news()[news_id]
184	            embeddings[news_index] = title_and_abstract_embedding
185	
186	
187	def set_random_seed(seed):
188	    os.environ['PYTHONHASHSEED'] = str(seed)
189	    torch.manual_seed(seed)
190	    torch.cuda.manual_seed(seed)
191	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
192	    numpy.random.seed(seed)
193	    random.seed(seed)
194	
195	
196	def main():
197	    set_random_seed(1)
198	
199	    # read data
200	    data_loader = MindData(train_news_file, train_impressions_file, valid_news_file, valid_impressions_file)
201	    num_users = len(data_loader.users())
202	    num_news = len(data_loader.news())
203	    num_categories = len(data_loader.categories())
204	    num_subcategories = len(data_loader.subcategories())
205	    num_entities = len(data_loader.entities())
206	
207	    # read BERT embeddings
208	    bert_embeddings = read_bert_embeddings(data_loader, train_embeddings_file, valid_embeddings_file)
209	
210	    # create model
211	    model = ContentBasedModel(num_users, num_news, num_categories, num_subcategories, num_entities, embedding_size, bert_embeddings)
212	
213	    # train model
214	    train_model(model, data_loader)
215	
216	
217	if __name__ == "__main__":
218	    main()

You are deciding energy-waste suspicions in a Python repository at /home/javad/energy-run/sample-apps. Read-only: write no files.

Step 1 (already done) listed units with suspicions. Your job is step 2: for each unit assigned below, read it and decide every suspicion ACCEPTED or REJECTED.

Procedure per unit:
1. Read the whole unit (use Read on its file, at the line range given, plus its surroundings as needed). Follow it DOWN into what it calls within the repo, and UP into its callers (grep the repo for the function name and for the attributes/state it reads or writes). Check every caller and every reader of any state the edit would change.
2. Say in one sentence what the unit computes and where its work goes (what_it_does).
3. For each suspicion, check on a second reading:
   - Does the waste really apply to this code (name the variable, line, structure)?
   - Can you write the repair as a concrete edit to THIS unit? State it in one or two sentences. If you cannot write it, REJECT.
   - Does the repair preserve the unit's contract on every input: same return value; same effect on arguments and on module/class-level values it uses; same printed output and log records; same files written; same exception type. Removing a print or a log call changes printed output, so REJECT such a repair. Changing a return value's type or shape is REJECTED unless every caller in the repo is checked and listed.
   - State the mechanism: what work stops happening and why that costs less energy. 'Built-ins are faster' is not a mechanism.
   - If the edit reaches beyond the unit (another function or state read elsewhere), REJECT unless you verified and can say what you checked (sole_caller_evidence).
   ACCEPTED only if all hold. Otherwise REJECTED, with the specific check that decided it.
   If two suspicions would get exactly the same edit, say 'same edit as label X' in the why, and still give each its own verdict.
   Do not fold in a second, unrelated fix. One repair per suspicion.

Output format: one JSON object per unit, one per line, and nothing else in your reply. Exact shape:
{"step": 2, "unit": "<unit exactly as given>", "what_it_does": "<one sentence>", "decisions": [{"label": "a", "lines": [<ints>], "verdict": "accepted" or "rejected", "why": "<accepted: the mechanism and the concrete edit in one or two sentences, plus sole-caller evidence if beyond the unit; rejected: the check that decided it>"}]}
Every label of the unit must appear exactly once. Inside string values do not use double quotes; use single quotes or backticks. The energy meter is not needed for this step.

Your units (unit :: suspicions from step 1 with their lines):
1. news/src/python/mind_data.py::MindData.read_data :: a[93, 101] strptime per impression row; the parsed time is stored as 'timestamp' which nothing reads (grep to confirm)

3. news/src/python/mind_data.py::MindData.add_impressions :: a[181, 201] per-sample lookups into news_content repeated
4. news/src/python/mind_data.py::MindData.sample_valid_data :: a[159, 179] with train=True the whole train set converted to per-impression tensors each epoch
5. news/src/python/mind_data.py::MindData.read_news :: a[63, 74] second entity column computed and carried; only column 0 is used (check train_cold_start and any other reader of entities)
6. news/src/python/evaluate.py::calc_metrics :: a[86] full impression file parsed then random.sample keeps sample_size
7. news/src/python/evaluate.py::read_impressions_file :: a[25, 47] every row parsed into objects
8. news/src/python/evaluate.py::calc_impression :: a[72, 73] user embedding re-fetched per impression
9. news/src/python/evaluate.py::find_hit :: a[55, 68] linear scan over hits per candidate
10. news/src/python/metrics.py::ndcg_score :: a[18, 30] ideal DCG recomputed per call; ndcg called for k=5 and k=10
11. news/src/python/metrics.py::mrr_score :: a[43, 47] re-sorts y_score
12. news/src/python/metrics.py::group_auc :: a[8, 15] sklearn roc_auc_score per impression
13. news/src/python/vespa_client.py::query_user_embedding :: a[45, 49] requests.get without Session
14. news/src/python/vespa_client.py::query_news :: a[52, 67] requests.post without Session

Notes: the metrics functions return values that are printed or aggregated; an edit must return the same numbers exactly, including floating-point results where possible (argsort tie order matters for ndcg and mrr). For random.sample in calc_metrics, the random state is part of the behaviour: an edit that changes which random draws happen changes the printed metrics, so it must consume the RNG identically or be REJECTED. For read_data and read_news, check the MindData object's attributes (they are part of what other code reads) before deciding.

4	import os
5	import io
6	import sys
7	import json
8	import random
9	import datetime
10	
11	import torch
12	from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset, RandomSampler
13	
14	
15	class MindData:
16	    def __init__(self, train_news_file, train_impressions_file, valid_news_file, valid_impressions_file):
17	        self.user_map = {}    # Mapping from user_id to index, e.g. "U82271" -> 0, "U84185" -> 1 etc
18	        self.news_map = {}    # Mapping from news_id to index, e.g. "N27209" -> 0
19	        self.cat_map = {}     # Mapping from category to index, e.g. "health" -> 0
20	        self.sub_cat_map = {} # Mapping from subcategory to index, e.g. "medical" -> 0
21	        self.entity_map = {}  # Mapping from entity id to index, e.g. "Q212" -> 0  (WikidataId for "ukraine")
22	        self.news_content = {}
23	        self.train_impressions = []
24	        self.valid_impressions = []
25	        self.read_data(train_impressions_file, self.train_impressions)
26	        self.read_data(valid_impressions_file, self.valid_impressions)
27	        self.read_news(train_news_file)
28	        self.read_news(valid_news_file)
29	
30	    def users(self):
31	        return self.user_map
32	
33	    def news(self):
34	        return self.news_map
35	
36	    def categories(self):
37	        return self.cat_map
38	
39	    def subcategories(self):
40	        return self.sub_cat_map
41	
42	    def entities(self):
43	        return self.entity_map
44	
45	    def read_news(self, news_file):
46	        if not os.path.exists(news_file):
47	            print("{} not found.".format(news_file))
48	            sys.exit(1)
49	        print("Reading data from " + news_file)
50	
51	        with io.open(news_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
52	            for line in f:
53	                news_data = line.split("\t")
54	                doc_id = news_data[0]
55	                category = news_data[1]
56	                subcategory = news_data[2]
57	                title = news_data[3]
58	                abstract = news_data[4]
59	                url = news_data[5]
60	                title_entities = json.loads(news_data[6]) if len(news_data) > 6 else []
61	                abstract_entities = json.loads(news_data[7]) if len(news_data) > 7 else []
62	
63	                entities_to_keep = 2
64	                entity_ids = []
65	                self.add_entities(entity_ids, title_entities)
66	                self.add_entities(entity_ids, abstract_entities)
67	                entity_ids.extend([""] * entities_to_keep)
68	
69	                self.news_content[self.lookup_news_index(doc_id)] = {
70	                    "news_id": doc_id,
71	                    "category_index": self.lookup_category_index(category),
72	                    "subcategory_index": self.lookup_subcategory_index(subcategory),
73	                    "entity_index": [ self.lookup_entity_index(id) for id in entity_ids[:entities_to_keep]]
74	                }
75	
76	    def add_entities(self, entity_ids: list, entities: list):
77	        for entity in entities:
78	            entity_id = entity["WikidataId"]
79	            if entity_id not in entity_ids:
80	                entity_ids.append(entity_id)
81	
82	    def read_data(self, impressions_file, impression_list):
83	        if not os.path.exists(impressions_file):
84	            print("{} not found.".format(impressions_file))
85	            sys.exit(1)
86	        print("Reading data from " + impressions_file)
87	
88	        with io.open(impressions_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
89	            for line in f:
90	                impression_data = line.split("\t")
91	                impression_id = impression_data[0]
92	                user_id = impression_data[1]
93	                time = datetime.datetime.strptime(impression_data[2], "%m/%d/%Y %I:%M:%S %p")
94	                history = set(impression_data[3].split(" "))
95	                impressions = impression_data[4].split(" ")
96	
97	                news_indices, labels = self.find_labels(impressions, history)
98	
99	                impression_list.append({
100	                    "user_index": self.lookup_user_index(user_id),
101	                    "timestamp": time,
102	                    "news_indices": news_indices,
103	                    "labels": labels
104	                })
105	
106	    def find_labels(self, impressions, history):
107	        news_indices = []
108	        labels = []
109	        for impression in impressions:
110	            news_id, label = impression.split("-")
111	            if news_id not in history:  # don't add news previously clicked (in history)
112	                news_indices.append(self.lookup_news_index(news_id))
113	                labels.append(int(label))
114	        return news_indices, labels
115	
116	    def lookup_user_index(self, user_id):
117	        return self.lookup_index(user_id, self.user_map)
118	
119	    def lookup_news_index(self, news_id):
120	        return self.lookup_index(news_id, self.news_map)
121	
122	    def lookup_category_index(self, category):
123	        return self.lookup_index(category, self.cat_map)
124	
125	    def lookup_subcategory_index(self, subcategory):
126	        return self.lookup_index(subcategory, self.sub_cat_map)
127	
128	    def lookup_entity_index(self, entity_id):
129	        return self.lookup_index(entity_id, self.entity_map)
130	
131	    def lookup_index(self, id, map):
132	        if id not in map:
133	            map[id] = len(map)
134	        return map[id]
135	
136	    def sample_training_data(self, batch_size, num_negatives, prob=1.0):
137	        user_indices = []
138	        news_indices = []
139	        category_indices = []
140	        subcategory_indices = []
141	        entity_indices = []
142	        labels = []
143	
144	        for impression in self.train_impressions:
145	            if random.random() <= prob:
146	                self.add_impressions(impression, user_indices, news_indices, category_indices, subcategory_indices, entity_indices, labels, num_negatives)
147	
148	        data_set = TensorDataset(
149	                        torch.LongTensor(user_indices),
150	                        torch.LongTensor(news_indices),
151	                        torch.LongTensor(category_indices),
152	                        torch.LongTensor(subcategory_indices),
153	                        torch.LongTensor(entity_indices),
154	                        torch.FloatTensor(labels))
155	        generator = torch.Generator()
156	        random_sampler = RandomSampler(data_set, generator=generator)
157	        return DataLoader(data_set, batch_size=batch_size, sampler=random_sampler)
158	
159	    def sample_valid_data(self, prob=1.0, train=False):
160	        data = []
161	        impressions = self.train_impressions if train else self.valid_impressions
162	        for impression in impressions:
163	            if random.random() <= prob:
164	                news_indices = impression["news_indices"]
165	                labels = impression["labels"]
166	                category_indices = [ self.news_content[index]["category_index"] for index in news_indices ]
167	                subcategory_indices = [ self.news_content[index]["subcategory_index"] for index in news_indices ]
168	                entity_indices = [ self.news_content[index]["entity_index"] for index in news_indices ]
169	                user_index = [ impression["user_index"] ] * len(labels)
170	                if sum(labels) > 0 and sum(labels) != len(labels):
171	                    data.append([
172	                        torch.LongTensor(user_index),
173	                        torch.LongTensor(news_indices),
174	                        torch.LongTensor(category_indices),
175	                        torch.LongTensor(subcategory_indices),
176	                        torch.LongTensor(entity_indices),
177	                        torch.FloatTensor(labels)
178	                    ])
179	        return data
180	
181	    def add_impressions(self, impression, user_indices, news_indices, category_indices, subcategory_indices, entity_indices, labels, num_negatives):
182	        user_index = impression["user_index"]
183	        positive, negative = self.find_clicked(impression["news_indices"], impression["labels"])
184	
185	        # add each positive label
186	        for pos_news_index in positive:
187	            user_indices.append(user_index)
188	            news_indices.append(pos_news_index)
189	            category_indices.append(self.news_content[pos_news_index]["category_index"])
190	            subcategory_indices.append(self.news_content[pos_news_index]["subcategory_index"])
191	            entity_indices.append(self.news_content[pos_news_index]["entity_index"])
192	            labels.append(1)
193	
194	            # for each positive label, sample negative labels
195	            for neg_news_index in random.sample(negative, min(num_negatives, len(negative))):
196	                user_indices.append(user_index)
197	                news_indices.append(neg_news_index)
198	                category_indices.append(self.news_content[neg_news_index]["category_index"])
199	                subcategory_indices.append(self.news_content[neg_news_index]["subcategory_index"])
200	                entity_indices.append(self.news_content[neg_news_index]["entity_index"])
201	                labels.append(0)
202	
203	    def find_clicked(self, news_ids, labels):
204	        clicked = []
205	        skipped = []
206	        for news_id, label in zip(news_ids, labels):
207	            if label > 0:
208	                clicked.append(news_id)
209	            else:
210	                skipped.append(news_id)
211	        return clicked, skipped
212	
213	    def get_news_content_tensors(self):
214	        num_docs = len(self.news_map)
215	        news_indices = [0] * num_docs
216	        category_indices = [0] * num_docs
217	        subcategory_indices = [0] * num_docs
218	        entity_indices = [0] * num_docs
219	
220	        for news_index, content in self.news_content.items():
221	            news_indices[news_index] = news_index
222	            category_indices[news_index] = content["category_index"]
223	            subcategory_indices[news_index] = content["subcategory_index"]
224	            entity_indices[news_index] = content["entity_index"]
225	
226	        return torch.LongTensor(news_indices), \
227	               torch.LongTensor(category_indices), \
228	               torch.LongTensor(subcategory_indices),\
229	               torch.LongTensor(entity_indices),

25	def read_impressions_file(file_name):
26	    impressions = []
27	    if not os.path.exists(file_name):
28	        print("{} not found.".format(file_name))
29	        sys.exit(1)
30	    print("Reading impressions data from " + file_name)
31	
32	    with io.open(file_name, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
33	        field_list = ["id", "user_id", "timestamp", "history", "impressions"]
34	        reader = csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=field_list)
35	        for line in reader:
36	            user_id = line["user_id"]
37	            impression = {
38	                "user_id": user_id,
39	                "news_ids": [],
40	                "labels": []
41	            }
42	            for i in line["impressions"].split(" "):
43	                news_id, label = i.split("-")
44	                impression["news_ids"].append(news_id)
45	                impression["labels"].append(int(label))
46	            impressions.append(impression)

49	
50	def query_news_ids(user_vector, news_ids):
51	    news_id_filter = [ 'news_id contains "{}"'.format(i) for i in news_ids ]
52	    news_id_filter = "AND ({})".format(" OR ".join(news_id_filter))
53	    return query_news(user_vector, len(news_ids), news_id_filter, url, cert, timeout=10)
54	
55	def find_hit(hits, news_id):
56	    for child in hits["root"]["children"]:
57	        if child["fields"]["news_id"] == news_id:
58	            return child
59	    return None
60	
61	
62	def predictions(hits, news_ids):
63	    preds = []
64	    for news_id in news_ids:
65	        hit = find_hit(hits, news_id)
66	        relevance = hit["relevance"]
67	        preds.append(relevance)
68	    return preds
69	
70	
71	def calc_impression(impression):
72	    user_id = impression["user_id"]
73	    user_vector = query_user_embedding(user_id, url, cert)
74	    result = query_news_ids(user_vector, impression["news_ids"])
75	    preds = predictions(result, impression["news_ids"])
76	    labels = impression["labels"]
77	
78	    return preds, labels
79	
80	
81	def calc_metrics(file):
82	    all_predictions = []
83	    all_labels = []
84	    impressions = read_impressions_file(file)
85	    if sample_size > 0:
86	        impressions = random.sample(impressions, sample_size)

93	
94	    metrics = {

96	        "mrr": mrr(all_predictions, all_labels),
97	        "ndcg@5": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 5),
98	        "ndcg@10": ndcg(all_predictions, all_labels, 10)
99	    }

1	#! /usr/bin/env python3
2	# Copyright Vespa.ai. Licensed under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. See LICENSE in the project root.
3	
4	import numpy as np
5	from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
6	
7	
8	def group_auc(preds, labels):
9	    group_auc = np.mean(
10	        [
11	            roc_auc_score(each_labels, each_preds)
12	            for each_labels, each_preds in zip(labels, preds)
13	        ]
14	    )
15	    return round(group_auc, 4)
16	
17	
18	def dcg_score(y_true, y_score, k=10):
19	    k = min(np.shape(y_true)[-1], k)
20	    order = np.argsort(y_score)[::-1]
21	    y_true = np.take(y_true, order[:k])
22	    gains = 2 ** y_true - 1
23	    discounts = np.log2(np.arange(len(y_true)) + 2)
24	    return np.sum(gains / discounts)
25	
26	
27	def ndcg_score(y_true, y_score, k=10):
28	    best = dcg_score(y_true, y_true, k)
29	    actual = dcg_score(y_true, y_score, k)
30	    return actual / best
31	
32	
33	def ndcg(preds, labels, k):
34	    ndcg_temp = np.mean(
35	        [
36	            ndcg_score(each_labels, each_preds, k)
37	            for each_labels, each_preds in zip(labels, preds)
38	        ]
39	    )
40	    return round(ndcg_temp, 4)
41	
42	
43	def mrr_score(y_true, y_score):
44	    order = np.argsort(y_score)[::-1]
45	    y_true = np.take(y_true, order)

54	            for each_labels, each_preds in zip(labels, preds)
55	        ]

4	"""Shared query helpers for the news sample application.
5	
6	The endpoint and - on Vespa Cloud - the mTLS certificate are resolved from the
7	Vespa CLI, so the same scripts work against a local container and against a
8	Vespa Cloud deployment without any changes.
9	"""
10	
11	import re
12	import subprocess
13	import urllib.parse
14	
15	import requests
16	
17	
18	def vespa_endpoint():
19	    """Return the endpoint URL of the current 'vespa' CLI target."""
20	    result = subprocess.run(["vespa", "status", "--format", "plain"],
21	                            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
22	    return result.stdout.strip()
23	
24	
25	def vespa_cert():
26	    """Return (cert, key) paths from 'vespa curl', or None when no mTLS is configured."""
27	    result = subprocess.run(["vespa", "curl", "-n", "/"],
28	                            capture_output=True, text=True)
29	    output = result.stdout + result.stderr
30	    paths = dict(re.findall(r'--(cert|key) (\S+)', output))
31	    if "cert" in paths and "key" in paths:
32	        return (paths["cert"], paths["key"])
33	    return None
34	
35	
36	def connect():
37	    """Return (url, cert) for the current 'vespa' CLI target."""
38	    return vespa_endpoint(), vespa_cert()
39	
40	
41	def parse_embedding(hit_json):
42	    return hit_json["fields"]["embedding"]["values"]
43	
44	
45	def query_user_embedding(user_id, url, cert):
46	    yql = 'select * from sources user where user_id contains "{}"'.format(user_id)
47	    url = '{}/search/?yql={}&hits=1'.format(url, urllib.parse.quote_plus(yql))
48	    result = requests.get(url, cert=cert).json()
49	    return parse_embedding(result["root"]["children"][0])
50	
51	
52	def query_news(user_vector, hits, filter, url, cert, timeout=None):
53	    nn_annotations = [
54	        'targetHits:{}'.format(hits)
55	        ]
56	    nn_annotations = '{' + ','.join(nn_annotations) + '}'
57	    nn_search = '({}nearestNeighbor(embedding, user_embedding))'.format(nn_annotations)
58	
59	    data = {
60	        'hits': hits,
61	        'yql': 'select * from sources news where {} {}'.format(nn_search, filter),
62	        'ranking.features.query(user_embedding)': str(user_vector),
63	        'ranking.profile': 'recommendation'
64	    }
65	    if timeout is not None:
66	        data['timeout'] = timeout
67	    return requests.post(f'{url}/search/', json=data, cert=cert).json()

13	    query_text: str, top_k: int = 10, query_id: str = None
14	) -> Dict[str, Any]:
15	    """

21	            qb.select("*")

35	                        query_vector="embedding",
36	                        annotations={
37	                            "targetHits": 100,
38	                            "label": "chunk_label",
39	                        },
40	                    )
41	                    | qb.userQuery(
42	                        query_text,
43	                    )
44	                )
45	            )
46	        ),
47	        "query": query_text,
48	        "ranking": "collect-second-phase",
49	        "input.query(embedding)": f"embed({query_text})",
50	        "input.query(float_embedding)": f"embed({query_text})",
51	        "hits": top_k,
52	        "timeout": "5s",
53	        "presentation.summary": "no-chunks",

60	) -> Dict[str, Any]:

67	            qb.select("*")

103	
104	def generate_collector_name(
105	    collect_matchfeatures: bool,
106	    collect_rankfeatures: bool,
107	    collect_summaryfeatures: bool,
108	    second_phase: bool,
109	) -> str:
110	    """
111	    Generate a collector name based on feature collection settings and phase.
112	
113	    Args:
114	        collect_matchfeatures: Whether match features are being collected
115	        collect_rankfeatures: Whether rank features are being collected
116	        collect_summaryfeatures: Whether summary features are being collected
117	        second_phase: Whether using second phase (True) or first phase (False)
118	
119	    Returns:
120	        Generated collector name string
121	    """
122	    features = []
123	    if collect_matchfeatures:
124	        features.append("match")
125	    if collect_rankfeatures:
126	        features.append("rank")
127	    if collect_summaryfeatures:
128	        features.append("summary")
129	
130	    features_str = "_".join(features) if features else "nofeatures"
131	    phase_str = "second_phase" if second_phase else "first_phase"
132	    return f"{features_str}_{phase_str}"

135	def main(args):
136	    dataset_path = Path(args.dataset_dir)
137	    queries_path = dataset_path / args.queries_filename
138	
139	    # Validate file exists
140	    if not queries_path.exists():
141	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Queries file not found: {queries_path}")
142	
143	    logging.info(f"Loading queries from: {queries_path}")
144	    with open(queries_path, "r") as file:
145	        queries_data = json.load(file)
146
